News.title: Burnham must come clean about his dealings with Man City… or he risks being engulfed by the scandal himself
News.content:
Time to Man up







Next

ANDY Burnham’s relationship with Manchester City’s football cheats gets murkier by the minute.

The Prime Minister promised to come clean about his dealings with the club’s mega-rich owners after his ill-judged remark that it would be a “terrible loss” if they were kicked out of the game.



But he seems to have suffered a serious bout of political amnesia on Monday when he coughed to just one “formal meeting” with City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

In fact, as we reveal today, he dined twice with him in a VIP hospitality suite before two Premier League games at the Etihad stadium.



It has also emerged that two months after the first dinner, the Greater Manchester Combined Authority — of which he was then mayor — approved a £24.5million taxpayer-backed loan to a housing venture between Manchester City Council and the club’s owners.

The PM must come clean about the full extent of his dealings with the club.

Otherwise, he risks being engulfed by the scandal himself.

On scrapheap

BRITAIN’S runaway benefits culture isn’t just a drag on economic growth, it’s a tragic waste of lives.

It is a national disgrace that our proud nation — once branded the “workshop of the world” — now has 9million Brits stuck on the jobs scrapheap.

Many were simply “written off” by successive governments as they flooded the market with cheap foreign labour.



British nationals accounted for just one in five of the increase in payroll jobs since 2014.

But the situation has been made worse by the sicknote culture gripping the country, with an estimated 300,000 people dropping out of the workforce every year.

Meanwhile, ministers demand even more foreign worker visas.

The welfare crisis is one of the biggest challenges facing the Government, according to a report by the Centre of Social Justice.

We simply cannot afford to import thousands of foreign workers while paying people to stay at home.



When will the Prime Minister give this crisis the attention it desperately needs?

Doing it for kids

WHILE the Government idles, Britain’s bosses are stepping up to help give our youngsters the future they deserve.

Companies big and small have responded with gusto to our Jobs Army crusade to tackle youth unemployment.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Household names like Octopus, British Airways, Hilton Hotels and Severn Trent Water are among those providing nearly 100,000 vacancies and apprenticeship opportunities, plus 61,000 work experience placements.

Labour is still scratching its head but our Jobs Army is already on the march.

News.title: How Andy Burnham has become the ‘yeah but no but’ Prime Minister as he flip flops on issues from Russia to Brexit
News.content:
Next

U-TURN king Andy Burnham is fast becoming the Vicky Pollard of politics.

His flip-flops on a string of policy positions have left him metaphorically mouthing “Yeah, but, no, but . . . ” like the Little Britain character.



The Prime Minister’s latest about-face followed his claim on Sunday that Russia interfered with the EU referendum of 2016.

The inference to many was that the Kremlin had swayed the result.



Just 24 hours later, Downing Street was forced to clarify that the Leave vote had been “legitimate”.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said: “The busiest job in Westminster is running after the PM with a dustpan and brush, sweeping up whatever he said five minutes earlier.”

Here, we look at some of his other corrections and clarifications . . .

WASPI WOMEN

CAMPAIGNING at the Makerfield by-election, Burnham pledged to “stick by the Waspi women because they deserve some recompense for the unfairness”.

Burnham said he felt “uncomfortable” when politicians were all holding up the Waspi Women’s banner and then got into government and didn’t do anything.

Some 3.6million women — who were left out of pocket after the state pension age was equalised — appeared to have discovered their white knight.



Just 24 hours later, however, his spokesman revealed Burnham now considered the £10billion compensation case was closed.

PERSONAL ALLOWANCE

AFTER winning in Makerfield, Burnham indicated that he might increase the personal tax-free allowance that has been frozen at £12,570 for five years.

Shortly before moving into No10, Burnham insisted it was “the thing I heard most on the doorsteps”.

Soon his team were frantically backpedalling. A source said the PM had shied away from making an announcement because of the cost.



A Burnham ally then added: “What he was saying is that people are feeling unheard”

DRINKING AT FOOTBALL

EVERTON fan Burnham suggested a trial on allowing football supporters to have a pint in the stands.

Describing the current drinking ban during men’s games as “discrimination”, he added: “I don’t think it’s fair for football fans to be singled out”.

Our leader highlighted that fans watching rugby league at Everton’s Hill Dickinson Stadium were able to drink alcohol in the stands.



However, the idea was swiftly placed on ice after the UK Football Policing Unit warned that violence and disorderly conduct from some fans was fuelled by alcohol.

SCOTTISH INDEPENDENCE

THE PM appeared to open the door to another Scottish independence vote if there was “majority public support”. Burnham was accused by the Scottish Tories of “pulling the pin on a constitutional hand grenade”.

For more than a decade, PMs have rejected demands for a fresh referendum.

Burnham swiftly changed his mind and said a fresh poll was “off limits” after all.

REJOINING THE EU

WHEN he was fighting the Makerfield seat, Burnham insisted that “the last thing we should do right now is rerun” the Brexit arguments.



He added: “Britain will be stuck in a permanent rut if we’re just constantly arguing and people are pulling away from each other.

“It is time, surely, to bring people back together . . . ”

Then last month Burnham suggested that Britain might “go all the way” and rejoin the EU, despite Labour fighting the 2024 election pledging not to.

This week he has talked about little else — despite war in Europe and the Middle East, and a raging cost-of- living crisis.

The suspicion is that he is flirting with Brexit now to win back voters from Remainiacs who have switched over to the Greens or Lib Dems.



MANCHESTER CITY

BURNHAM triggered a huge row when he insisted he didn’t want to “lose” Manchester City’s mega-rich owners, after the club were found guilty of more than 100 financial breaches.

He added: “They have been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester and obviously the building of Manchester City into the global force it is.”

Accused of political interference, No10 had to clarify that the charges against Manchester City — which the club denies — were “serious” and “there can’t be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The extent of his ties to City are still emerging. The Prime Minister had insisted he only ever had one “significant” meeting with City chief Khaldoon Al Mubarak while serving as the mayor of Manchester.

But a Sun probe today uncovers two entries in a now-deleted register of interests revealing Burnham dined twice in a luxury hospitality suite at the Etihad.

News.title: Dad killed with wife & 2 boys in ‘petrol bomb’ arson days after statement to gardai as neighbours reveal horror screams
News.content:
Next

A FATHER who died along with his wife and two of their children in a suspected petrol bomb attack had recently made a statement to gardai.

Philip English reported that his car had been set alight, The Irish Sun can reveal.



Innocent Philip, 50s, wife Kim 30s, and two of their sons, Callum, 12 and Jayden, nine, died after their home on the outskirts of Waterford City was targeted in an arson.

Two other children, a girl and a boy, are in a critical condition at Children’s Health Ireland in Crumlin, Dublin, following the horror blaze at Birch Avenue in the Birchwood estate around 5am on Tuesday.



Devastated locals — who heard screams of ‘I’m on fire’ as the blaze raged — could only watch as emergency services attempted to save their lives.

A quadruple murder probe is now underway as the main line of inquiry is drug debt intimidation.

Justice Minister Jim O’Callaghan said: “This shocking event has had a very significant impact not just on the people of Waterford but on the whole country.

“There is no place in a civilised society for such a heinous act of violence.



“I am confident those responsible for this brutal and heinous act will be brought to justice to face the full rigour of the law.”

The Irish Sun has learned how the English family were subjected to a campaign of terror at the hands of what cops believe is a dangerous mob.

Philip had sat down with gardai just ten days ago to give a statement on what was the latest in a string of incidents in recent weeks when their car was set alight.

Investigators believe that today’s deadly arson is connected to and part of the same intimidation.

And as part of the cops probe two raids were carried out on homes in the Waterford area tonight.



It is understood the family had been targeted due to a connection that Philip, who had no involvement in crime whatsoever, had to a man who owed a debt.

Pals of Kim also told us how she had expressed fears for her own life and that of her family’s.

The couple and their four children were in bed when their front door was hit with a suspected petrol bomb at around 5am.

Locals were awoken by a huge “bang” as the property was quickly engulfed in flames that also caught their car parked at the front of the house.

A woman whose home is on a road behind told us of her horror.



She said: “I heard the bang and ‘I’m on fire, I’m on fire, I’m on fire.’

“And I heard it and I just thought, ‘someone is going to be f burnt to death in front of me.’

“My poor son ran over, jumped a wall to get in but he couldn’t see his hand in front of his face the fire and smoke was so strong.”

A group of Kim’s pals revealed how she had expressed fears for her life.

They said the ongoing intimidation included paint thrown at the car when they were sleeping, and even a social media account set up to target the family.

Kim had sought to be moved home by the city council, it was claimed.



One of the women told us: “They should have moved her when her house was first targeted.

“She made numerous complaints to Waterford City Council.

“She was in fear for her life. She was in fear for the lives of her family.”

Another one explained: “It was heartbreaking watching Philip and one of the boys get carried out in a coffin.

“They didn’t deserve this at all. But I will say that Waterford City Council did fail them.



“She was in fear for her life for months.” A third neighbour added: “There was a social media account that was taken down magically last night that Kim had asked me to report.”

One of the women fumed at those responsible as tears streamed down her face.

She said: “No matter who they are or where they come from, they’re the lowest of the low. Absolute scumbags.

“And they need to be held accountable for their actions.

“They took out a family. And if them two children wake up to no father, no mother and no siblings, was the money they were paid worth it? And what they have done to the community here. Was it worth it?”



Bishop Alphonsus Cullinan, of Waterford and Lismore, said of the kids who died: “They should be running around the yard there now, and yet they’re dead, and two more then in hospital.

“We pray for them — and it is amazing to see the community around here gathering, supporting and comforting each other.

“We just hope that we’ll gather tomorrow. We’ll pray together and see if we can make some sense out of all of this.

“And God rest all those who have died and all those who’ve been affected by this huge tragedy.”

Sinn Fein TD David Cullinane said that Waterford is “a community in mourning” and the murder probe added “another level of shock to what has happened”.



He said: “What has happened in Waterford today is beyond shocking. There is an enormous sense of grief, trauma and heartbreak across the entire community.

“I knew the family very well and I am utterly devastated. Like so many people across Waterford, I am struggling to find the words to describe the shock and sadness we are all feeling. The loss of life is heartbreaking. The fact that children are among those who have lost their lives makes this tragedy even more difficult to comprehend.”

The Garda investigation into the multiple murders intensified last night as searches were conducted around Waterford city.

Detectives backed up by armed officers carried out raids on the homes of two criminal figures.

The two men are connected to the drugs trade and are suspected of being heavily involved in ­drug-related activity and drug debt intimidation.



As of last night, no arrests have been made. Gardai also said that they have received good co-operation from the public and that all contact will be treated confidentially.

Chief Supt Anthony Pettit, of the Waterford/Kilkenny Garda Division, confirmed that huge resources, including national units, have been drafted in to help with the probe.

He said: “This investigation is being coordinated from an incident room at Waterford Garda Station under the direction of a senior investigating officer.

“The investigation is being carried out by the Serious Crime Unit at Waterford Garda Station, supported by divisional resources and the Garda National Bureau of Criminal Investigation, and all other resources as necessary. An Garda Siochana believe that the house was attacked by a person or persons unknown and that the fire was started deliberately.”

Chief Supt Pettit also appealed to anyone with information to contact investigating officers.



The investigation team can be contacted at the incident room at Waterford Garda Station on 051 305 300, the Garda Confidential Line 1800 666 111, or any Garda station.

Post-mortem examinations are due to be carried out at University Hospital Waterford.

A GoFundMe has been launched to help the English family with the costs of funerals.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It reads: “With the heaviest of hearts, we are reaching out to ask for help following an unimaginable tragedy that has devastated our family.”

Over €16,000 had already been raised at time of publication.

News.title: ‘Devastated’ family pay tribute to ‘warm and engaging’ man killed by tiger after entering zoo enclosure
News.content:
Next

A FAMILY has paid tribute to a “warm and engaging man” who was killed by a tiger after he jumped into a zoo enclosure.

William Chapman, who was in his early 20s, was tragically pronounced dead at Yorkshire Wildlife Park in Doncaster, South Yorkshire, on Saturday afternoon.



Emergency services descended on the wildlife park shortly after 1.30pm, following reports a man had entered a tiger enclosure.

Park rangers fired warning shots at a Siberian tiger to scare him away before it retreated to a nearby shelter and was secured.



But despite the best efforts of emergency medics, William was tragically pronounced dead at the scene.

His family released a heartbreaking statement on Tuesday evening, saying William was on “strong medication” having suffered from “significant mental illness” in recent years.



It read: “William was a bright, warm and engaging young man whom his family dearly loved – and William loved them back.”

“The family are utterly devastated by their loss and are struggling to come to terms with what has happened,” the statement continued.



“The family are hopeful that the relevant authorities will do their upmost to get to the bottom of why our amazing son did what he did.”

William had reportedly posed for photos with the tiger in the background just moments before he recorded himself approaching the 30st apex predator.

It is thought he leapt from a viewing platform before the animal dragged him away.

He reportedly asked the big cat – named Altai – to “stop being naughty” before its “eyes locked on him and it pounced”.

At one stage, he was filmed sitting on the grass, face-to-face with the animal, forcefully pointing his finger and kicking out.



Another visitor twice shouted “Hey!” in a bid to distract the beast, but it clamped its mouth around the man’s neck and hauled him away.

In other shocking footage he can be heard yelling “No, no, no!” and “Stop, stop, stop, stop, stop!” as the five-year-old big cat repeatedly lunged for him in front of families with children.

A brave and quick-thinking mother “desperately tried to pull back” the man before he jumped into the pen.

Witnesses reported seeing William “dancing erratically” when arriving at the park earlier in the day.

It also emerged on Tuesday that William was a child actor on an ITV show alongside a Harry Potter star.



William appeared in the ITV show May Contain Nuts alongside Shirley Henderson – best known for playing Moaning Myrtle in the Harry Potter films – and Darren Boyd, reported the BBC.

The two-part comedy drama aired in 2009 with Chapman credited as playing the role of Alfie Chaplin, the younger son of Henderson and Boyd’s characters.

The child actor was also credited with portraying Edward Jenner – who pioneered the smallpox vaccine – as a young boy in the educational BBC series True Stories in 2012.



He was a former student at the renowned Jackie Palmer Stage School in High Wycombe, which counts stars Eddie Redmayne, James Corden and Aaron Taylor-Johnson among its alumni.

The school said on Tuesday evening that they were “deeply saddened” to hear of the loss of their former student.

“Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with William’s family and friends during this incredibly difficult time,” the school said.

“We loved watching William grow, both as a person and as a performer, during his time with us.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It was a privilege to be part of his journey, and he will be remembered with great fondness by everyone who had the pleasure of knowing him.



“William will be truly missed, and he will always hold a special place in our hearts. Rest in peace, William.”

News.title: Cops probe new theory after celeb BBL doc assassinated in clinic as ‘hitman’ refuses to answer questions
News.content:
Next

A NEW theory on the assassination of a celebrity BBL surgeon is being probed by cops – as the alleged hitman refuses to answer questions.

Dr Alexander Aslani, 57, whose clients included Towie’s Chloe Sims and Love Island’s Hannah Elizabeth, was shot dead at his Marbella clinic.



Detectives believe a furious patient may have hired a hitman after a row over cosmetic surgery and have launched a probe into the horror.

An 18-year-old Swede arrested on Thursday admitted to gunning down the surgeon, according to Spanish sources.



The alleged killer – who has since been remanded in custody without bail – is reportedly refusing to answer questions.

A judge ordered on Saturday that he be held in solitary confinement pending the probe.



He was cuffed less than 24 hours after the deadly shooting which took place in front of horrified clients last week.

Police are focusing on a new theory Aslani cancelled an operation with a client halfway through after deeming her psychologically unfit.



The doctor then refunded her and refused to continue the procedure.

Another line of enquiry is that one patient became disgruntled due to the outcome of the surgery.

She then allegedly went to the clinic and threatened the doctor.

Four days after this is said to have happened, stones were thrown at the clinic’s windows, according to El Debate Andalucia.

Reports claimed Aslani received angry messages and threats over mobile hours before he was killed.



A major hunt has been launched for the dissatisfied female client – with local reports claiming she has fled Spain.

The suspect reportedly left Spain to her home country in the Persian Gulf, according to local outlet Okdiario.

She is said to have left the country with her wealthy husband – who allegedly previously visited Aslani’s Cirumed Clinic to “issue warnings to staff”.

On Friday local outlet Sur reported Aslani had gone to cops in April to complain he had been receiving “work-related” threats.

It was not clear whether he had pointed the finger at named individuals in his police statement or not.



Investigators said the masked gunman entered the clinic with several customers inside and opened fire before shooting Aslani in the head.

The shooter was reportedly dressed in black head-to-toe, fleeing on a motorbike driven by an accomplice.

Aslani’s clinic claimed to have carried out more than 14,000 operations, but the surgeon also faced complaints from former patients, including one who accused him of botching three procedures.

Influencer Paulina Sobierajska claimed she needed reconstructive surgery and warned women considering using Aslani: “DON’T DO IT.”

The Sun revealed Aslani had been embroiled in a bitter High Court battle with the influencer.



Aslani successfully sued her for libel after she failed to defend the case.

Mr Justice Saini awarded him £40,000 damages in 2021, saying the sum reflected the “total falsity” of the allegations.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Cops have ruled out an earlier theory that Aslani was killed in revenge for a patient dying during surgery, after finding no evidence of any such death.

News.title: When did we become a nation that shrugs, rolls its eyes & accepts thieves can help themselves without punishment?
News.content:
Next

A PROLIFIC parcel thief is facing prison after fed-up homeowners turned detective and caught him red-handed on multiple occasions.

Nice to know that someone is policing our streets.



Ronald De-St-Aubin, 61, initially denied stealing packages containing, among other things, champagne, children’s clothes, a £150 ceiling light and — oh, the irony — an educational DVD about the history of money.

But after being confronted in court with a dossier of doorbell-camera footage painstakingly collated by local residents, he changed his plea to guilty.

Hardly surprising, given that one resident had even followed him home — to a bail hostel, no less — filming him all the way.



There, they discovered discarded Amazon packaging from addresses all across Fulham in South West London.

One of the amateur sleuths responsible for bringing De-St-Aubin to justice said: “I don’t want to bash the police [but] they are just not very interested in this low-level crime . . . but it is not victimless.”

Apparently, officers had told residents it was difficult to prosecute someone for nicking a single parcel and suggested they gather more examples.

In other words, do our job for us.

The resident also criticised delivery companies for abandoning parcels in plain sight, pointing out that thieves “like Ronnie know to follow the vans down the road”. Indeed.



Why bother with gainful employment when you can make money flogging the stolen fruits of other people’s labour?

It would be laughable if it weren’t so depressingly familiar to anyone who knows that reporting these thefts to the police is often pointless.

In my own corner of South London, several people have had their cars stolen, only to discover that police interest barely extends beyond issuing a crime reference number for the insurance company.

So the notion that officers will spring into action over a stolen package is fanciful.

But when did we become a nation that simply shrugs, rolls its eyes and accepts that thieves can help themselves to our property with virtual impunity?



Ask most rank-and-file officers and I suspect they’d love nothing more than to rid our streets of persistent offenders like Ronnie whose victims referred to him as “our thief”.

But police enthusiasm must be severely tested by the revolving-door justice system that sees prolific criminals repeatedly returned to the streets.

Take “prolific” shoplifter Michael Bogle, for example.

Just 24 hours after his early release from Wandsworth prison on October 1, he embarked on yet another crime spree and police spent an entire day dealing with the fallout.

Bogle was subsequently charged with four counts of shoplifting, commercial burglary and breaching court orders, and has now been returned to prison for the sixth time.



The senior officer involved spelled out the absurdity of the Government’s early release scheme.

“It puts demand straight back into policing who must arrest, investigate and put the individual back into custody,” he said.

“In this case, 27 officer hours were needed, leading to a cost of £1,887.”

That’s almost £2,000 of taxpayers’ money spent dealing with one repeat offender who, presumably, will eventually be back on the streets to start the whole sorry process again.

And it’s not an isolated case.



Metropolitan Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley says offenders released early from prison are breaching their electronic tagging conditions around 100 times a day in London alone.

Worse still, many are simply bailed back into the community under precisely the same conditions they’ve already flouted, with what he describes as “zero sanction”.

So, with the “justice system” being such a lame duck in the face of a petty crimewave, who could blame demoralised police officers for their lacklustre response when our parcels, bikes, garden tools or even cars are stolen?

They know full well that the “punishment” won’t be worth the paperwork.

Time to stomach real men



AROUND 20 years ago, I was sitting with Jeremy Clarkson and his family on a beach in Barbados when he got to his feet and sighed: “Right, let’s get it out of the way.”

As he removed his T-shirt and entered the sea, what I’d assumed was a beach full of relaxed sunseekers suddenly transformed into a paparazzi scrum as towels lifted to reveal long lenses.

The resulting photos appeared the next day with the headline “Pot Gear”.

Two decades later and 51-year-old Leonardo DiCaprio’s supposed “dad bod” has gone viral after he went topless on a Hawaiian beach at the weekend.

Good for him. Because let’s face it, as a “movie heart-throb” there could easily be pressure to spend every spare hour in the gym to appear box office “buff”.



Instead, this is the relatively normal, midlife physique of a man who’s perhaps decided to let his Oscar-winning acting do the talking.

And why not? Women are encouraged to embrace their bodies without apology, so men can too.

BEEFY A RARE BREED

FORMER England cricketer Lord Ian “Beefy” Botham has given an interview that’s refreshingly colourful in this world of increasingly vanilla public figures.

Highlights include the following.



On sports psychologists, special diets, curfews and hydration routines: “All bollocks”.

On coaching qualifications: “I am the certificate.”

On playing high-level cricket: “It’s a gift. You either have it or you don’t.”

On the police failing to investigate the theft of his farm vehicle: “They did f*** all. They’re an embarrassment.”

On health: “What is going on with the bloody NHS? In Australia, you get a blood test and the results the next day. Here – months!”



On illegal immigration: “There are no checks. Who are we letting in? Murderers, terrorists? Come on. We have no bloody idea.”

Sadly, the man whose life philosophy is, “don’t sit on your arse waiting for something to happen” has shown zero inclination to enter politics.

Botham or Burnham at the ballot box?

The latter would be out for a duck.

UN-LIKE TRUTH



AN official biography of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un predictably paints him as a man of great genius.

Apparently, he has “completely mastered” all military specialities across the army, navy and air forces, and has built “extensive knowledge” by reading “massive volumes of books” in sciences, computer engineering, politics, economics, culture, history and geography.

What a guy.

Meanwhile, back in the real world, friends who attended a Swiss school with him say he showed little academic promise and preferred basketball.

Such insubordination – orf with their heads.



KATE’S SMARTY TUBE

THE Princess of Wales has been spotted travelling the Tube with 11-year-old daughter Charlotte.

They sat among incredulous fellow passengers, with their security detail at a discreet distance.

Is this Catherine following the example of her mother-in-law Diana by showing her kids how ordinary people live?

Or is it one in the eye for Harry and Meghan, who appear to suggest their lives are in danger every time they leave the house?



Either way, I’m here for it.

THE King has bailed out brother Andrew again by paying the £1.5million repair bill on his old home Royal Lodge.

His continuing generosity towards his errant sibling has baffled many, but one assumes there’s method in the seeming madness.

For the alternative might mean Andrew doing a Prince Harry/Charles Spencer and raising funds via a tell-all book.

TRANS TESTS

LIONEL SHRIVER – the author who wrote the famous book We Need To Talk About Kevin, about a school shooter – says her next focus will be on the “fad for transgenderism”.



She knows it’s controversial and adds that she has “never dreaded” writing a novel more.

Hmmm, writing it is one thing.

Getting it past the Gen Z gatekeepers that now seem to populate so many publishing houses is quite another.

Still, there’s always self-publishing.

THE legal profession is scandalised by a “computer error” that, rather than just the customary glowing reviews for top barristers, allowed less than flattering appraisals to be uploaded to the Legal500 website.



One lawyer’s work was described as “sloppy” while another was called “adequate but disorganised and indecisive”.

The comments have now been removed but, considering the high charges for a top barrister, perhaps the public should be given the full picture on who they’re hiring?

News.title: Headteacher, 56, mowed down and trapped under car for over a mile before he died, murder trial hears
News.content:
'FLED THE SCENE' Headteacher, 56, mowed down and trapped under car for over a mile before he died, murder trial hears







Next

A HEADTEACHER was mowed down and trapped under a car for more than a mile before he died, a murder trial has heard.

Michael Mullins, 56, was cycling home from Stretford Grammar School in Manchester on April 20 when he was struck by a Volvo XC90 driven by Simon Richardson, Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court heard.

Richardson, 35, is said to have driven straight through give way markers at a junction and collided into Mr Mullins in Altrincham, Greater Manchester, the court was told.



Opening the case, Phil Barnes KC told jurors: “A number of eyewitnesses saw what happened.



“They did what any decent person, any of us, would have done having just seen a collision.

“They stopped their cars, they got out to see if everybody was OK.

“They called the emergency services.



“But not Simon Richardson.

“Simon Richardson did not stop to see if the cyclist he had just ploughed into was OK.

“Simon Richardson knowing he was to blame for what had just happened, turned his head, put his foot down and – at times travelling at double the speed limit – he fled the scene.

“The bike was obvious to the people who stopped to help. They could see it lying in the road.



“But what they could not find, despite searching the hedgerows and the fields by the road, was the cyclist who had been riding it.

“Michael Mullins was nowhere to be seen. Why? Because he was trapped beneath Simon Richardson’s car.

“This was murder, say the prosecution, because the evidence will show you that for a significant proportion of that journey Simon Richardson knew that Michael Mullins was there beneath the wheels of his car – trapped and injured but alive.

“He knew that what he was doing would kill Michael Mullins or at the very least cause him serious injury and yet he drove on anyway.”

Jurors were told that visible damage to Richardson’s Volvo was captured on an ANPR camera as he drove away from the collision – both to the bonnet and to the windscreen almost directly in front of the driver.



Mr Barnes said: “That damage was not there before the collision. It is beyond doubt, we say, that damage was caused by Michael Mullins being thrown up on to the bonnet of the Volvo when the defendant hit him.

“Putting it bluntly, there is no way on earth that Simon Richardson could not have known that he had just hit Michael Mullins and that he was very likely to be hurt.”

Later in the journey Richardson stopped his Volvo in a quiet country lane, got out of the driver’s seat and attempted in vain to pull Mr Mullins out from under the car, the court heard.

The defendant then drove on and was seen “veering sharply and deliberately from side to side” before his car mounted a grass verge, the court heard.

Mr Barnes said it was the Crown’s case that Richardson then drove over his victim at least once before he was finally dislodged and then made off from the scene.



He said: “Michael Mullins was crushed to death beneath the wheels of this defendant’s car, and his death was made quicker by the fact that he had been dragged against the surface of the road by Simon Richardson for more than 2km.”

Several witnesses to the collision followed “a trail of blood” and discovered Mr Mullins laid out on the grass verge.

Mr Barnes said: “The first man to get to him found him to be still breathing and barely alive.

“His breath would give out within the next few moments of that man arriving to help him.”

Medics attended and Mr Mullins, from Northwich, Cheshire, was pronounced dead at the roadside at 6.50pm – 40 minutes after the collision more than a mile and a third away.



Richardson was arrested the following day after he was said to have driven dangerously at speed in residential streets in Failsworth, Oldham, in a van as he was pursued by police, the court heard.

Richardson denies murder.

He has also pleaded not guilty to an alternative count of manslaughter and to an allegation of dangerous driving.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The trial continues.

News.title: Woke warrior Greta Thunberg joins France protests as cars torched & bins burned with 250,000 taking to streets
News.content:
Next

GRETA Thunberg has joined hundreds of thousands of enraged students in France as violent protests sweep the nation.

The Swedish woke-warrior joined joined protesters at the Paul-Eduard Lycée – one of the schools at the centre of the violent protests – in Saint-Denis, near Paris , on Tuesday.



Thunberg, 23, condemned what she saw as a “extremely violent” police response.

She said: “Our future is being robbed away from us”.



The woke activist, told reporters: “They should know that all over the world we are following these developments.

“We are inspired by the young people who are demanding their basic rights.



“Whether it’s not funding schools enough, or the climate crisis, or social injustice crises … it’s about time that young people are stepping up and reclaiming that future.”

The militant-Thunberg arrived on Tuesday where more than 250,000 protesters took to the streets across the country, according to the BBC.

Riot police in Paris were met with burning cars and rubbish bins as angry youths continue to inflict wide-spread havoc.

Teens in the capital reportedly blocked several entrances to schools before dawn.



Some 41,500 people participated in protests in Paris alone, the Interior Ministry said.

Outside Paris town hall, demonstrators sang anti-Macron slogans to an orchestra playing tunes including the Star Wars theme tune.

Demonstrations also took place in Nantes, Lens, Lyon, Strasbourg, Bordeaux and Marseille where protesters chants the revolutionary cry of “the struggle, the struggle, until victory”.

In Lyon, violence was met with tear gas after some of the 11,000 dissidents smashed windows of banks and insurance companies.



The education ministry said 214 schools were closed on Tuesday, while most universities were had closed in a show of solidarity.

Sparked by student protests in mid-September over teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms, and crumbling, rat-infested buildings, the movement has recently descended into violence and thuggery.

Last week, protesters torched classrooms and pelted police with rocks and bottles in clashes across Paris, Marseilles and Strasbourg.



One teenage boy had his fingers blown off by a grenade.

Thunberg is proving to be a rebel with many causes as her advocacy expands far beyond the issues that originally brought her notoriety.

Last December, the young activist was arrested in London at a demonstration in support of Palestine Action.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She was seen in footage holding a sign which read: “I support Palestine Action prisoners. I oppose genocide.”

Months before this she embarked on a voyage to Gaza on the so-called “Freedom Flotilla” in what would be her second attempt at reaching strip.

News.title: Andy Burnham to welcome Zelensky to No10 after Donald Trump's latest attack
News.content:
Andy Burnham to welcome Zelensky to No10 after Donald Trump's latest attack

No10 said the PM will use the Ukranian wartime leader's visit to reiterate the UK's 'rock-solid' support for Kyiv in their battle against Russian despot Vladimir Putin's barbaric attacks

View 2 Images Andy Burnham will welcome Ukraine's Zelensky to Downing Street on Wednesday (Image: ANDY RAIN/POOL/EPA/Shutterstock)

Andy Burnham is set to welcome Volodymyr Zelensky to Downing Street - after pledging to stand with the Ukrainian people for as long as it takes.

‌



‌



Downing Street said the Prime Minister will use the Ukrainian wartime leader's visit to London on Wednesday to reiterate the UK's "rock-solid" support for Kyiv in their battle against Russian despot Vladimir Putin's barbaric attacks.

‌



The public show of solidarity comes just days after the US President Donald Trump launched an extraordinary attack on Mr Zelensky, claiming it was "time for Ukraine] to get a new President".

‌



The pair clashed after the US announced a surprise deal to buy diesel from the Kremlin - undermining western sanctions against Moscow's war chest - and an "energy ceasefire" between Ukraine and Russia.

Mr Burnham said ahead of the visit: "Our rock-solid support to Ukraine is vital for keeping us safe here in the UK and ensuring those on the frontlines have the equipment they need to push back Russia.

"My message to the Ukrainian people could not be clearer, we are with you for as long as it takes, and we will go further and faster in our support to back your courageous fight for peace in Europe. It is not just the right thing to do, but it's the necessary thing to do. Russia's aggression cannot be allowed to succeed on our continent."

‌



View 2 Images PM Andy Burnham with Ukrainian President Zelensky during his visit to the US to attend the United Nations General Assembly in New York in September (Image: Toby Melville/PA Wire)

The Prime Minister is also expected to tell Ukraine's leader that UK ministers have been ordered to draw up further sanctions. Britain will also step up support with the delivery of £45 million of surface-to-air missiles deliveries, No10 added.

This includes deliveries of British Lightweight Multirole Missiles (LMMs), which they said had proven effective against jet-powered drones striking areas far beyond the frontlines of the war, including Kyiv.

‌



Chancellor John Healey will also use meetings at this week's International Monetary Fund (IMF) summit in Bangkok to urge allies to fully implement an equivalent ban on Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports.

Mr Healey said: "Conflict in the Middle East and in Europe is hitting people across the world. As the full-scale invasion of Ukraine by Putin continues, our commitment to the Ukrainian people is unshakeable. I urge partners to back the ban on Russian LNG, like we have done in the UK, to curtail the war chest funding Putin so desperately wants."

On Tuesday, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, who visited Kyiv last week, also suggested Britain could use frozen Russian assets to directly fund Ukraine's fightback against Putin's invasion.

‌



He claimed the EU and Britain could revisit plans to use the full value of frozen Russian assets, rather than just the profits and interest accrued on them. UK sanctions have frozen more than £25billion of Russian assets since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion.

Speaking at the Warsaw Security Forum, Mr Miliband claimed Russia was not winning the war, but that Vladimir Putin's advisers were afraid to tell him the truth.

He said: "Europe has big decisions to make, including on Russian sovereign assets. I think we need to return to this issue.

‌



"Britain is willing to do this alongside the European Union, because we know that every wrong message that is sent to President Putin is a message that sets back our security and sets back the Ukrainian cause, and we need to send the right messages."

The senior minister, who last week visited Ukraine, praised the resolve of its people, adding that it had shocked Putin.

He said: "It is a resolve which four and a half years ago Putin thought would not be there; he thought our resolve wouldn't be there either. We have proved him wrong on both of these fronts.

Article continues below

"I do think, by the way, in our narrative, we should talk about the barbarity of Putin. We are right to do so. We should also talk about the fact, as I did at the UN Security Council, he is not winning this war. And the truth is Lavrov and others don't want to tell him the truth: he is not winning this war, and that is very important."

News.title: Tiger attack victim identified as William Chapman who was a former child actor - latest
News.content:
William Chapman, described as in his 20s, took harrowing footage of the 30st tiger after he entered the enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park near Doncaster on Saturday

Tiger attack victim identified as William Chapman who was a former child actor - latest

The man who was horrifically mauled to death by a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park near Doncaster was a former child actor, it has emerged tonight.

William Chapman, described as in his 20s, jumped into the tiger enclosure at the zoo as terrified onlookers urged him to "play dead".

The Amur tiger, named Altai, then viciously attacked Mr Chapman and he was later pronounced dead at the scene. He had filmed chilling footage of himself approaching the tiger breathing heavily in the moments before the mauling.

Witnesses said Mr Chapman had seemed "so happy" before he climbed into the enclosure with police confirming he was not accompanied by anyone at the time of the attack .

The park confirmed that the tiger will not be euthanised following the incident but the site remains closed for the fourth day in a row.

A health and safety investigation is being conducted by City of Doncaster Council.

News.title: 'I'm a menopause expert - I swear by this quick trick to feel better'
News.content:
'I'm a menopause expert - I swear by this quick trick to feel better'

Perimenopause and menopause symptoms can feel overwhelming, but help is at hand. Ahead of World Menopause Day, Georgina Donnelly of Spirit 19 Yoga and Wellness menopause yoga club shares her top tips to feel empowered

View 3 Images Georgina says: "Exercise doesn't have to mean an expensive gym membership or punishing workouts." (Image: Luis Alvarez/Getty)

World Menopause Day is Sunday 18th October — so what better time to start a conversation about menopause? You don't need to spend a fortune, follow every piece of advice on social media or completely overhaul your life.

‌



‌



For me, it's about simple changes, listening to my body and finding what works for me. Here are 5 simple ways to feel more empowered through menopause.

‌



MOVE — find exercise you love

Exercise doesn't have to mean an expensive gym membership or punishing workouts. For me, discovering Yin Yoga and Reformer Pilates has made a real difference. One helps me slow down and stretch, while the other helps me build strength and feel good in my body. Find something you enjoy — because you're far more likely to keep doing it.

‌



EAT — nourish your body

Instead of spending a fortune on lots of supplements, start by looking at what's on your plate. Adding more vegetables, fruit, wholegrains, protein and calcium-rich foods to your everyday meals is a simple way to support your health. Small changes to your food can make a big difference.

View 3 Images Georgina says: "Pack your diet with nutrient-rich food to nourish yourself from the inside out." (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

REST — make time for yourself

We're often so busy looking after everyone else that we forget ourselves. Whether it's a walk, reading a book, a bath whilst listening to a podcast (a highlight for me!) or simply enjoying a cup of tea, give yourself permission to pause. Rest isn't selfish — it's self-care.

‌



ASK — don't suffer in silence

Talk to your GP about your symptoms and don't be afraid to ask questions. Go prepared with a list of your symptoms and make a few notes beforehand so you don't forget anything you want to discuss.

Ask for a blood test, including checking your hormone levels. You know your body best, so don't be afraid to speak up and ask for the support you need. Understanding what's happening to your body can be incredibly empowering.

View 3 Images Many say the stigma around the menopause has decreased in the last decade (Image: Getty Images)

‌



TALK — don't let social media overwhelm you

There is so much menopause advice online that it can quickly become overwhelming. One minute you're scrolling, the next you're wondering whether you need a cupboard full of supplements!

Step away from the screen and talk to other women, family and friends. You'd be surprised how many people have been through it, are going through it or simply understand what you're experiencing. Sharing experiences, having a laugh and knowing you're not alone can make a huge difference.

Menopause is a new chapter

You don't need an expensive wellness regime or a complete lifestyle overhaul. Move. Eat well. Rest. Ask questions. Talk. Find what works for you, take care of yourself and remember — you don't have to navigate menopause alone.

Join Georgina and other amazing women at Stretford Public Hall on Saturday 17th October for a day of exercise, conversation, wellbeing shopping and a silent wellness rave.
