News.title: Family of tiger attack victim pay tribute to 'bright' and 'amazing' man
News.content:
Family of tiger attack victim pay tribute to 'bright' and 'amazing' man

The family of William Chapman have paid tribute to their 'bright, warm and engaging' son after he was killed in a tiger attack as he entered the animal's enclosure

View 3 Images William Chapman's family have paid tribute to their son (Image: Sky News)

The family of a man who was mauled to death by a tiger after he entered its enclosure at a wildlife park have described him as "bright" and "dearly loved".

‌



‌



William Chapman, who was in his mid-20s, entered the pen at Yorkshire Wildlife Park near Doncaster on Saturday. He was pronounced dead at the scene.

‌



His family have released a statement which says William suffered from "significant mental illness" over a number of years and was given "strong medication".

‌



The statement continued: "William was a bright, warm and engaging young man whom his family dearly loved - and William loved them back.

View 3 Images Tributes have been left at the park entrance in memory of William Chapman (Image: Tom Maddick / SWNS)

"The family are utterly devastated by their loss and are struggling to come to terms with what has happened.

‌



"The family are hopeful that the relevant authorities will do their upmost to get to the bottom of why our amazing son did what he did."

City of Doncaster Council has launched a health and safety investigation into Chapman's death and the park remains closed.

The coroner will decide whether William's mental illness played a part in his death.

‌



William was a former child actor who appeared on the BBC and ITV. Chapman starred in the ITV production May Contain Nuts alongside Shirley Henderson, best known for playing Moaning Myrtle in the Harry Potter films.

He also played Edward Jenner as a young boy in the BBC series True Stories.

View 3 Images William Chapman was a child actor who played Edward Jenner in a BBC show (Image: BBC)

‌



It emerged today that he posted video footage of himself approaching the big cat before he was mauled to death.

Moments later, he was pictured sat on the floor as Altai repeatedly lunged at him. He was pronounced dead shortly after 1.30pm.

Before scaling the enclosure William had been dancing to music. He has also asked a park-goer to take a picture of him with Altai in the background before the incident.

Article continues below

The zoo, which opened in 2009 and spans 260 acres, has been closed since Saturday as investigations continue.

Yorkshire Wildlife Park have confirmed that the tiger will not be euthanised and was safe and well.

News.title: Katie Price tells child rape trial her ex-husband had 'done stuff' with other underage children
News.content:
Katie Price tells child rape trial her ex-husband had 'done stuff' with other underage children

Kieran Hayler, 39, is accused of committing three rapes and a sex assault against a 13-year-old girl between June and October 2016, while he was married to Katie Price

View 5 Images Katie Price arrives for a second day to Lewes Crown Court to give evidence (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

Katie Price today told a child rape trial that her ex-husband had "done stuff" with other underage children

‌



‌



Kieran Hayler, 39, is accused of committing three rapes and a sex assault against a 13-year-old girl between June and October 2016, while he was married to Ms Price. He denies all charges.

‌



Giving evidence from behind a screen, Ms Price, 48, spoke about checking into the Priory, which she claims she did to cope with the -allegations against Hayler.

‌



She said: “If you want to discuss the Priory, I’ll discuss it with you. I can expose Kieran for all the other children he’s done stuff with. I’m happy to tell the truth about the other kids who haven’t come forward, including [a child].”

View 5 Images Katie gave evidence in the trial on her ex-husband Kieran Hayler (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

During her evidence, Ms Price named two separate underage victims she claims Hayler abused. Neither are involved in the case and cannot be named for legal reasons. She did not elaborate on her claims.

‌



During cross-examination at Lewes crown court, in East Sussex, she was shown messages. She told the jury: “He also did stuff with [the named girl], she was underage.” She added: “I haven’t seen the name here for ages and it’s triggered me seeing the name in evidence.”

View 5 Images Katie Price leaving court on Tuesday (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

The trial has previously heard how Ms Price began quizzing the alleged victim in May 2017, when she was aged 14, about rumours she had heard about Hayler’s alleged conduct. In messages, Ms Price told her: “I’ll make you a little star.” Asked about the comment, Ms Price claimed: “That’s a figure of speech. She was 13. There was no agenda or nothing behind that.”

‌



Ms Price also accused Hayler of driving her to drugs by allegedly conducting a number of affairs with women, including with family nanny Nikki Brown. She alleged he introduced her to cocaine and removed SIM cards from her phones.

Ms Price said: “I went into the Priory because of the damage he had done to me with [complainant]. I had a breakdown. I -self-medicated on coke and had lots of therapy. Kieran introduced me to it.”

The court yesterday heard it is accepted that Hayler had an affair with Ms Brown. Ms Price said: “Ten months he had an affair with her.”

‌



View 5 Images Ms Price told the trial her ex-husband had 'done stuff' with other underage kids (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

Asked by the defence if she chose to employ Ms Brown because she was middle-aged, Ms Price said: “She was younger than me. I don’t know, I can’t remember how old she was. I don’t know, do I look middle-aged? I’m 48, I don’t know these days. I don’t know old Nikki was. But she was an adult.”

Challenged by Hayler’s barrister that she had chosen to employ her because “she wasn’t very attractive and was -overweight”, Ms Price said: “-Absolutely. There was a reason for that, so he didn’t cheat on me again, but he did.”

‌



Ms Price also denied claims from Hayler’s barrister Arlette Piercy that she has acted in an angry and vengeful way by making her accusations against him.

View 5 Images Katie Price walking into court on Monday (Image: Getty Images)

Ms Piercy told Ms Price: “You have evidenced a vendetta against him over a number of years.” Ms Price replied: “That is not true.” She was asked whether she had been following media reports of her trial. She said she had been handcuffed to Reform UK MP Suella Braverman all week for a TV show, saying: “I haven’t followed any reports.”

‌



Ms Price is set to give her third day of testimony today. She told the court she must attend a medical appointment in the morning, followed by a visit to her mum.

She said: “I promised my mum I’d see her tomorrow. My mum’s dying at the moment and I haven’t been able to see her because I’ve got a cold... she’s got days.”

Ms Price and Hayler were married from 2013 to 2021, but split in 2018. Last week, the jury heard Ms Price told a social worker in August 2018 that Hayler had groomed his alleged victim from when she was aged 13.

Article continues below

The mother of the alleged victim told the court in August 2017 her daughter claimed: “He’s done everything to me, Mummy.” She said she told Ms Price weeks later as she felt “a burden”. The trial continues.

News.title: Pope Leo XIV diagnosed with lung cancer as surgery to remove right lung lobe proves successful
News.content:
Pope Leo XIV diagnosed with lung cancer as surgery to remove right lung lobe proves successful

Pope Leo XIV has been diagnosed with lung cancer after undergoing major surgery, which saw part of his right lung removed, the Vatican has said today

View 2 Images Pope Leo has been diagnosed with lung cancer (Image: Getty Images)

Pope Leo XIV has been diagnosed with lung cancer after undergoing major surgery which saw doctors remove part of his right lung, the Vatican said.

‌



‌



Tests confirmed the 71-year-old has lung adenocarcinoma, which had been suspected by pre-operative tests and was confirmed during the 90-minute long procedure on Tuesday.

‌



The Vatican said there were currently no plans for the Pope to begin chemotherapy or other therapies, adding that the surgery was "successful" with "no complications".

‌



The Pope was in the operating room for around three hours, with the procedure itself lasting roughly 90 minutes, the statement added.

Pope risks reigniting Trump feud and slams death penalty after botched execution READ MORE :

View 2 Images The Pope's surgery was 'successful,' the Vatican said (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

He woke up normally after the surgery, and after a brief period of observation, returned to his room on the 10th floor of Rome's Gemelli Hospital to recover.

‌



According to the medical report, the Pope's operation involved the "radical" removal of the lower lobe of his right lung in a bid to eliminate the cancer.

"In order to make the procedure curative, the lower lobe of the right lung was removed using a video-assisted technique," lead surgeon, Professor Stefano Margaritora, said after the surgery.

"A rapid intraoperative histological examination confirmed the diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, as had been suspected from the pre-operative tests."

‌



Lung adenocarcinoma is the most common type of lung cancer, developing in cells that produce mucus, usually in the outer parts of the lungs.

It is a form of non-small cell lung cancer, and treatment depends on factors including how far the cancer has spread.

All of the Pope's audiences up to October 20 have been cancelled to allow him time to recover.

Article continues below

During his Sunday noon prayer, Leo revealed doctors had discovered a small nodule on his lung, adding that he would have it removed.

Oncologists previously said that even if the growth proved to be cancerous, Leo's prognosis was "excellent" as the nodule would be removed at an early stage.

News.title: Iran 'threatens ground invasions of US-allied neighbours' if Donald Trump’s war continues
News.content:
Iran 'threatens ground invasions of US-allied neighbours' if Donald Trump’s war continues

Iranian officials have reportedly threatened to launch ground invasions of neighbouring US allies as a retaliatory measure is Trump resumes attacks on Iran

View 5 Images Iran has reportedly threatened to attack its neighbours if the US resumes its war with Tehran (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Iran has threatened to launch ground invasions of neighbouring countries allied to the US if Donald Trump's war continues, reports have claimed.

‌



‌



Iranian officials have reportedly fortified nuclear and military sites along its borders with several nations that have backed Donald Trump since the US and Israel launched the war with Iran back in February. Iran has also reportedly rallied regime loyalists and is threatening to widen the ongoing conflict amid the upcoming US midterm elections.

‌



The US President, last week, promised not to attack Iran before the midterms but sources have reportedly said the country is preparing for possible attacks by Trump after the elections.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 5 Images Missiles on display next to a portrait of Iran's supreme leader (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Saudi pledged massive revenge attack after Houthis hit airports READ MORE :

Tehran has told regional officials that it would respond to any new attacks by hitting neighbouring US allies in retaliation, according to the Wall Street Journal.

‌



Iran shares borders with both Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, which have both been staunch supporters of the US. Other neighbouring countries include Afghanistan, Iraq, Pakistan, Oman, Bahrain, Qatar and Turkmenistan.

View 5 Images Female members of Iran's 'self-sacrificing' forces operating an anti-aircraft gun during military training (Image: Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

Iranian officials, cited by the WSJ, said forces "could conduct land incursions into neighbouring countries". This comes as Iran's security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, warned that Iran could target data centres, cables and artificial intelligence facilities across the region.

‌



Rezaei, on Monday, wrote in a X post: "Every miscalculation by the enemy against Iran has resulted in a heavy defeat for them; the next mistake will bring new fronts and greater surprises."

View 5 Images Iran has reportedly bolstered military sites near its borders (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Iran has reportedly also been preparing its people for a "renewed" conflict by making soldiers read war stories in schools to kids and holding political rallies.

‌



Billboards along the roads in Iran have also reportedly popped up to advertise sniper courses and training for civilians on how to use defensive shoulder-fired missile systems.

View 5 Images Pro-government supporters at an anti-US rally in Tehran, on October 11 (Image: Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

Iran has previously attacked its neighbours through drone attacks earlier in the war. These included an attack by Dubai's international airport in March, which saw a fire break out near the airport and even a residential luxury high rise on fire after an attack.

Article continues below

This comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham told the Commons yesterday that the alleged terror plot at RAF Fairford was "almost certainly" led by Iran.

He told MPs: "I can confirm our assessment that it is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran, almost certainly directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard."

News.title: William Chapman: Tiger attack victim was former child actor who appeared on BBC and ITV
News.content:
William Chapman: Tiger attack victim was former child actor who appeared on BBC and ITV

William Chapman, the man who died after entering a tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park, was a former child actor who appeared on the BBC and ITV, it has emerged

View 6 Images Tiger attack victim William Chapman (Image: Sky News)

The man who was fatally mauled after entering a tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park has been identified as a former child actor, it has emerged.

‌



‌



William Chapman died on Saturday afternoon after entering the pen, where he was attacked by a 200kg (31 stone) Amur tiger as onlookers made desperate attempts to distract the animal in a bid to save him.

‌



Emergency services were alerted shortly after 1.30pm but Chapman, who police said was visiting the park by himself, was declared dead at the scene.

‌



Tiger attack victim identified as William Chapman as first pictures emerge - latest READ MORE :

View 6 Images William Chapman was pronounced dead at the scene on Saturday (Image: Not known)

It has now come to light that the victim was a former child actor who featured in programmes on BBC and ITV.

Chapman appeared in the ITV drama May Contain Nuts alongside Shirley Henderson, best known for her role as Moaning Myrtle in the Harry Potter films, according to the BBC and confirmed by IMDB.

‌



He also played Edward Jenner as a young boy in the BBC series True Stories.

View 6 Images Clip from ITV show May Contain Nuts of character Alfie Chaplin, reportedly played by William Chapman (Image: YouTube)

Chapman, who is believed to be in his 20s, is said to have recorded the moment he approached the animal, according to footage shared on an Instagram account that has since been removed.

‌



The brief clip was shot from inside the tiger's enclosure and captured the large cat resting on top of a wooden platform, a few metres away from the camera.

In the audio, the person filming can be heard breathing heavily while distant voices shout "Oh my God" and "seriously".

View 6 Images Altai the Amur tiger (Image: Yorkshire Wildlife Park / SWNS)

‌



The park was evacuated and closed following the incident, and will stay closed on Wednesday, October 14, for the fifth consecutive day, reports the Daily Star.

Footage that began circulating online appeared to show Chapman being grabbed and wrestled by Altai inside the tiger enclosure at the park.

A separate clip seemingly captured the voice of Chapman requesting that people photograph him alongside the tiger just minutes before the horror unfolded.

‌



Visitors told how they noticed Mr Chapman on the viewing platform above the enclosure "dancing happily with his [headphones] in" as he watched the tigers with a group of roughly 15 to 20 people.

View 6 Images Yorkshire Wildlife Park after it was evacuated (Image: Charley Atkins / SWNS)

"He obviously wasn't with anyone and he asked a total stranger to take a picture of him with the tiger in the background," one visitor said. "Probably the last photo on his phone."

‌



Others told how a mum had desperately tried to stop Mr Chapman from climbing into enclosure, but "wasn't strong enough".

University graduate Anthony Hunt, 22, who was at the park with his partner Scarlet Hogan, 21, a pharmacy worker, said the victim appeared to be "praying and bowing down to the tiger" before the mauling.

Hogan said the man "started to fight back and screamed," adding: "It was like he was just detached from reality."

‌



View 6 Images Police were on the scene as the park was evacuated (Image: Charley Atkins / SWNS)

"The last thing we saw was the tiger was on his neck," he said.

In an earlier statement posted on social media, the wildlife park revealed that "many, many people" had reached out regarding Altai, the Amur tiger at the centre of the incident, confirming he is "safe and well" and will not be put down.

‌



The park also stated that members of its staff were "deeply affected" by the incident and are currently receiving specialist support.

South Yorkshire Police said officers received reports of a man entering a tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park at 1:35pm on Saturday, October 10.

"The tiger subsequently attacked the man, resulting in serious injury," the force added. "Emergency services attended and sadly, despite the best efforts of medical personnel, the man was pronounced dead at the scene.

Article continues below

"The man's family is aware and is being supported by specialist officers. Our thoughts are with them at this distressing time."

News.title: Family pays tribute to 'warm and engaging' man killed in tiger attack
News.content:
The family of a man who was killed by a tiger after he entered its enclosure at a wildlife park has paid tribute, describing him as "bright, warm and engaging".

William Chapman, 23, visited Yorkshire Wildlife Park near Doncaster on Saturday and was attacked after going into the animal's pen. He was pronounced dead at the scene.

In a statement, his family said that he had suffered from "significant mental illness" over a number of years and had been prescribed "strong medication".

It said it was for the coroner to decide whether his mental illness played a part in his death, asking that the public respect that process.

City of Doncaster Council has launched a health and safety investigation into Chapman's death and the park remains closed.

"William was a bright, warm and engaging young man whom his family dearly loved - and William loved them back," a statement released on Tuesday evening said.

The family also asked for privacy, saying "the publication and circulation of deeply offensive media content is causing them severe distress at an exceptionally vulnerable time".

"The family are utterly devastated by their loss and are struggling to come to terms with what has happened," the statement continued.

"The family are hopeful that the relevant authorities will do their upmost to get to the bottom of why our amazing son did what he did."

The incident, which took place shortly after 13:30 BST on Saturday, led to the evacuation and ongoing closure of the park.

An eyewitness described seeing Chapman wearing headphones and "pacing around" near the enclosure before he went in.

Mobile phone footage, believed to be from Chapman, appears to show the inside of the enclosure as he approaches the tiger across a patch of grass.

A stage school where Chapman had been a former pupil also posted a tribute on Tuesday.

"We loved watching William grow, both as a person and as a performer, during his time with us," the Jackie Palmer Stage School in High Wycombe said.

"It was a privilege to be part of his journey, and he will be remembered with great fondness by everyone who had the pleasure of knowing him."

Staff at Yorkshire Wildlife Park have separately said their "thoughts and heartfelt sympathies" are with Chapman's family and confirmed the rare Amur tiger, called Altai, remained in the enclosure and would not be euthanised.

News.title: Saudi man charged with planting 'sophisticated' recording device in OpenAI office
News.content:
A Saudi national has been charged with secretly planting a recording device in one of OpenAI's offices in California, federal prosecutors announced.

Abdulrahman Alfozan, who worked at the AI firm as an engineer, was charged federally with using or endeavoring to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications.

OpenAI said it had discovered a "sophisticated recording device" hidden in their San Francisco office and alerted the FBI. The company said it used its AI models to track that it had been planted by an employee.

Prosecutors say the device, wrapped in toilet paper, was found inserted in a USB port on the back of a TV in an executive conference room.

OpenAI, the maker of the popular chatbot ChatGPT, said that it has no indication that source code, model weights or customer data were inappropriately accessed or taken in the incident. It said the employee has been fired.

According to the complaint, Alfozan "allegedly concealed a covert recording device inside his employer's executive conference room to secretly capture sensitive communications," FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement.

Patel said that the alleged goal was to capture information about the company's AI product.

Alfozan has been working as an engineer at OpenAI since July 2025, prosecutors say.

On 30 September, OpenAI employees discovered the device - two days after prosecutors say it had been installed. The device was encrypted, prosecutors said.

OpenAI said they were able to use their AI models "to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier".

According to the FBI, the suspect used a "productivity tool" and a "chatbot" to research sensitive locations at OpenAI and how to secretly place audio equipment.

Chatbot prompts that he is alleged to have searched include "building, customizing, installing, audio recording, testing, obfuscating, and remote accessing a device", prosecutors allege.

He is also accused of using the chatbot to ask about "'build[ing] a continuous audio recorder,' 'customiz[ing] Wi-Fi . . . connectivity,' 'improv[ing] audio and live listening,' and 'encrypt[ing] the SD card'".

News.title: 'If we don't scream, they won't listen to us': Student protesters speak to BBC in Paris
News.content:
Students protests in France have entered their fourth week and with a renewed impetus, according to the BBC's James Waterhouse.

The nationwide demonstrations against poor classroom conditions, including old buildings, teacher shortages and overcrowded classrooms, have caused disruption to education across France as hundreds of lycÃ©es (15-18 year-olds colleges) had to be closed.

Students on the streets of Paris told the BBC that they had not achieved anything yet and that stopping now would be a "defeat".

More on this story.

News.title: Football regulator says he would quit over any political interference in Man City case
News.content:
The head of English football's independent regulator says he will resign if he encounters any political interference over the future of Manchester City.

As chairman of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR), David Kogan has the power to assess the suitability of club owners and executives.

If an independent commission's findings that the club broke Premier League financial rules are upheld, the watchdog could even force a sale.

Last month, the Prime Minister Andy Burnham was criticised for saying he would be "really concerned" if the scandal led to Manchester City's Abu Dhabi owners selling the club.

"They've been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester and obviously the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is," he added.

When asked about Burnham's comments, Kogan told BBC Sport: "The Prime Minister is entirely entitled to make his own observations on anything.

"We are independent. That is in the name. I am the chairman of the Independent Football Regulator and independence absolutely runs through everything we're doing.

"And no politician has tried to influence and would try to influence anything we do on that."

When asked what he would do if he did come under political pressure over the case, Kogan replied: "I would resign."

An independent commission found City had broken rules over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018. Owners Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) - a private investment company belonging to United Arab Emirates vice-president and deputy prime minister Sheikh Mansour - are said to have topped up the value of commercial deals as part of a "disguised funding scheme" to the scale of Â£830m.

City insist they are innocent and have appealed.

News.title: Russia did try to interfere with Brexit vote but had little impact, MI5 chief says
News.content:
MI5 chief Sir Ken McCallum has said there was Russian interference in the the Brexit referendum, but warned against overstating its impact on the result.

It comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham provoked a backlash from some Brexit campaigners by saying it was "clear" there had been interference by Moscow in the 2016 vote.

Sir Ken said it was "a matter of public record" that there was interference in the referendum by online trolls and bots.

However, he suggested Russian trolls would be "delighted" to be front page news again, "despite the comparative unimpressiveness" of their efforts.

He added: "There is a really important difference between interference attempted and outcome swayed.

"I am a little bit anxious that we don't play into our adversaries' hands by making these trolls look 10ft tall."

Conservative deputy leader Alex Burghart branded Sir Ken's comments "an extraordinary slap down to the prime minister".

In an interview released on Monday, Burnham told The Rest is Politics podcast, external that upon arriving in Downing Street, he had asked if there had been Russian interference in the 2016 vote, adding: "I've had the clear answer that, yes, there was."

He did not provide details about the extent or nature of Russian activities during the interview, and when pressed on the subject in the House of Commons on Monday afternoon appeared to be less definitive.

The PM denied claims from Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch that he was implying the referendum result was illegitimate because of Russian interference.

He said it was a "matter of record" that Russia sought to interfere in the 2019 general election, adding: "We think it is inconceivable that this was the first time".

A No 10 spokesperson also clarified that while the prime minister believed it was highly likely Russia tried to influence the referendum result, he did not believe those efforts were successful.

The Conservatives accused Burnham of making an "embarrassing retreat" after "being caught out trying question the legitimacy of the referendum result".

News.title: Zelensky and Burnham to meet in Downing Street
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham will host Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky at Downing Street on Wednesday, as the UK announces it will accelerate its delivery of air defence missiles to Kyiv.

Burnham is also expected to set out how his government will draw up further sanctions against Russia.

Speaking ahead of the meeting, Burnham said the UK was with Ukraine "for as long as it takes", adding: "Russian aggression cannot be allowed to succeed on our continent."

The UK will also urge allies to step up pressure on Russia, with Chancellor John Healey using International Monetary Fund (IMF) meetings to call for a ban on Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG).

This will be Zelensky's second visit to the UK since Burnham became prime minister. His first was in late July, days after Burnham entered No 10, when the pair met troops and led a news conference at a naval base in Portsmouth.

Burnham said: "Our rock-solid support to Ukraine is vital for keeping us safe here in the UK and ensuring those on the frontlines have the equipment they need to push back Russia.

"My message to the Ukrainian people could not be clearer, we are with you for as long as it takes, and we will go further and faster in our support to back your courageous fight for peace in Europe.

"It is not just the right thing to do, but it's the necessary thing to do."

Among the measures being announced is the quicker delivery of British Lightweight Multirole Missiles (LMMs), with the UK having already committed to send more than 5,000 worth Â£1.6bn over the next four years.

The UK will also reaffirm its plans to fully implement a maritime services ban on Russian LNG exports.

The meeting between Zelensky and Burnham follows what Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband described as a "very difficult few days" for UK-US relations due to President Donald Trump's decision to ease sanctions on Russian diesel.

Zelensky criticised the US deal with Russia, calling it a "gift" to President Vladimir Putin. Trump, in response, called for new leadership in Ukraine and criticised Zelensky for striking Russian oil refineries.

Meanwhile, Healey will ask partners at the IMF to step up support for Kyiv and ensure Russia heeds the US' call for a full energy ceasefire.

Trump claimed on Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an immediate energy ceasefire - but hours later, Zelensky said Russian attacks on energy facilities had continued.

On Monday, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Ukraine did not deserve the "respite" a ceasefire would bring.

News.title: Bumble bought for $1.3bn in 'bet on the future of humanity'
News.content:
Dating app Bumble has been bought for $1.3bn (Â£980m) in what the new owners called "a bet on the future of humanity".

Investment firm Ithaca Holdings is taking over the loss-making firm and it directors, Ravi Gupta and John Hegeman, will become co-chief executives of the company which once differentiated itself by having a "women-first" chat rule.

Bumble ditched the rule in August this year.

Whitney Wolfe Herd, Bumble's founder and current chief executive, said she would remain "actively involved" with the business she set up 12 years ago.

While it is unclear what Wolfe Herd's role at the dating app will be, she said she will work closely with the new owners.

Gupta and Hegeman said they wanted to use technology to "renew and accelerate businesses...in a world transformed by AI".

They said: "Technology should work in service of our deepest source of fulfillment, human connection and this investment is a bet on the future of humanity."

This contrasts with a recent debate over the safety of AI, with some experts claiming the speed of its development threatens the future of humanity.

Bumble's share price has soared as news of the deal began to emerge. The jump lifted its company valuation to over $580m but that is still far below a peak of more than $14bn it reached after it floated the business on the Nasdaq stock index in 2021.

Since becoming a public company, it has made an annual pre-tax profit only once, in 2023.

In the following two years, it reported steep losses, though during that period Bumble had been working to incorporate new technology, including AI, into its app.

Its chief executive in 2024, Lidiane Jones, told the BBC she believed AI had "exciting potential" in dating apps related to safety, and Bumble had been looking at research that found Gen Z and milliennials were interested in AI assistance with creating profiles.

This year, the dating app unveiled several new AI features, including profile guidance to help people create dating profiles.

Bumble was launched in 2014 by Wolfe Herd who built the brand around a distinctive feature that only allowed women to initiate conversations with matches.

It recently abandoned that rule, prompting debate among users over whether the app had lost what set it apart from rivals.

"Today, our community is asking for more flexibility, less pressure, and more opportunities to create real, meaningful connections and that is what this new experience provides," Wolfe Herd said in August.

Dating apps like Bumble have come under pressure in recent years as some younger users have grown disillusioned with browsing for dates.

Bumble said in 2025 that it would cut almost a third of its workforce as the industry grappled with what Wolfe Herd described as an "inflection point" in online dating.

Investments in other dating companies have also soured as apps have struggled to convince users to pay for their services.

Match Group - which owns apps including Tinder, OkCupid and Hinge - has also seen its shares fall sharply from their peak in 2021.

According to a report by media watchdog Ofcom in 2025, adults in the UK were spending less time on dating apps compared to three years earlier.

Some single people are instead turning to board game get-togethers, book clubs and other group activities in the hope of finding a partner.

News.title: Three things we've learnt about the UK economy from the IMF
News.content:
There is increased concern about how much money countries are borrowing, but the IMF said the UK is doing better than all other major economies at this.

The IMF said the UK "basically stands out, along with India" when it comes to addressing the problem and by 2031 it is projected to have the lowest annual borrowing of the G7 group of countries, which includes Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the US.

Sir Howard Davies, former deputy governor of the Bank of England, said this was largely because the UK has a government with a majority which has committed to tackling the situation, which it is expected to achieve either through tax rises, cuts to public services, or a mix of both.

By contrast, he says the US has said little about reducing its deficit, while France and Germany don't have majority governments.

"So, we [the UK] are not great students, but we look somewhat better than some of the others we are sharing the class with," he said.

Meanwhile, the IMF's growth forecasts for the UK mean it is expected to have the second-fastest growing economy in the G7 this year along with Germany.

Sir Howard believes this should also be seen in context.

"We're still growing slowly. It's almost like saying we're winning a slow bicycle race here because other people are going backwards a bit more rapidly than we are."

News.title: Argentina targets UK in legal claim over Falklands oil exploration
News.content:
The Sea Lion oilfield, around 130 miles (209 km) from the Falkland Islands, contains an estimated 1.7 billion barrels of oil.

The Falkland Islands government extended exploration licences last month and the field is expected to start pumping in 2028, potentially generating huge revenues for the roughly 3,500 inhabitants of the islands.

Two oil companies â Britain's Rockhopper Exploration and Israel's Navitas Petroleum â have insisted they have valid licences issued by Britain.

The Argentinian government claims the marine environment of disputed maritime areas is protected by international law.

Its application "seeks to preserve Argentina's sovereign rights over its continental shelf and prevent activities authorised unilaterally and illegally by the United Kingdom".

In a post on X, Argentinian Foreign Affairs Minister Pablo Quirno said the government was requesting the tribunal make a number of orders against the UK, including halting new exploration permits.

But the UK government insists Sea Lion is lawful, located on the Falkland Islands shelf and regulated by the islands' government.

While the Falkland Islands government grants exploration licences, they must be signed off by the UK Foreign Secretary.

Kumaran said the tribunal application "does not invalidate licenses issued by the Falkland Islands government, alter the islands' regulatory authority, or require lawful hydrocarbon development activities to cease".

The tribunal that will consider the dispute is an independent judicial body based in Hamburg which is responsible for the fair application of the United Nations' Convention on the Law of the Sea.

FCDO officials have made clear the UK will engage with the tribunal but resist Argentina's claim firmly.

They said the aim was not to escalate the dispute but respond firmly to Argentina's latest move, and defend what the UK sees as legitimate economic activity.

They also hope to provide reassurance to businesses fearful of Argentine retribution. That is why they are introducing measures under the Protection of Trading Interests Act that would protect firms from any extra-territorial impact of Argentine laws following Milei's sanctions threats.

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said: "Argentina's attempts to intimidate businesses and individuals engaged in legitimate commercial activity are unacceptable. Companies should be free to make lawful commercial decisions without the threat of political coercion."

The latest move comes after Milei roundly criticised the UN in his speech at the General Assembly late last month for failing to act over the sovereignty of the Falkland Islands.

He said the UN had become "a useless organisation" which only serves "arrogant parasites dressed up as well-intentioned bureaucrats".

On Tuesday Kumaran described Milei's remarks at New York as "inflammatory".

Despite its defeat in 1982, Argentina has always maintained its right to the Falkland Islands. But over the years successive governments have pressed their claim with varying degrees of aggression and diplomacy.

UK officials believes the current Argentine leadership is deliberately picking a fight ahead of elections next year.

News.title: Supreme Court hears church warden murder appeal
News.content:
A former deputy church warden could not have have legally caused a university lecturer's death by giving him potentially sedated whisky, the Supreme Court has been told.

Benjamin Field, 35, was jailed for at least 36 years in 2019 after being found guilty of murdering 69-year-old Peter Farquhar in Maids Moreton, Buckinghamshire.

In April, appeal judges quashed Field's conviction and ordered a retrial, but said the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) could take the case to the Supreme Court first.

And on Tuesday, five justices at the UK's highest court were asked to consider whether Field could have made Mr Farquhar cause his own death without Field legally being responsible.

During his murder trial prosecutors said Field drove Farquhar to believe he was losing his mind, secretly drugging him and spiking his whisky so his death would appear to be suicide or an accident, allowing Field to inherit his home and money.

The case has previously been adapted into Bafta winning BBC drama The Sixth Commandment, starring Timothy Spall and Anne Reid.

Before his murder trial, Field admitted burglary and fraud offences connected with relationships he had formed with Farquhar and his neighbour, fellow pensioner Ann Moore-Martin, to persuade them to change their wills.

He received a concurrent 16-year sentence for those offences. He was cleared of conspiring or attempting to murder Moore-Martin and of possessing an article for use in fraud.

The hearing was due to conclude on Tuesday, with a decision expected at a later date.

News.title: Majority of English football clubs on the edge of financial disaster, report says
News.content:
English football's finances are "dangerously exposed, with the majority of clubs living on the edge of financial disaster", according to a landmark report by the independent football regulator.

Research by the watchdog found 94% of clubs are loss-making, and more than 60% of EFL and National League clubs are technically insolvent.

The regulator (IFR) warns of "a dangerous cocktail of rising debt and an over-reliance on owner funding, leaving clubs and their fans at risk".

The 'State of the Game' report also suggests that despite the economic success of the Premier League, the financial 'cliff-edges' between and within leagues have grown significantly.

The report says:

94% of clubs in the top five English leagues made losses in 2025-26

17 clubs across the EFL and National League would be loss-making even if their players played for free

66% of clubs could not survive for more than 90 days without new owner funding

29% of clubs reported they could not survive more than 30 days without such funding

68% of clubs have no contingency plan if their owner walks away

The IFR claims "the underlying foundations of the pyramid are under intense strain and require urgent reform", and its report "should serve as a wake-up call" for English football.

"Seventeen clubs are now trading in such a way that if their players played for free, their non-playing costs would mean they would go bust," IFR chair David Kogan told BBC Sport.

"Thirty-two clubs are operating on only 30 days' cash. If the owner chooses not to pay cash at the end of the month, those clubs go bust.

"That is a very, very risky scenario. This is the moment of addressing these problems before money starts to dry up.

"We can actually fix the house while the sun is still shining and that's essentially what our role is going to be in this."

News.title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash
News.content:
The court heard Dowling, from Caerphilly, was driving with his wife and their lifelong friend, who they were taking to a hospital appointment, when the collision happened.

Despite wet and windy conditions, heavy rain and high levels of surface water, he was travelling at 76mph (122 km/h) just three seconds before the crash.

After aquaplaning, the defendant crashed into a stationary black Audi A3 driven by Sharon, who had pulled over because of the weather conditions.

She suffered catastrophic injuries and spent three months in hospital before her death in January 2024.

In a victim impact statement, her son Luke Berry, who is expecting a child, described the family's loss as immeasurable, saying his mother would never get the chance to meet her grandchild.

He said: "She was loving, caring and would do anything to make sure I was OK.

"My family will never be the same without her."

The court was also told Jane Beedell suffered multiple injuries in the crash, including chest and elbow injuries, bruising, wounds to her fingers, bleeding on the brain and multiple fractures to her ribs.

She was placed in an induced coma for weeks, and told the court the crash had left her struggling with "fear, anxiety and depression".

"I used to be confident, strong and an outgoing individual," she said, explaining how she now relies on family and friends for daily support and struggles with everyday tasks, finding it difficult to go out alone.

After 48 years working in the civil service, Jane said she had lost her job and now relied on benefits.

She said she was devastated by the changes to her life, adding: "I sometimes feel guilty I survived".

The court heard how Kim Dowling was left paralysed with a broken back and neck and unable to speak after her voice box was removed following the crash.

Mitigating, Dowling's barrister said the defendant felt "deep regret and remorse for the loss of life", along with "strong feelings of guilt and emotional distress".

The court heard that every time Dowling looked at his wife, he was reminded of what he had done.

The case was initially brought as dangerous driving, but the charges were later changed to careless driving, to which he pleaded guilty.

Dowling had previously been disqualified from driving for six months about 15 years ago after reaching 12 penalty points, the court heard.

However, he had no previous convictions despite years of long-distance driving for work and was described as a man of "good character" who was a full-time carer for his wife.

During the sentencing, Judge Hughes said Sharon Berry had suffered a "senseless death", adding that "no amount of sentence given to Dowling would bring her back".

Dowling was sentenced to 27 months in prison for causing death by careless driving and two counts of causing serious injury by careless driving, suspended for two years.

He was also disqualified from driving for four years, ordered to complete 250 hours of unpaid community work and pay Â£1,630 in prosecution costs.

News.title: Raye hits back at ticket touts who 'overwhelmed' sign-up for Albert Hall show
News.content:
Raye has hit back at ticket touts who she says "overwhelmed" the sign-up process for an upcoming live show by using artificial intelligence (AI) bots to create "hundreds of thousands of fake registrations".

The Where Is My Husband! singer revealed there were 1.8 million sign-ups for her one-off 5,000-seat performance at the Royal Albert Hall on 23 October.

To avoid a pre-sale which she felt scalpers could exploit, Raye said the sign-up list had been manually reviewed to identify a shortlist of people believed to be "real fans".

A spokesperson for the Royal Albert Hall said they "invest heavily" in protecting their ticketing systems from "automated attacks" but the "law needs to catch up".

The award-winning artist said she had "never witnessed bots on this scale" and was changing the process as it is "so important" to her that fans can buy tickets at the face value price.

"I'm not sure what the future holds for ticketing, I do know this experience has really opened my eyes," she said in a statement shared on her social media accounts, external.

"Me and my team are going to think really hard about what we can do in the future."

Raye said the fans manually selected would receive a pre-sale link and code by email at 11:45 BST on Tuesday, and pre-sale opened shortly afterwards.

She added that the remaining tickets would be available to all on general sale.

This Symphony May Contain Hope show will showcase songs from her recent chart-topping second album, This Music May Contain Hope, that fuses old-school jazz with orchestral sound, blues, big band and soul.

The 17-track record is a concept album which explores overcoming heartbreak, self-doubt and internet trolling.

News.title: Katie Price denies 'any venom' against ex at his rape trial
News.content:
Katie Price has denied having "any venom" against her ex-husband at his rape trial.

Kieran Hayler is on trial at Lewes Crown Court accused of three counts of rape and one of sexual assault against a then-13-year-old girl in West Sussex in 2016, all of which he denies.

When challenged by defence lawyer Arlette Piercy on her view of her ex-husband, Price said: "I don't have any venom against Kieran, it was amicable when we split."

Reality star Price also denied being "angry and vengeful" towards Hayler.

During her evidence to Lewes Crown Court, Price was asked by Piercy if she "loved revenge or is it just TV?".

"It's TV, it's what I say. It's what drives me in my work," Price said.

Piercy told Price: "You are angry and vengeful towards the defendant Kieran Hayler, you have evidenced a vendetta against him over a number of years."

Price responded: "That is not true."

Price also said she was using "a figure of speech" when she messaged the teenage girl allegedly raped by her then-husband.

Jurors had previously seen messages sent between Price and the girl, then aged 14, in which the media personality said she had heard Hayler and the girl kissed and he had "tried it on" with her, adding: "I'm only asking as this is a serious allegation."

The teenager replied that it was "just a flirt thing" and "nothing happened".

News.title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme
News.content:
About 650 more offenders are leaving jails in England and Wales on Tuesday, in the second phase of the early release scheme - the government's plan to tackle the prison population crisis.

It includes offenders sentenced to up to two and a half years who are leaving jail after serving a third of their sentence behind bars, rather than half.

The second wave of releases comes as the government takes its plan to radically overhaul criminal courts back to Parliament - but also as probation officers prepare to vote in a ballot that could lead to a strike over pay and workload.

Some 700 offenders left jail early on 1 October - all of whom were serving terms of less than 19 months.

Tuesday's second stage begins the process of releasing batches of offenders on increasingly longer sentences - culminating next June with those serving more than 12 years.

Around 5,000 prisoners are scheduled to be released, down from 6,000 after ministers intervened to make rapists and the most serious child sex offenders exempt.

Prisoners convicted of manslaughter are also excluded, meaning the killers of PC Andrew Harper, who died in the line of duty in 2019, will not be eligible. Those jailed for a range of offences, including members of child grooming gangs convicted of indecent assault are also ineligible.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said "the programme is clearly not working," stating she is "worried about dangerous people being let out on the street when they haven't served their sentence, haven't been rehabilitated".

Victims' groups have also raised concerns about the scheme.

Alice Russell-Harris from the charity Refuge - which supports survivors of domestic abuse - told the BBC that domestic abuse perpetrators are among those being released.

This "will put survivors at serious risk of harm," she said, adding that even though there may be conditions such as electronic tagging and restriction zones, "we know that license conditions are frequently breached."

The early release scheme is "terrifying for survivors," said Veronica Oakeshott from the charity Women's Aid.

Reports of failures in the electronic tagging system have added to their concerns. The scheme is "dangerous and should not go ahead," Oakeshott told the BBC.

News.title: Ex-Met Police officer trained to support rape victims accused of rape
News.content:
He later phoned her and said nothing sexual had happened, the court was told.

Tyrrell is also accused of perverting the course of justice by trying to delete messages between them. In one, he apologised for "being a sex offender" and for ruining her life, jurors heard. When she told him not to say such things, he replied that they were true.

The prosecution alleges Tyrrell raped the woman by having sex with her after she had repeatedly said no.

Afterwards, he allegedly asked whether she realised that what he had done "was rape", and said he would report himself and would undoubtedly go to prison, Farrelly said.

The woman alleges that on several occasions she woke to find Tyrrell penetrating her, despite having refused sex the night before.

On one occasion, when she asked him what had happened, he shouted at her and asked whether she realised what she was saying and what could happen to him, the prosecutor told the court.

Jurors heard the woman kept a list of incidents involving Tyrrell, including the alleged sexual assaults.

In a police interview, she said she had felt pressured by him and feared no-one would believe her because she could not prove what had happened. She was also worried police would protect him because he was an officer, the court heard.

After his arrest, Tyrrell denied ever having sex with her.

Tyrrell, of Meltham, West Yorkshire, has admitted misconduct in public office. He has also pleaded guilty to a separate count of perverting the course of justice by persuading the woman to lie to police about why he was in her bedroom.

The trial continues.

News.title: Atletico Madrid v Man United LIVE: Michael Carrick responds after bombshell Lisandro Martinez interview
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

( Reuters )

Manchester United’s winless run stretched to a fifth game after falling to a 2-0 defeat at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League, as Michael Carrick’s side conceded inside the opening 60 seconds and finished with 10 men as Leny Yoro was sent off.

The visitors made the worst possible start in Madrid as a simple ball behind the much-changed United back-line led Alex Baena to square to Pablo Barrios for a simple finish, despite Heaven’s attempt to clear.

In fairness, United responded well but were guilty of missing chances. Bryan Mbeumo spurned two opportunities in the first half before Bruno Fernandes volleyed wide from in front of goal and then hit the crossbar in the second half.

Yoro’s red card for denying a goalscoring opportunity, awarded following a VAR review after the young centre-back pulled down Jonathan David, ended the match as a contest and Ademola Lookman turned in a rebound to double Atletico’s lead.

After a 1-1 draw against 10-man Tottenham this weekend, Carrick will face mounting pressure as he takes his side to Elland Road on Sunday for a must-win clash at rivals Leeds United.

Follow latest updates from the Metropolitano with our live blog below:

News.title: Kelly Clarkson saga escalates again as Brooklyn toy shop owner says singer ‘put us in danger’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Kelly Clarkson has been accused by the co-owner of a New York City toy shop of putting its staff in “danger.”

A dispute between the two parties has been rumbling since this weekend, when the 44-year-old “Breakaway” singer shared in an X post to her eight million followers that she had visited Brooklyn games store Art of Play and interacted with a “rude” sales associate in an experience she compared to a famous scene in Pretty Woman.

On Tuesday, Adam Rubin, one of the shop’s three co-owners, answered questions from a scrum of reporters.

According to New York magazine, Rubin described the situation as an “insane misunderstanding.”

He added: “Nothing happened in this shop to justify her scolding our shopkeeper on the way out, but I can let that go. You know, everybody has a bad day. But things changed when she used her platform to attack us. It’s asymmetrical social warfare.”

open image in gallery Kelly Clarkson has been accused of ‘asymmetrical social warfare’ by a NY toy shop ( NBC/The Kelly Clarkson Show )

Rubin said that Clarkson had visited on an occasion when the store was busy, and had been assisted by staff who offered to show her a variety of products. “She was in the shop for less than five minutes,” he said. “If this tweetstorm had not happened, we wouldn’t have realized there was a negative interaction in the shop; it was that undramatic. We treated her like a normal person, but apparently that didn’t live up to her expectations.”

He went on to strongly criticize Clarkson for directing her large social media following at the store, saying: “Kelly Clarkson has put us in danger. People are getting threatened on the street, and the worst part is we didn’t know this was going to happen but Kelly Clarkson did. Anyone who expresses admiration, positivity, or sympathy for Art of Play is getting attacked by trolls.”

Workers did receive the backing of the local community, said Rubin, who added: “People were coming by almost entirely in support. On Monday, when we were closed, people were bringing pastries and cupcakes, according to the press that was staked out here. But our friends are getting attacked, and our fans are getting attacked. We’re concerned on behalf of our shopkeepers.”

open image in gallery Molly, a singing and dancing mechanical bird created by artist Bliss Kolb, has found itself at the center of the online furore ( AP )

Rubin explained that Art of Play has received numerous threatening calls and online comments, saying of the trolls: “They’re calling. They’re emailing. They’re leaving reviews on every platform, they’re review-bombing, they’re attacking anyone who mentions us on social media. They’re shouting, they’re screaming. They show up, they shout, ‘You’re racially profiling Kelly Clarkson!’ This was out on the sidewalk, so neighbors called the police, and when they filmed the neighbors their followers doxxed the neighbors.”

The shop owner added that on Sunday they “turned off the phone” but they continued to receive a stream of negative comments. “There’s so much hate speech, so many threats of violence,” he said. “If an actual customer tries to get in touch with us right now, they will never be able to.”

After the shop earlier posted a statement stating that the wooden bird automaton that Clarkson had been interested in was not for sale, the singer and former talk show host doubled down and responded: “So you’re not only rude, you’re also a liar. Got it.”

News.title: Trump rails against ‘disgusting’ nemesis Letitia James handling Cornell rape investigation
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Donald Trump on Tuesday demanded that New York Attorney General Letitia James be removed from an investigation into an alleged rape at Cornell University, calling the state’s top prosecutor a “disgusting cop” with “zero credibility.”

He posted to Truth Social that James’s involvement in the case would lead to automatic appeals and urged New York Governor Kathy Hochul to replace her.

“How can ‘New York State Attorney General,’ Letitia James, be allowed to investigate the Cornell rape scandal, when she is a DIRTY AND DISGUSTING COP herself, and has ZERO credibility?” Trump posted. “Any decision will be appealed by her mere presence on this case. The stench of Letitia James will greatly add to the anguish that everybody feels in viewing how this case is being handled.

“The Governor should take James off this case, IMMEDIATELY, and replace her with somebody who is not a Third Rate, Crooked Politician!”

This is a breaking story. More to come...
