News.title: ‘We expect more from the top’: Lisandro Martinez scorches Man United leadership in astonishing interview
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez called out the club’s technical director Jason Wilcox for not supporting Michael Carrick in the transfer market in an astonishing interview following the 2-0 defeat at Atletico Madrid.

United have won just two of their first nine games of the season, and are winless in their last five, after a summer in which the club spent £148m on upgrading their midfield, but in which they were also outspent by their closest rivals and failed to strengthen other key areas.

A fuming Martinez said the United players wanted the club to show more ambition to build a Premier League title challenge after finishing third last season and insisted others must take the blame for their poor start to the new campaign, pointing his finger at the “technical director” Wilcox and the club’s wider leadership.

open image in gallery Jason Wilcox, the technical director of Manchester United, was called out by Lisandro Martinez ( Getty )

“Really poor. Really poor. I have to control myself a lot,” Martinez told Prime Video after the defeat at Atletico. “But... sometimes it’s a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment, you know? We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top, from up.

“You know, doing more, [signing] more players to compete because many, many teams, bring many players as well. And today, also, Atletico, they have an amazing team. And they deserved to win today.

“I expect more, 100 per cent. I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]. I have to be honest, you know. As players, we have to do more, but it's so important when you make a strong squad to be ready to this kind of night.

“I think last season, we did everything, we create a base to build an amazing team. But this is something, to be honest. And to prove something, you know? It's annoying, disappointing, coming here, and I'm not seeing my team trying to get an amazing result here. It’s disappointing.”

Carrick will now be under further pressure ahead of Sunday’s trip to Leeds but Martinez said there should be criticism of “other areas” of the club rather than continuing the cycle of blaming the manager.

“He [Carrick] does his best. Every season is different. You can't stay with what you did last season,” Martinez said. “The teams knows how you play, they know every detail, if you don't change next season is a big problem.

"You can't keep changing, changing, changing the manager. What about other areas? I can't say more. Tonight it is easy to say the coach, easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas.”

Carrick told Prime Video immediately after Martinez’s interview that he had not seen the Argentina international’s comments and refused to respond to them when they were read out to him by interviewer Gabriel Clarke.

"I haven't seen it. After a game like this you come here to try and get something from the game and you are disappointed and can be emotional. I have not seen it so I don't think it is the right time. We all care and show that in different ways but now is the time to be together and work through."

News.title: Manchester United’s latest loss proves time is running out for Michael Carrick
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The chaos continues, and so will the scrutiny on Michael Carrick. In a match where Manchester United needed a win to stop the rot, a goal within 47 seconds and a red card for Leny Yoro set up a bruising loss to Atletico Madrid.

If the draw to Tottenham last week brought a sense of disbelief at full-time, this was a game that will leave many with a sense of hopelessness. United barely looked like they even believed they could turn it around, in what is a fitting metaphor for Carrick’s current situation.

Indeed, at the same venue where this season’s Champions League final will be held, United provided a reminder – not that any was needed – of exactly why they won’t be participating in club football’s biggest game in June.

open image in gallery Barrios opened the scoring in 47 seconds in the Spanish capital ( Getty )

United desperately needed to keep things tight at the back early on if they were to settle the nerves at a raucous Metropolitano, and yet they were behind within a minute.

The goal summed up the current circus, with far too much space behind the defence as Alex Baena raced clear. United never looked like they could deal with it, and their fears were confirmed as Pablo Barrios opened the scoring within 47 seconds.

It was the worst possible start but it felt oddly befitting of this current United side, who seem to produce a ridiculous moment (or performance) every week.

Conceding within a minute at one of the most difficult away grounds in Europe suggested that United would be in for a disastrous evening, though they did manage to wrestle back some momentum, with Bryan Mbeumo forcing a superb save from Jan Oblak.

open image in gallery Mbeumo went close twice with United’s best chances of the game ( PA )

United continued to threaten – with Mbeumo going close again and Carlos Baleba missing a free header at the back post – but it was the hosts who looked the most dangerous, with several well-worked attacks that led them into the United penalty area.

Thankfully for United, Atletico were lacking with the final ball on a few occasions. It could have been a nightmare otherwise, and indeed it almost was before Johnny Cardoso’s lovely curled effort was ruled out for handball in the build-up.

Even though United continued to look better in the second half, there was time for it to descend into chaos again. There always seems to be time for that.

With the visitors pressing for an equaliser, a poorly defended counter-attack led to Jonathan David racing clean through, with Yoro putting his arm across the Canadian. It looked fairly innocuous in real time, but referee Glenn Nyberg went to the monitor and produced a straight red for the Frenchman in the 74th minute.

open image in gallery Yoro was sent off for fouling David as the last man ( PA )

The visitors had threatened again after half-time – with Fernandes lifting an effort narrowly wide before hitting the top of the woodwork with an audacious effort – but the sending off effectively ended their chances of getting back into the game.

It had been a fairly even match until then too, with both sides having notable chances in the second half, but substitute Ademola Lookman wrapped up the result as he tapped in a rebound from close range.

And while it’s not a result that puts United’s European campaign in jeopardy, it’s another performance that raises questions around the manager.

Carrick made several changes to the side that laboured to that poor draw against Tottenham, with Fernandes playing on the right wing and Baleba making his first start, but while the change in personnel created a few notable chances, United were still far too open.

open image in gallery Ademola Lookman tapped in from close range to seal the result ( AP )

The ease with which the hosts cut through United – sometimes with the simplest of long balls directly over the defence – was a huge concern, and another sign that the current coaching set-up is out of ideas in terms of coaching defending and out of possession.

Everyone knows United need better defenders, but sometimes there’s not a lot you can do when the system leaves you so exposed. United are still overrun far too easily and far too often in midfield too (even though Baleba put in a great performance), and while some of the play in possession was improved on the night, the attack still relies far too much on individual quality and fortuitous counter-attacking.

All of this points to failures from Carrick and his coaching staff. Several players, including Baleba, Mbeumo and Ayden Heaven, put in solid performances, but it still wasn’t enough to make up for deficiencies in the set-up.

It is true that Carrick has been hung out to dry by those in charge of recruitment, with the sight of Joshua Zirkzee and the absence of Benjamin Sesko a reminder that the squad planning from Jason Wilcox and co. has been poor, as Lisandro Martinez pointed out in an explosive interview. Even the so-called ‘midfield rebuild’ feels ridiculous now, with the £50m signing of Andrey Santos particularly confusing in hindsight.

However, the man in the dugout could still get more from these players, as he showed in the second half of last season. United’s failure to replicate that form means that Carrick deserves to face questions, and unfortunately the approval he earned last term is quickly disappearing.

Hopes were high around the club at the start of the summer, but by autumn they have been extinguished. United are reeling, and with just two wins from their opening nine games of the season, someone will have to pay the price soon.

News.title: DNA ties a former Chicago detective to unsolved murder of 8-year-old girl
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The latest headlines from our reporters across the US sent straight to your inbox each weekday Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

Chicago police say DNA evidence has tied a former homicide detective to the decades-old murder of an 8-year-old girl who vanished while walking to church more than 65 years ago.

Gloria Kowalewicz was found shot dead in a ditch in 1960, just hours after disappearing.

Police say new technology allowed them to match a fingerprint and DNA from the crime scene to Thomas F. McInerney Jr., who joined the department in 1959 and later became a homicide detective working on violent crimes.

"McInerney should never have worn the CPD star, and it is devastating to accept that he was never identified and held accountable while he was alive," police said in a statement provided to The Associated Press on Tuesday.

The State's Attorney's Office in Cook County, where the murder took place, is "making efforts to identify cases that may have involved" McInerney, the office said in a statement emailed to The AP on Tuesday.

Gloria was walking a few blocks from her home to morning Mass on Nov. 12, 1960, but she never arrived, according to police.

Her body was found roughly four hours later, dumped in a forest preserve in southwest Chicago.

Chicago Cold Case ( Chicago Tribune )

Authorities formed a task force to investigate the killing.

They "knocked on hundreds of doors," interviewed more than 1,300 people, and questioned over a dozen individuals under polygraph, according to the statement.

Police collected and preserved a bullet, Gloria’s coat and shoes, and a white communion purse containing her prayer book.

Using modern forensic technology alongside assistance from the FBI and Illinois State Police, investigators matched DNA found on those items and a "carefully preserved" fingerprint lifted from the purse strap to McInerney.

The FBI said in a statement to The AP that it was "pursuing every investigative lead that may bring closure on other potential unsolved crimes that occurred during that time period in our area."

The technology used to identify McInerney allows law enforcement agencies to compare crime scene evidence with genetic profiles on genealogical websites. Previously used to identify the

Golden State Killer by matching DNA from a tissue found in a trash can, the technology has prompted privacy concerns.

McInerney retired from the police force in 1987, police said.

He subsequently worked for the Federal Public Defender's Office in Reno and Las Vegas until his retirement in 2004, according to a Chicago Tribune obituary.

He died in 2006.

News.title: Arsenal produce second-half blitz to sink Lille and continue perfect Champions League start
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Bukayo Saka came off the bench to help turn a frustrating evening into a rout as Arsenal beat Lille 3-0 at the Emirates Stadium.

The substitute scored the third of three Arsenal goals in a seven-minute burst after the hour mark, with Jurrien Timber and Eberechi Eze also finding the net.

The win was Arsenal's second from two matches in the Champions League this season, and their ninth in 10 across all competitions.

It was also the club's 14th consecutive victory in the group stage of the competition, as they chase the first Champions League title of their history after going one step less far last season.

Arsenal have not dropped points in the league phase for almost two years, since a 1-0 defeat to Inter Milan in November 2024.

For the first hour of Tuesday's contest under the lights, that streak looked in danger, with the French side frustrating their English counterparts.

open image in gallery Jurrien Timber opened the scoring ( PA Wire )

Bruno Guimaraes might have scored for the second game running, but side-footed wide after neat build-up play between Noni Madueke and Timber midway through the first half.

Mikel Merino then headed a Timber cross straight at Berke Ozer in the Lille goal.

The visitors believed they had gone ahead through Ayase Ueda in the 22nd minute, only for the offside flag to come to the home side's rescue.

Eze, handed a rare start, drew a save from Ozer as the hosts pushed for a breakthrough.

Guimaraes' deflected shot was scrambled away by Ozer on the stroke of half-time.

Arsenal kept pushing and probing after the interval, but the hour mark arrived without Lille's goal coming under threat.

Guimaraes wanted a penalty when he went down in the area after a collision with Alexsandro, but referee Felix Zwayer waved away his appeals and VAR did not intervene.

It was beginning to feel as though it could be one of those nights for the Gunners before Mikel Arteta's men, as they so often do these days, found a way.

open image in gallery Eberechi Eze was on the scoresheet in Arsenal’s win against Lille (John Walton/PA) ( PA Wire )

Madueke, in what would prove his final contribution, played in Timber, and the full-back's first touch was exquisite, allowing him to get away from Lille captain Benjamin Andre before chipping the on-rushing Ozer.

Timber's goal arrived shortly after the hour mark. Reinforcements then arrived from the bench, with Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz all introduced.

Saka was immediately involved in Arsenal's second, finding Guimaraes' pass in the right-hand channel before Eze cooly finished the substitute's cross three minutes after the opener.

Suddenly, Lille were on the ropes, and Saka delivered the knockout blow in the 71st minute when he combined with fellow substitute Havertz to score his fourth goal of the season.

Olivier Giroud, now 40, made his Emirates comeback in the final dozen minutes. Max Dowman, 24 years the Frenchman's junior, was also handed a late cameo.

Arsenal will face a sterner examination of their European credentials when they travel to Germany to face Bayern Munich a week on Wednesday.

For now, it is six points from six, without conceding, following an encouraging evening's work, with Nottingham Forest to follow this weekend.

News.title: Manchester United show signs of fighting spirit despite defeat by Atletico Madrid
News.content:
They seem to lack players who can play on the front foot, who have the athletic dynamism required in this league and too many self-indulgent forward players who either can’t be bothered to help out their team-mates or cannot concentrate long enough to do so. Spooked by their lack of pace in defence and midfield, they are hidebound by caution, dropping ever deeper, ever more reliant on counter-attacking despite the blatant disconnect between the front four and back six. If they drift through this match and Sunday’s trip to Elland Road, Carrick may join the long list of Ineos-driven managerial mis-steps.

Atlético have won six of eight in La Liga and have been defeated only once. They are five points behind Barcelona in second and have score 18 goals and let in eight, which may seem a curious thing to include in a preview but it is done to emphasise that many fans’ perception of Diego Simeone’s team are out of date. Back in the days of Diego Godín, Gabi, Juanfran et all, six wins a draw and a defeat would have had goals for of about 10 and goals against of maybe three.

Simeone is a martinet about attitude not systems or styles and his team have evolved, with the World Cup-winner Alex Baena, who has scored four goals so far, driving them on. He has reintegrated Julián Alvarez, too, after his brazen attempt to force a move to Barcelona so incensed Atléti fans that it seemed they would drive him out of the club. Simeone refused to let Alvarez get his own way and he is now buckling down. Ten years ago Simeone would have bitten his head off.

News.title: Arsenal’s big guns blow Lille away after the second string flop
News.content:
After signing his new Arsenal contract last week, Mikel Arteta described May’s Champions League final defeat as “poison in his veins,” and last season’s campaign demonstrated the benefits of finishing top of the league phase.

Arsenal enjoyed home second legs all the way through to the final after winning eight from eight, and in a 50:50 draw they fell into a considerably kinder bracket.

Sometimes it can be hard to gauge the importance of these league-phase matches, but Arteta will strive for another perfect record to give Arsenal the best possible chance of going deep in the competition again.

Fixtures against Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are likely to determine whether Arsenal finish in the top two, but there is still a job to be done against Lille this evening.

Arsenal have played against 10 different French opponents in European competition but have never faced Lille, who are managed by Davide Ancelotti, son of five-time Champions League winner Carlo.

Lille sell their best players every summer. After finishing third in Ligue 1 last season they lost Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Manchester City and Newcastle United for a combined £130m. They have claimed 10 points from their first five league games of the season and led Paris St-Germain 2-0 before being pegged back in stoppage time.

Leading the line for Lille is 40-year-old Olivier Giroud, who scored 105 Arsenal goals in 235 appearances between 2012 and 2018. After leaving the Emirates, Giroud went on to score against Arsenal for Chelsea in the 2019 Europa League final, but he can still expect a warm reception.

Arsenal’s home record in the Champions League has been formidable since they returned to the competition under Arteta in 2023. They have won all 11 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals (two of those were shipped against Kairat Almaty in a dead rubber).

Arteta’s scope for rotation has been reduced by injuries to Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi, but tonight’s game should offer Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres a chance to impress, while Jurrien Timber needs minutes to build his fitness.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it
News.content:
England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

News.title: Donkey prices in Gaza skyrocket from $1,000 to $30,000
News.content:
The price of a donkey in Gaza has jumped from about $1,000 before the war to $30,000 today, according to one of the embattled enclave’s most senior vets.

The surge in the value of the pack animals is due to the virtual elimination of motorised private transport in the strip and the emergence of a small group of black marketeers who have become hugely rich trading in intercepted aid.

The donkeys, whose number has been halved in the past three years, are also now in comparatively short supply.

“It’s a little bit crazy and people keep asking me ‘are you sure about that number?’”, Dr Ahmed Thabet, a Gazan veterinary surgeon told the Telegraph.

“They say ‘do you mean $3,000?’ but I tell them ‘no’. The average price of a donkey before the war was between $1,000 and $1,200. Recently it was $20,000 and last week I witnessed one that was sold for $30,000”.

News.title: The secret to the perfect holiday in Somerset
News.content:
Somerset’s landscapes are steeped in legend, from the lush fields of “Avalon” to Cheddar Gorge and the wilds of Exmoor. Its winding, country lanes lead to secrets and natural splendour. The local food scene is flourishing, too, involving everyone from Michelin-starred chefs to foragers on the Mendip Hills and farmers selling cheddar and cider from the barn door.

Glastonbury Festival shines as the centre of the musical universe in June – but the region is becoming known for much more than this. Quiet, agrarian villages are now fashionable places to spend time – I’m often found dawdling over a lazy brunch, browsing designer ceramics and paddleboarding down river. Bruton has an internationally renowned art gallery and the county’s hip, country house hotels – from Soho House-owned Babington House to The Newt – are some of the UK’s most desirable.

What makes Somerset so exciting is that it preserves a bucolic way of life while keeping its finger firmly on the pulse.

News.title: Painful Coventry defeat will send shudder of fear through Newcastle
News.content:
You can get a sense of what sort of mode a team are in within the first few passages of play and Newcastle were not sharp or precise. It was sloppy.

That was certainly true of goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who was off his line in no-man’s land trying to snuff out a through ball that he was not going to get. He stood up to deflect it away, but then rashly chased after it, diving at full stretch at the feet of Coventry’s Sidiki Cherif and failing to get the ball. Jack Rudoni coolly sent the Czech goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

Newcastle had been awful in their last away game at Leeds, another 4-1 thrashing, and there were many of the same faults on display.

It was not a good first half for Fernandez-Pardo up top. They are mystified in Belgium why he believes he is a centre-forward rather than a winger and he did not do himself any favours here. Newcastle’s best move of the game resulted in Lewis Miley playing in Jacob Murphy down the left. His cutback was perfect for Fernandez-Pardo to sweep home at the near post but instead of trying to make contact, he dummied it, thinking Harvey Barnes was better placed. He was not. It was a baffling piece of centre-forward play.

It had been the easiest 40 minutes Lampard’s side have had since they were promoted, but Newcastle still should have scored before the break.

Nico González spotted the run of Fernandez-Pardo through the middle. He wriggled clear of Bobby Thomas and sat down goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, but the Coventry centre-back got back to block his shot.

Newcastle pressed the self-destruct button early in the second half. A long throw into the box was half cleared. There was a half-hearted attempt to close Cherif down from Yoane Wissa and then a shot that somehow went through a crowd of three Newcastle defenders, including the legs of Botman, and nestled in the bottom corner.

News.title: AI cuts diagnosis for eye disease from 23 days to just 30 seconds
News.content:
Patients whose eye scans were read by an AI programme got results in 30 seconds, compared to facing an average waiting time of 23 days for results from a doctor, a study in Tanzania has shown.

Millions of people around the world have diabetic retinopathy, a condition where high blood sugar levels damage the tiny blood vessels in the retina.

It can lead to irreversible blindness if left untreated. Around a third of the 23 million people with diabetes in Africa have the complication.

In its early stages, diabetic retinopathy can have no symptoms, and the World Health Organization recommends that people living with diabetes undergo regular screening to check their eye health, so that they can be treated if necessary.

For the new study, published in the Lancet Global Health, researchers randomly assigned over 2,000 patients with diabetes visiting clinics in Tanzania’s Kilimanjaro and Arusha regions to either receive usual screening care, or to have a new type of AI-assisted screening.

Two fifths of the participants had changes in their eyes that needed referral to specialist care. In the half screened using AI, 36 per cent attended the central ophthalmology clinic within eight weeks, compared to 18 per cent in the standard care group.

Most of the people working in the regions where the study was based are farmers, said Dr Justus Rwiza of the Kilimanjaro Christian Medical Centre, co-author on the paper. “They depend on vision.”

The economic effects of blindness are felt by the whole family, he said, recalling how the daughter of one patient “had to stop schooling to help the mother”.

News.title: WHO probes ‘unanswered questions’ over Russian plague worker
News.content:
The World Health Organization has said it still does not have enough information to rule out a lab accident after the death of a worker in a Russian plague lab.

Last week reports emerged that Darya Shipilova, a lab worker in Irkutsk, Siberia, had died of pneumonic plague after dropping a test tube containing samples of the pathogen Yersinia pestis, which causes the disease.

Some 200 people were quarantined and there were reports of a further case. Shipilova was working at the Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East in Irkutsk.

Russian authorities have insisted that there was no lab accident and Shipilova’s mother, Svetlana, has also disputed that her daughter dropped a test tube.

“It’s impossible to break a test tube like that,” she said. “Even if you fling it at the wall. Only an amateur could say something like that,” she said.

Sports.title: ‘I expect more’ – Lisandro Martinez slams Man Utd board over transfers before Wayne Rooney accuses him of ‘disrepect’
Sports.content:
Next

LISANDRO MARTINEZ has slammed Manchester United technical director Jason Wilcox over the club’s transfer policy.

But former Red Devils captain Wayne Rooney reckons Martinez is being “disrespectful”.



Martinez, 28, was in action as United lost 2-0 at Atletico Madrid.

The Argentine said after the game: “Really poor. Really poor. I have to control myself a lot but sometimes is a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment.



“We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top, more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well. Atletico have an amazing team and they deserve to win today.

“I expect more [investment]. 100 per cent. I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox].

“I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night.”

Sports.title: Why did Arsenal wear black armbands against Lille?
Sports.content:
Next

ARSENAL secured a 3-0 win over Lille to maintain their perfect start in the Champions League.

After a slow first half, the Gunners sparked into life in the second period as Jurrien Timber, Eberechi Eze and Bukayo Saka scored three in seven minutes.



ARSENAL VS LILLE LIVE REACTION

Players wore black armbands during the clash as both sides paid tribute to Arsenal legend Ken Friar, who died today aged 92 earlier in the day.



Why did Arsenal wear black armbands against Lille?

Arsenal wore black armbands tonight to honour club legend Ken Friar, who died today aged 92.

Friar worked for the club for 70 years and became their life president in 2020 after retiring from his executive responsibilities.



His first role was with the club’s box office in 1950, before he was appointed Arsenal’s secretary in 1973.

Friar’s greatest legacy is the part he played in the Gunners’ move from Highbury to Emirates Stadium at the turn of the century.

After 23 years as Arsenal’s managing director, Friar changed roles in 2000 to oversee the stadium project.

He worked alongside his friend and fellow director, Danny Fiszman, and the club moved into the Emirates six years later.



Friar was awarded an OBE in 2000 for his services to association football and also received the Freedom of the Borough of Islington.

Despite stepping down from the board in 2020, Friar would still attend Arsenal games and the club remained close to his heart.

Affectionately known by those at Arsenal as ‘Mr Friar’, he was a part-time box office runner four years prior to officially starting work with the club in 1950.



Born in Islington, Friar used to play football outside of the old Highbury stadium as a youngster.

An Arsenal statement said: “It is with profound sadness that we announce the death of Life President Ken Friar OBE.

“Since our formation in 1886, there have been many inspirational individuals who have driven our club forward, but no one has had an influence on Arsenal Football Club quite like ‘Mr Friar’ and he leaves an extraordinary life of service to the club as his legacy.

“One that will surely never be matched.

“Rest in peace.”



Arsenal also announced further commemorations and tributes against Everton on Saturday, October 24.

Sports.title: Man Utd player ratings: Marcus Rashford fails to track back but Carlos Baleba shows his worth again
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED wasted a host of chances in their 2-0 defeat against Atletico Madrid.

Leny Yoro was sent off with 16 minutes left before Ademola Lookman doubled the hosts lead following Pablo Barrios’ opener inside the first 49 seconds.



Despite the result, United improved on their recent shambles, missing tons of chances against Diego Simeone’s fine-tuned Champions League stars.

But under-fire Michael Carrick needs this improved performance to start turning into results – after United suffered four defeats and just two wins in their opening nine matches across all comps.



Here’s how SunSport’s Katherine Walsh rated and slated the United players.

Senne Lammens – 5

Looks bereft of confidence and a cloud is starting to form over the Belgian, who is appearing more shaky by the game.

Undone by poor defending in behind, as well as an outrageous strike from Cardoso, whose stunner was chalked off for handball and two chances smacked his woodwork.

His push out to Jonathan David’s initial shot for Lookman’s rebound was not becoming of an elite stopper.

Diogo Dalot – 4

A mess when he was caught sleeping to Alex Baena straight after kick-off.

The hosts carved through United like butter for their opener and Dalot was nowhere to be found as the ball was passed over the top of the Portuguese. Training ground stuff.



Leny Yoro – 6

The Frenchman was solid before the first red of his career. Spoiler alert – United don’t thrive as 10 versus 11.

It was soft and not a clear and obvious mistake, but he left the ref with a decision to be made at the monitor. Before that incident, his handling of Julian Alvarez suggested he bounced back from poor start to the season

Lisandro Martinez – 6

Another game, another back line for Martinez and United. His distribution was back but he was still shaky at the back once the ball was in behind, even as the senior defender alongside two 20 year olds.

Ayden Heaven – 6

In his first senior match at left back, the England youth star worked hard to redeem himself after Barrios’ strike haphazardly bounced under him before trickling into the net.

Though highly promising, he needs to choose his runs more adeptly, failing to follow Alejandro Grimaldo‘s fast dash into the box for the opener.



Andrey Santos – 6

The £50m failed to stake his claim in his first minutes since the Brighton League Cup debacle. A few sloppy challenges saw Atleti break away on several occasions.

Has a hospital pass in him and his cock up led to Yoro’s foul for the red card. Carrick should have subbed the Brazilian ahead of his midfield partner.

Carlos Baleba – 7

The £70m signing stood up to the daunting occasion on his first club start and Champions League debut.

The deep-lying midfielder was on hand to pick pockets and cover ground, but missed a free header inside 24 minutes.

Bruno Fernandes – 5

Fernandes is out of sorts. The skipper is carrying an injury, but his body language is becoming more worrying.



He appears either exhausted or plagued with troubles. Maybe it is both. His quality on the ball was not there as he was shunted to the right wing. His threat improved after half-time, hitting the crossbar from range and edging another half volley inches wide.

An inquest will surely be needed into how news leaked that United’s talisman would be moved out right six hours before kick-off.

Youri Tielemans – 6

Tielemans has caught plenty of flack for his pace and lack of intensity at the start of his Old Trafford career.

But Tielemans was more at ease at the No10 in Spain. The midfield was more compact around him and he could move the ball in pockets in attacking areas.

Marcus Rashford – 5

After a rest against Tottenham, Rashford offered lively forward runs in the first half, but did not match it with defensive tracking.



The England man, who crashed out of the quarter-finals at the Metropolitano with Barcelona last season, was booked after the restart and soon replaced.

Bryan Mbeumo – 6

Back through the middle, the Cameroonian did well to get touch out of his feet to have a shot just go wide. But he should have taken his two clear chances better.

Often too casual on the ball, causing shaky ground around him.

SUBS

Mason Mount (Baleba, 64) – 6

Worked hard.

Amad (Rashford, 64) – 5

Limited impact.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Joshua Zirkzee (Tielemans, 64) – 5

Anonymous.

Matheus Cunha (Fernandes, 80) – 6

Harry Maguire (Heaven, 80) – 5

Subs not used: Karl Darlow, Dermot Mee, Matthijs De Ligt, Dan Armer, Harry Amass, Tyler Fletcher, Shea Lacey

Sports.title: Andy Burnham accused of covering up Man City links after Sun probe finds he had two freebie dinners with club chairman
Sports.content:
Next

PM ANDY Burnham was accused of covering up his links to scandal-hit Manchester City after a Sun probe rubbished his claims he had only one “significant” meeting with its chairman.

A deleted register of interests revealed that while Manchester’s mayor, he twice joined Khaldoon Al Mubarak at a luxury hospitality suite in the Etihad Stadium.



The revelation uncovered by a Sun investigation comes days after the PM vowed to be transparent over his relationship with the club which has been found guilty by an independent panel of more than 100 Premier League rule breaches.

In all he accepted City-funded freebies worth almost £1,200.



These were logged on a register he signed on December 7 2020, but it was removed from the Greater Manchester Combined Authority’s website.

Last night there were claims that Mr Burnham had misled the public about the extent of his dealings with City bosses.



Reform MP Robert Jenrick said: “This whole saga stinks.

“Burnham appears to have lied about his extensive links to Manchester City’s owners. No wonder he was so desperate to leap to their defence. Fans deserve better than a Prime Minister compromised by this scandal.”

Shadow Sports Minister Louie French added: “This is far from the full transparency that football fans deserve.

“We have been given precious little information about these meetings, what was discussed and what may have been agreed.



“If Burnham has nothing to hide, why is he so tight-lipped?”

Mr Burnham had to backtrack after saying he would be “really concerned to lose” City’s Abu Dhabi owners.

Sources in the United Arab Emirates had previously indicated that a particularly harsh City punishment could scupper £30billion of investment.



On Monday, the PM told the House of Commons that all his dealings with City’s owners would be published.

Hours later, the GMCA released a statement on his behalf claiming he had been a guest at City home games “on a small number of occasions”.

The authority admitted he had met Mr Al Mubarak “informally in the stands” at ex-captain Vincent Kompany’s testimonial in September 2019.

But it said there had been only one “formal meeting” between the pair, at a government-organised investment summit in October 2021.

Neither pre-match dinner was mentioned even though they were declared in council paperwork at the time.



On Sunday, Mr Burnham told The Rest Is Politics podcast: “I will quite clearly put out there everything that I have done working with them in my previous role as Mayor of Greater Manchester.

“None of it is recent, actually, in terms of the meetings I had. I only had one significant meeting, actually, and that was in 2021.”

Yet in August 2017, the then-mayor dined with Manchester City Council leader Sir Richard Leese and Mr Al Mubarak when the club played his beloved Everton.



The hospitality was declared on his register of interests, valued at £338, and reported as provided by “Manchester City Football Club”.

In April 2018, Mr Burnham was wined and dined by the chairman again at the Manchester derby. The meal and seat were valued at £699.

A month after the derby, the club handed Mr Burnham two tickets worth £150 to see Ed Sheeran perform at the Etihad.

In 2019, Mr Burnham was pictured arriving at a charity dinner organised by Kompany at Manchester’s Hilton Hotel, where City fan Noel Gallagher took the stage.

Freebies from Mr Burnham’s second term as Mayor of Greater Manchester remain accessible online, but those from his first stint have been taken down.



‘Andy was detached from Utd’ By Samuel Luckhurst, Man United correspondent ANDY Burnham showed his true colours when he attended a ­testimonial dinner for Manchester City captain Vincent Kompany in February 2019. The PM, a lifelong supporter of the royal blue of Everton, rubbed shoulders with players and their then boss Pep Guardiola in City’s domestic treble-winning season. Guardiola was accompanied by his wife at the Beetham Tower on Deansgate. Almost every City star was also there. Oasis star Noel Gallagher performed a set. Bez and Rowetta from the Happy Mondays rocked up. So did Ricky Hatton. Mr Burnham, in keeping with the occasion’s “Manchesterism”, arrived in a North Face anorak and kept it on while interviewed. The dinner, held at the tower’s Hilton Hotel, was to combat homelessness in the city through the Tackle4MCR initiative. Mr Burnham, the then mayor of Manchester, said in a speech: “We want this to be a place that catches people when they fall.” Nearly £250,000 was raised at the dinner. A testimonial match for former captain Kompany in September 2019 boosted Tackle4MCR’s funds even further. It was at that Etihad game that Mr Burnham was photographed cosying up to the City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak. The Hilton dinner featured in an episode of the four-part BBC documentary series Manctopia: Billion Pound Property Boom. Earlier this year, Mr Burnham bragged Manchester was “the fastest-growing city in the UK”. Until Sir Jim Ratcliffe returned to his home town with the intention of building a new 100,000-seater stadium for Manchester United, Mr Burnham was seen as attached to City and detached from United.

The details of his two dinners were uncovered in a PDF submitted and signed by Mr Burnham in line with local authority rules in December 2020.

The Sun was able to track down an archived version.

Two months after the 2017 dinner, the GMCA approved a £24.5million loan to Manchester Life, a joint property venture between the city council and club owners the Abu Dhabi United Group. Sir Richard Leese was on the board.

He is now an honorary president of the club after stepping down as council leader in December 2021.

Three Manchester Life companies controlled by ADUG owner Sheikh Mansour received around £55.7million from the authority.



Manchester Life says the loans were repaid in full with interest.

GMCA sources said all gifts had been declared at the time in line with its rules.

Mr Al Mubarak met Mr Burnham’s Trade Secretary Jonathan Reynolds inside No10 in September, a fortnight before the rule breach verdicts became public.

Last week The Sun revealed Labour politicians have pocketed nearly £300,000 in freebies from the UAE and Man City.

We also revealed Mr Burnham joined City’s delegation at the opening of the club’s second office in China in 2018.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Manchester City have repeatedly denied any wrongdoing and are appealing the panel’s findings.

No10 declined to comment.

Sports.title: Arsenal player ratings: Eze and Saka take game away from Ligue 1 side but Gyokeres struggles again
Sports.content:
EZE DOES IT Arsenal player ratings: Eze and Saka take game away from Ligue 1 side but Gyokeres struggles again







Next

ARSENAL turned on the style in the second half to cruise their way to three points with a 3-0 victory over Lille.

The Gunners struggled to find the spark in the first half before hitting their rhythm in the second spell and blowing the visitors away.



Jurrien Timber opened the scoring with a brilliantly taken goal, before Mikel Arteta changed the game with his substitutions.

The Arsenal chief brought on Bukayo Saka, Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard to unleash more star power on Lille.



Saka was involved straight away, setting up Eze for Arsenal‘s second, before netting himself just a few minutes later.

Here’s how SunSport Arsenal Reporter Joshua Hall rated each individual Arsenal performance…

DAVID RAYA – 6

The Spaniard was inches away from gifting a goal to Lille when he rolled the ball out of his box and straight into the path of Ayase Ueda.

An uncharacteristic mistake that was glossed over by his clean sheet.

JURRIEN TIMBER – 9

A brilliant performance from the Dutchman.

Hit touch and chipped finish for Arsenal’s opener was simply sublime, and the type of quality the Gunners had been missing.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And it was him that won the ball back to start the move for Eberechi Eze’s goal a few moments later.

Arteta will be over the moon that his right-back is looking back to his best after a lenghty spell struggling with injury.

EZRI KONSA – 7

Another good showing from the England international, who has taken absolutely no time to settle in next to Gabriel.

So calm when dealing with counter attacks and shows immense strength in every duel.



GABRIEL MAGALHAES – 7

A typically solid showing from the Brazilian, who rarely puts a foot wrong.

Always putting his body on the line to get in the way of pop shots and efforts from distance.

MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY – 7

Back at left-back following the injury to Piero Hincapie in the warm-down from Saturday’s win over Leeds.

His versatility is invaluable to Arteta and this performance showed he can slot back into defence with ease when needed.



DECLAN RICE – 7

Part of both the attacking and defensive sides of Arsenal’s game.

He rescued Raya with a crucial toe on the ball to prevent Ueda a certain goal in the first half.

The midfielder was always bursting forward to help with attacking phases too and put in yet another top performance.

BRUNO GUIMARAES – 7

Missed a golden opportunity inside 20 minutes when he blazed wide from inside the area.



But made up for it with an all-round performance that included line-splitting passes and some abitious efforts on goal.

MIKEL MERINO – 5

A third start for the Spaniard who was in electric form for his country during the international break.

Had little impact in attacking midfield compared to Martin Odegaard and picked up a silly yellow card for a frustrated tackle when things weren’t going his way.

NONI MADUEKE – 5

Back on his preferred right flank after a promising display on the left against Leeds at the weekend.

Within five minutes he had fallen over the ball and played a pass directly out of play.



That set the tone for his night which was another frustrating performance littered with overhit crosses and botched final balls.

EBERECHI EZE – 8

The only one of Arsenal’s starting forwards to impress.

As well as some nice moves in the first half, Eze took his second-half goal like a seasoned striker.



Arteta opted against using him at left wing at the weekend, but might be tempted to select him over Madueke against Nottingham Forest off the back of this showing.

VIKTOR GYOKERES – 4

A rare start for the Swede, who has been starved of minutes by Arteta this season despite his goalscoring exploits on international duty.

But he did nothing to help his case for a starting spot.

Gyokeres has become a frustrating watch and feels like he is disconnected from the rest of the team when he is on the pitch.



SUBSTITUTES

KAI HAVERTZ (for Gyokeres, 65 mins) – 7

A vast improvement on Gyokeres when he came on, notching an assist just six minutes after coming on.

BUKAYO SAKA (for Madueke, 65 mins) – 8

An instant impact off the bench, sliding a pass into the box to find Eze for Arsenal’s second before finding the net himself a few moments later.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Saka changed the game when he came on and has yet again silenced critics who came after him following his performance against Leeds.

MARTIN ODEGAARD (for Merino, 65 mins) – 7

His dancing feet caused Lille problems from the moment he came on the pitch, and made Merino’s performance look even more damning.



BEN WHITE (for Timber, 78 mins) – N/A

MAX DOWMAN (for Eze, 85mins) – N/A

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney slams Cristiano Ronaldo over Portugal fallout and says former Man Utd teammate’s behaviour ‘just so wrong’
Sports.content:
Next

WAYNE ROONEY blasted former team-mate Cristiano Ronaldo’s Portugal outburst as “so wrong.”

The Real Madrid legend left his national side’s camp in the middle of the international break after being an unused substitute against Norway in the Nation’s League.



He then released a lengthy statement explaining the situation in which he revealed that he gave manager Jorge Jesus a list of comments to say during a press conference to clear the air.

Rooney did not hold back on the bizarre conduct while appearing on Stick to United.



He explained: “My thoughts on Ronaldo were – ‘why?’

“He’s such a great player, and I think when you see it was the same day Messi was retiring from Argentina, for him to come out of that Portugal squad that way, and then put that statement out… it’s just wrong in every sense.



“To undermine your manager, undermine your team-mates, it was just so wrong. To undermine the Portuguese FA!

“Everything about it was just wrong, from a football point of view, being a team-mate and being a manager, it wasn’t nice to see.”

Rooney attributed at least some of the 41-year-old’s outburst to his struggle to adapt to a new stage of his career.

He is no longer the electric forward of his Real or Juventus days, and is not Portugal‘s most important player compared to the likes of Vitinha and Bruno Fernandes, who are in their prime.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Rooney continued: “You know what’s a shame? It comes to every player. You have to finish international football, you have to finish football.

“Unfortunately he’s not dealing with it well, and it’s getting uncomfortable to see.”

Rooney, 40, was especially shocked at his demands of the manager, which included an eight-point list of statements he wanted the manager to tell the press.

He added: “You can’t tell the manager what he’s got to say in a press conference. That just goes beyond anything I’ve ever seen.

“This is part of his strength as well, I don’t think he listens to anyone, he’s doing what he is doing.”

Sports.title: Atletico Madrid 2 Man Utd 0: Michael Carrick left clinging to job with 10-man Red Devils now FIVE games without a win
Sports.content:
Next

ATLETICO MADRID unfurled a banner pre-match that said “defend what we love”. Manchester United struggled to defend.

This was not a disgraceful effort from United and perhaps not as bad as their 3,750 supporters in the upper tier of the Wanda Metropolitano had braced themselves for, particularly as United were level for all of 50 seconds.



United had their chances and hit the woodwork. They were also reduced to ten men for the final 15 minutes after VAR deemed that Leny Yoro had upended Jonathan David for a deliberate denial of a goalscoring opportunity.

Michael Carrick’s side went down with a fight but he has a fight on his hands to continue beyond this month. It is now five games without a win, United’s longest winless sequence since January 2025.



Their fourth defeat from nine games this term came with Sir Jim Ratcliffe present. The ‘Jim Reaper’ has been to three United European away games and they have not won any of them.

Atletico’s stadium will host the Champions League final for the second time in June. Any optimistic United supporter who has booked a refundable hotel may be requesting their money back now.

Carrick resorted to drastic measures amid United’s spiral. Bruno Fernandes, a liability in recent weeks, shifted to the right and Youri Tielemans moved further forward, with Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos paired together for the first time.

The obvious ploy was a more compact set-up to plug the gaps that Tottenham exposed so damningly. Atletico were quicker off the mark.



Atletico are a quality enough side to command such respect but this was Fernandes’ first stint on the right-hand side since October 2023. His relocation raises questions about whether he compromises how the team functions, never mind whether a new contract should be forthcoming.

On one occasion that Fernandes miscontrolled the ball, he briefly stopped running. His whining can grate yet Fernandes’ body language is wholly negative and he did not appear to relish his change of position.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Ayden Heaven, whose two previous starts this season ended in defeat, started at left back for the first time in his nascent career. It showed throughout.

The chopping and changing kept United level for less than a minute. Diogo Dalot and Leny Yoro left a gap a London bus could have driven through for Alex Baena, who turned and coolly laid the ball off for Pablo Barrios. His side-footer squirmed off the sliding Heaven and trickled over the line.

Carrick’s head dropped. He turned around and trudged back to the dugout to watch a replay of the damage.



The United away-dayers still made themselves heard and the players did not capitulate, as Tottenham did at the Wanda Metropolitano last season.

United came close to equalising as early as the 14th minute as Tielemans’ stint as a No10 almost paid dividends. He received the ball from Leny Yoro, played a prompt pass to Bryan Mbeumo, who isolated David Hancko, danced past him but Jan Oblak gloved the placed effort past the post.

United received more encouragement in the 15th minute from a lofted Lisandro Martinez pass that Marcus Rashford ought to have trapped for a one-on-one.



Mbeumo and Tielemans combined again for a swift one-two after Cristian Romero’s lax pass was intercepted by Carlos Baleba. The imposing Oblak advanced and blocked the Cameroonian’s effort.

Alejandro Grimaldo’s whipped free kick that clipped the woodwork in the 27th minute and frustration got the better of Diego Simeone ten minutes later. He was booked for demanding that Andrey Santos be carded.

United were let off the hook by a VAR review in added time of the first half. Marcos Llorente barged past the flimsy Heaven yet the ball bounced off his arm before it was swept in by Johnny Cardoso.

Carrick slapped his hand repeatedly as referee Glenn Nyberg scrutinised the pitchside monitor and signalled handball. Carrick got his way. No goal.

Uefa deemed that Llorente’s right hand was “in an unnatural position and away from the body”. The handball continues to leave viewers scratching their heads.



Frustration got the better of Rashford, who did track back to scythe down Giuliano Simeone right under his father’s nose in the 51st minute. Rashford apologised.

Rashford, recalled at the expense of Matheus Cunha, did not provide Heaven with much protection. He continues to be found wanting in his own third amid a reluctance to muck in with defensive duties.

Julian Alvarez, whistled on his first start on home turf after failing to engineer a transfer to Barcelona, connected cleanly with Baena’s visionary pass yet his 55th-minute volley smacked the post.



Fernandes’ chance arrived in the 56th minute when the industrious Tielemans’ raking pass bounced into his path and Oblak was caught in no man’s land. Fernandes could only prod the ball wide.

Carrick still did not have the nerve to hook Fernandes. Tielemans, United’s most creative player, made way instead on 66 minutes.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Suddenly, there was a shift in Fernandes’ body language. Redeployed as the No10, soon pinged the crossbar with an overhit cross in the 71st minute.

Any resistance effectively ended with Yoro’s debatable red card by VAR. As Harry Maguire and Matheus Cunha waited to come on, Ademola Lookman tapped in on 79 minutes after Senne Lammens’ fumbled David’s shot.

Sports.title: Arsenal 3 Lille 0: Timber, Eze and Saka net as Gunners breeze past Giroud and co with seven-minute blitz
Sports.content:
Next

EBERECHI EZE sparked his season into life as Arsenal cruised past Lille.

The England star has had a difficult start to the campaign and this was only his third start.



Chances have been hard to come by for Eze – but he grabbed this one to give Mikel Arteta a headache ahead of Sunday’s trip to Nottingham Forest.

Arsenal are light on left-wing options right now because Christos Tzolis has a hamstring injury.



Eze’s first goal of the season in this win should give him confidence to make the spot his own – and it was part of a second-half blitz from the Gunners.

After a turgid opening 45 minutes, Mikel Arteta’s side clicked into gear after the break.

READ MORE ON FOOTBALL Welcome player Join Sun Vegas now and claim a 100% deposit match bonus and 100 free spins



Jurrien Timber opened the scoring, before Eze and Bukayo Saka also found the net in the space of seven minutes.

The win maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to this season’s Champions League and extended their remarkable record in the competition.

The Gunners have now not dropped points in Europe’s top competition since a loss at Inter Milan in November 2024.

Arteta will have been a bit worried that the record could end last night, as Arsenal were slow to get going.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

That could be put down to the five changes Arteta made to the team that beat Leeds last weekend.

The attack, in particular, looked very different because big guns Saka and Martin Odegaard were on the bench.

Viktor Gyokeres led the forward line – starting for just the third time this season – with Eze on the left and Mikel Merino as the No10.

Noni Madueke was the only attacker to keep his place from the win over Leeds, and even his role was altered as he swapped wings.

Lille also showed they would be no pushovers, and why they are second in the French top-flight this season.



Head coach Davide Ancelotti – son of legendary manager Carlo – has made them hard to beat and they have shipped just four goals in six leagues since he was hired in the summer.

Arsenal should have been ahead after 20 minutes, though, when Jurrien Timber’s cut-back picked out Bruno Guimaraes.

The Brazilian, who was rewarded with a start after scoring the winner against Leeds, somehow fired wide when the goal was gaping.]



The right flank looked like Arsenal’s best way of breaking Lille down and, shortly after Guimaraes’ miss, Merino wasted another Timber cross with a tame header.

It was all part of a frantic three minutes, with Lille striker Ayase Ueda having a goal ruled out as he was offside from former Tottenham midfielder Nabil Bentaleb’s deflected strike.

Arsenal continued to push on, but their play was like a polite knock on the door instead of hammering it down.

The frustration only grew after the break and the Gunners’ desperation increased.



Guimaraes typified the feeling of everyone in the Emirates, throwing himself to the ground and trying to win a penalty off the outstretched leg of Lille defender Alexsandro.

It was enough for Arteta to call for the cavalry on the hour mark, bringing on Kai Havertz, Odegaard and Saka.

But just as they were preparing to come on, Timber broke the deadlock.

Arsenal’s right flank had been their biggest threat all night and the

Dutchman combined with Madueke to score. It was a lovely chipped finish, too, which came after a silky first touch.



That released the tension in the Emirates as the Gunners finally played with freedom.

Three minutes after Timber struck, Eze was in on the act as he smashed home Saka’s cross.



Saka completed the second-half surge moments later, combining with fellow subs Havertz and Odegaard to kill the game. past goalkeeper Berke Ozer.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Arsenal then doubled the lead just two minutes later through Eberechi Eze.

The hosts were rampant as Bukayo Saka made it 3-0 in the 70th minute after linking up with Kai Havertz.

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Four punishments named as Premier League execs send texts
Sports.content:
Manchester City have appealed after being found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules and await a decision over the sanctions they face

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's Manchester City Premier League charges live blog.

An independent commission found City broke Premier League regulations relating to the provision of accurate financial information between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

City, who won 3-0 against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, have maintained their innocence and appealed against the commission’s findings.

But the fallout from that result and City leading the Premier League table has seen a great deal of frustration over the club's punishment still being unknown.

Speaking on Sunday, Gary Neville admitted he wants to be removed from all of Sky Sports’ City games for the next few months.

Sports.title: Kate Scott ruins Micah Richards live on TV over Man City 114 charges verdict
Sports.content:
Kate Scott ruins Micah Richards live on TV over Man City 114 charges verdict

CBS host Kate Scott couldn't resist a cheeky swipe at Micah Richards following Manchester City's guilty verdict

View 2 Images Micah Richards had no response to Kate Scott's cheeky swipe. (Image: CBS Sports)

Kate Scott took a cheeky swipe at Micah Richards when introducing the panel for CBS Sports' coverage of Champions League games. The former Man City defender has come under fire for his allegiance to the club, where he won a Premier League title and an FA Cup, following their guilty verdict.

‌



‌



Scott, who hosts the CBS Sports coverage of the Champions League, has a brilliant rapport with her colleagues, Thierry Henry, Jamie Carragher and Richards. However, it was Richards who found himself on the receiving end of the banter on Tuesday night - and was left hanging his head in defeat as Carragher and Henry burst out laughing.

‌



At the start of the show, Scott introduced the panel and said: "Welcome along to London, everybody, so good to have you with us. I'm Kate Scott, joined by a man who has won it all.

‌



"The World Cup, the Euros, the Champions League, the Premier League and La Liga, Thierry Henry. Next to him, a Champions League winner, also won what was the UEFA Cup, now the Europa League.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"He won the FA Cup and League Cup too, Jamie Carragher. And then, this is awkward isn't it? He already has less accolades on set than anybody else on set.

‌



"For now, he is still a Premier League winner and FA Cup winner before he has to mail those medals to somebody at Stoke or Manchester United. Big Meeks, Michah Richards."

View 2 Images Kate Scott took a cheeky swipe at Micah Richards and the Man City charges on CBS Sport tonight. (Image: CBS Sport)

Arsenal legend Henry could not believe what he was hearing, saying 'wow' three times during the brutal put-down, while Carragher could not hold back his laughter.

‌



Richards did not respond to the jibe, stooping his head and staring at the table before rearranging his pen and his phone.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Richards has already cut an emotional figure on our TV screens, saying he was devastated after hearing his former club had been found guilty of all 114 financial rule breaches.

‌



He told Sky Sports: “In terms of Man City, it'll galvanise the players. We've all been in dressing rooms where there is outside noise, you all come together.

“I feel devastated, really, for the fans. Coming through the Man City academy all the way to the first-team, winning trophies, for all that to be in question now is very confusing.

“You've got two sides, one saying there's charges [of guilt], the other saying there is irrefutable evidence [of innocence]. It just leaves me [as a former player] and fans so devastated.

‌



“I feel let down by the fact that it's dragged on for so long. Make it easier for the fans. Us as players, what we can do?

“I'd do anything for this club, but my integrity is being questioned. I'm in a difficult position. I’ve given everything for this club, I've literally got one knee… because of this club.”

City have appealed the independent Commission's decision and continue to maintain their innocence.

Sports.content:
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola responds to Bradley Barcola and Florian Wirtz criticism

Both Bradley Barcola and Florian Wirtz have endured slow starts to life with Liverpool but Reds head coach Andoni Iraola fully believes in the pair ahead of their Champions League clash with LASK

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola has spoken ahead of Liverpool's Champions League clash with LASK (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola says he trusts Bradley Barcola and Florian Wirtz “100 per cent” despite their difficult starts to the season. German midfielder Wirtz endured a tricky debut campaign at Anfield following his big-money switch from Bayer Leverkusen and is yet to find the net this term.

‌



‌



French winger Bradley Barcola is also waiting to get off the mark for his new club, having joined in a record-breaking switch from Paris Saint-Germain.

‌



But boss Iraola is sure that the pair will reach their potential with time. Speaking ahead of his side’s Champions League clash with Austrian side LASK, he said: "We need other players to give us those numbers.

‌



“We trust the players we have now to play in those positions. These injuries have been because of the international break and it will happen to other teams. It is a matter of adapting to these circumstances.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"With Bradley and Flo, they have had good games and bad games this season like everyone else. We know their level and we know they will give us good performances."

He added: "The possibilities are the same. The other day (against Manchester City), if Lewis Koumas scores the goal that he connects with really well, then it is one assist for Bradley Barcola.

"His performance is exactly the same but we will all say 'oof, he played really well with an assist'. Sometimes we focus only on the numbers.

‌



"With Bradley, the other day, he had good situations and we did not finish them. Bradley and Flo are players that I trust 100%."

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola has not yet found the net for Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

On Wirtz specifically, Iraola has warned the German international that he might need to get used to more severe criticism at Anfield. But he has also suggested that Wirtz will only show his true form when Liverpool are a more cohesive unit.

Article continues below

He said: “When you are at a big club like we are, when you don't have a good performance everyone starts looking for answers. The other day, he probably didn’t have his best game but he has had good games with us this season.

"He had some good performances in the national team - he scored one goal and he will have better or worse games but I would like to look at it more collectively and more how they help us play well and get results, and after I don’t care which one scores. I think it’s a more collective thing."

Sports.title: Football regulator David Kogan says he will QUIT if Andy Burnham interferes in Man City case
Sports.content:
Football regulator David Kogan says he will quit if there is any Government interference in the Manchester City case.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham caused shockwaves after admitting he would be “really concerned” if the City owners decided to sell up after the club was found guilty of breaching Premier League spending rules.

Burnham, formerly the Mayor of Greater Manchester, has revealed he had a meeting with City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and the Abu Dhabi ownership has pumped millions into regenerating the area.

That has led to warnings that the United Arab Emirates could halt investment into the United Kingdom depending on the severity of City’s punishment.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The new Independent Football Regulator has the ultimate power of stripping ownership from clubs. City are appealing the verdict but could face a huge points deduction or even being expelled from the Premier League.

IFR chair Kogan said: “Let me be really, really clear about this. You’ll be aware that the original legislation brought in by the Conservative Government had in it a reference which we have to take some regard of some British trade relationships. That was removed from the legislation.

‌



“Actually this was specifically discussed when it was going through Parliament so we are absolutely bound by one thing and that one thing is regulating football and regulating football clubs.

View 3 Images International Football Regulator David Kogan

“Considerations beyond that are beyond our view and are not going to be part of any decision that we make about any outcome of any club that we regulate.

“Our independence is absolute and my independence personally is absolute. I made it very clear last year that if have any form of Government interference on the way we operate is going to result in me resigning from this role and I stand by that completely.

‌



“I should say, to be crystal clear, we’ve come under absolutely no political pressure on this or any other topic and I don’t expect to in the future. Ministers know full well that we are going to act completely independently.”

City have lodged an appeal but there is no exact time scale when the final verdict will be delivered by a new independent panel. The sanctions can be dished out even before the appeal is completed.

They have been found guilty of creating “sham” contracts to over inflate commercial contracts to give them greater spending power over their Premier League rivals. It has caused a huge backlash from other clubs who are demanding strong action.

View 3 Images Man City won three league titles during the affected period (Image: Getty)

‌



The new regulator has power to force a sale of a club if there has been criminal activity or they deem the ownership to be unsuitable.

If it is proved City’s ownership have been complicit in false accounting the IFR could strip them of the club. The IFR’s new powers mean every club will have to apply for a licence with that process starting from next month.

City’s licence will not be in doubt while the appeal process goes on but that could change if the appeal fails.

Kogan added: “We have powers within the legislation which allow us to review the owners and directors and also senior executives and also whether those owners are fit and proper people to run clubs going forward.

‌



“What we would do in that particular instance - we would already be across any accusations against that club and therefore we would be having a view of whether a licence could be awarded.

“We haven’t had that prospect yet because we don’t start licensing clubs until November but we will be looking at the criteria that we have put forward in the presentation as well as any other circumstances that may affect them.

“But let’s be clear, there’s an appeal process going on and we don’t know what the outcome of that appeal process might be so we can’t make any precipitation judgements on any individual case at this stage.

‌



“The process is currently going through an appeal process and until we know the outcome of the appeal because it’s possible that Manchester City would argue - and this is what they’ve said right the way through - that they’ve got clear right on their side. That has to be tested by the new independent commission.”

Sports.title: Michael Carrick 'wants out' at Man Utd as replacement verdict lands
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick 'wants out' at Man Utd as replacement verdict lands

Michael Carrick has struggled to get Manchester United firing this season, with the Reds currently 13th in the Premier League after just six games

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is under pressure with Manchester United (Image: Alex Livesey, Getty Images)

Paul Scholes has questioned whether Michael Carrick "wants out" of Manchester United, following a difficult start to the new Premier League season. The 45-year-old only secured a permanent deal at Old Trafford this summer, having made a strong impression during an initial interim spell between January and May.

‌



‌



Yet any momentum Carrick appeared to have built towards the tail end of last season seems to have evaporated in the early stages of 2026/27. United currently sit 13th in the Premier League table after six matches, with just one win to their name.

‌



As a result, serious questions are beginning to surface regarding Carrick's position at the club, particularly given the Red Devils' well-documented history of relieving managers of their duties mid-season. To put it into context, Erik ten Hag was dispatched in October 2024, while his replacement Ruben Amorim was shown the door at the start of 2026.

‌



Jamie Carragher learns bankruptcy fate as HMRC issue update on his petition READ MORE :

Michael Carrick's worrying comment about Man Utd job emerges as sack threat clear READ MORE :

While the broad expectation is that the club will give Carrick more time in the dugout before taking any drastic action, the board will demand a marked improvement in results over the coming weeks, with October and early November shaping up to be a potentially pivotal period in United's season.

Against that backdrop, former United team-mate Scholes has cast doubt over whether Carrick's commitment to the cause is wholehearted. Speaking on the Good, the Bad and the Football podcast, the 51-year-old said: "Michael did okay in Middlesbrough with what he had.

"I think Middlesbrough were probably expecting more with the budget they had. There's a bit of me when you look at Michael because I know him...Michael's a nice lad. Is there a bit of him that's thinking, 'Get me out of here. Get me out of here, I'll take a few quid.'".

‌



Scholes also weighed in on the prospect of Fabian Hurzeler stepping into Carrick's shoes, should the club opt to look elsewhere. The German coach has made an impressive start to the campaign, with Brighton and Hove Albion sitting third in the table following four victories, one draw and a solitary loss.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Yet Scholes remains unconvinced that Hurzeler would be the ideal fit for the Old Trafford hot seat. He added: "He's done great. He looks the real deal, but again, Man United is different.

"The scrutiny is on you every single week. If Brighton didn't win a game for the next 10 games, nobody would really be that bothered. The one thing that someone like Hurzeler has got over Michael is that he's done a body of work in the Premier League."

View 2 Images Paul Scholes has questioned Michael Carrick's mentality (Image: PA)

Article continues below

Scholes also pointed out that United may need to start holding those at the top of the club to account, noting that the revolving door of managerial changes cannot be expected to yield a different result indefinitely. He added: "We've been here for the last three years. We look like it looks like or the sound it sounds like, they're going to change the manager again.

"How can we keep doing this? We're back to square one after six games of the season. When do you stop sacking managers and start blaming people above, the people who are possibly buying the players, the people who are pointing at Michael?"

Sports.title: Arsenal cruise to Champions League win over Lille
Sports.content:
Arsenal scored three goals in seven second-half minutes to beat Lille 3-0 and continue their winning start in the Champions League.

The Gunners were frustrated for an hour at the Emirates Stadium but Jurrien Timber's superb finish, lifted over the goalkeeper from Noni Madueke's pass, opened the floodgates.

Eberechi Eze added the second with the help of a slight deflection from substitute Bukayo Saka's pass, and Saka added the third himself after slick interplay with Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, who were introduced alongside him after the opening goal.

Mikel Arteta used the visit of Lille to rotate his side, making five changes from the 2-1 win over Leeds as Arsenal begin a run of eight games in 25 days, but their substitutes helped to ensure they followed up last month's win over Napoli with another victory.

The Gunners should have led earlier with Bruno Guimaraes, starting for the first time at the Emirates Stadium as an Arsenal player, and Eze missing their best chances of the first period.

But Lille's resistance broken with Timber's opener and Davide Ancelotti's side couldn't contain the Gunners, whose substitutions underlined their strength in depth, with Saka particularly impressive before another eye-catching cameo from Max Dowman.

At the other end, Lille did not register a shot on target, although striker Olivier Giroud received a positive reception on his return to the Emirates Stadium as a substitute.

The victory continues a positive start to Arsenal's Champions League campaign as last year's runners-up aim to go one better.

Ancelotti: We couldn't match their rhythm

Lille boss Davide Ancelotti:

"It's really tough. With the players they always have on the bench, they can change the rhythm of the game.

"For us it was difficult to keep up with the rhythm they put after 60 minutes.

"We have to keep the good things we did for 55 or 60 minutes.

"To come here and get a good result, you have to have many things aligned and we didn't have that.

"It's too hard on the players, the score. They didn't deserve this score."
