Sports.title: Saudi Boxing Money Has To Come Down
Sports.content:
Spencer Brown sees a noticeable shift coming to Saudi boxing. Tyson Fury’s manager expects the massive purses to shrink, with fewer mega cards happening each year even though the Kingdom plans to stick around. From his perspective, the current spending pace simply cannot hold, creating a whole new reality for fighters across the sport.

“I think that the money has to go down because nobody can keep paying that sort of money,” Brown told The Ariel Helwani Show.

He made sure to dismiss rumors that Saudi investment is drying up completely. Instead, he sees Riyadh scaling back the volume of blockbuster events.

He pointed to Fury’s December 11 meeting with Anthony Joshua in Cardiff, a deal he helped put together, calling it one of the final spectacles of its kind. Moving forward, he predicts fans will see just one or two events of that size annually. While speaking as a dealmaker rather than an official spokesperson for Riyadh Season, his perspective carries genuine weight.

“I think this is one of the last of the big fights we’re going to see. I think you might get one or two big fights a year in future,” Brown said about the Fury vs. Anthony Joshua clash.

The real trouble will be convincing boxers to accept smaller checks again. Once a fighter pockets Saudi riches, traditional offers funded by gate receipts or pay-per-view sales feel like an insult. A matchup can make all the sense in the world on paper, yet stall out completely if someone insists on another monster payday.

That dynamic could trigger prolonged layoffs. Fighters risk sitting around, holding out hope for an invitation to the rare marquee card. Veterans near the end of their careers do not have time to waste on the sidelines, but the temptation of holding out for life-changing money remains strong.

A market cool-down could ultimately force promoters to build fights around realistic budgets again. For that model to succeed, fighters who want to stay active will have to adjust their financial expectations accordingly.

Fighters who grew accustomed to eight-figure guarantees for low-demand, mismatched events are going to hit a wall of stubborn inactivity before reality sets in.

Human nature and boxing economics suggest the immediate reaction won’t be humility. It will be entitlement.

When a boxer makes $10 million to $20 million fighting an unheralded opponent in an atmosphere with minimal gate pressure, that number ceases to be a windfall in their mind. It becomes their baseline. Returning to a traditional promotional model where their guarantee is tied directly to pay-per-view buys and ticket sales in London, New York, or Las Vegas feels like a drastic demotion.

The fallout is likely to split fighters into distinct groups:

First come the holdouts. The biggest names with heavy bank accounts will sit on the sidelines, convinced that their manager or promoter simply isn’t trying hard enough, or that Riyadh will eventually circle back when a headline slot opens.

They will post training clips on social media, call out other stars, demand absurd splits, and reject viable market-rate offers. Some will sit out twelve to eighteen months before grasping that the sovereign wealth subsidy has actually contracted. For aging stars, this wait will quietly run out their athletic primes.

Second comes the rude awakening for mid-tier names. Fighters who received inflated purses simply to fill out stacked undercards will discover that traditional promoters have zero appetite to subsidize them. If a fighter does not shift tickets in their home market or drive subscriptions, domestic promoters cannot afford them at Saudi rates.

These fighters will face a blunt ultimatum: accept pay cuts of 60 to 75 percent, or retire. Those who need money to maintain luxury spending habits will swallow their pride, sign realistic contracts, and return to competitive, grinding fights where they actually have to take risks.

Ultimately, the market correction will be painful. Boxing spent years living in an artificial economy where risk and commercial return were completely divorced. Once the spigot tightens, the fighters who want to stay relevant will have no choice but to get back in the gym and fight each other on realistic budgets, while the ones chasing long-gone purses will simply wait themselves into irrelevance.

Sports.title: Carlos Adames Signs With Zuffa Ahead Of WBC Deadline
Sports.content:
Carlos Adames has joined Zuffa Boxing, handing the company another 160-pound titlist along with natural pairings against Aaron McKenna and Denzel Bentley. His immediate task centers on an existing top contender who has been waiting in line.

The WBC champion must handle top-ranked Meiirim Nursultanov. Both camps face an October 20 deadline to strike a deal before purse bids get called. Switching promotional banners does nothing to erase that mandate.

“One of the most avoided men in boxing has just joined the Zuffa Boxing roster!” the promotion posted on X, citing Adames as the reigning titlist and The Ring’s top middleweight.

The official statement omitted any debut date or specific rival, leaving open how rapidly matchmakers plan to get him inside the ring.

This acquisition allows the company to pit its stable against one another. Adames taking on IBF belt holder McKenna offers an obvious starting point, assuming both men navigate their mandatory duties. It would offer McKenna a prime platform to test himself against someone marketed as the best in the weight class.

Bentley has publicly staked his claim as well. Following his agreement to box Shane Mosley Jr. on November 7, he declared that facing McKenna would crown the division leader, openly doubting if Adames or Erislandy Lara truly deserve top billing based on their track records.

Adames landing under the same roof gives Bentley a direct chance to back up his talk. Overcoming McKenna would serve as a massive victory, yet stepping in against Adames settles the debate outright rather than trusting opinions and rankings.

The roster now holds enough talent to orchestrate high-level clashes at 160 pounds. The real objective lies in turning those names into actual fights. With the WBC cut-off date arriving in seven days, Adames faces a quick choice on how to direct his championship reign.

A title unification between Adames and Bentley makes plenty of sense on paper, yet Bentley must sort out his WBO status before anyone starts drawing up contracts. Yoenli Hernandez sits in the mandatory slot, leaving officials to rule on whether Bentley can take a voluntary defense against Mosley Jr. Skipping Hernandez risks Bentley losing his hardware at the conference table, which instantly ruins the appeal of unifying later.

Bentley might slip up against Mosley Jr. this November, while Hernandez represents an even sharper tactical threat if the order gets enforced.

The real problem Zuffa faces is its middleweight stable. Collecting belts and accumulating regional contenders looks great on a corporate roster sheet, but packaging belts does not automatically manufacture marquee attractions.

Adames, Aaron McKenna, and Bentley are capable fighters, but none of them possess the crossover appeal required to anchor major pay-per-view broadcasts on their own. Callum Walsh has UFC machinery and Dana White pushing him hard in Irish-American hubs, but his ceiling remains heavily questioned by anyone paying attention to genuine top-tier opposition.

Holding sanctioning body hardware without undisputed public recognition leaves the stable vulnerable. Hardcore observers recognize Yoenli Hernandez as the absolute boogeyman at 160 pounds. His Cuban amateur pedigree, slick defensive mobility, and offensive timing make him the nightmare matchup that sanctioning bodies love to avoid mandating. Bentley or McKenna entering a ring with Hernandez would mean walking into a technical trap with minimal mainstream commercial reward and massive downside risk.

Zuffa essentially has an internal ecosystem of mid-tier titleholders who can trade belts among themselves, but as long as Hernandez sits outside that circle waiting for his shot, any claims to real division supremacy remain empty to knowledgeable fans.

Without Yoenli, Zuffa is essentially running an insulated tournament of secondary names where the belts act as promotional props rather than proof of true dominance.

You can stage Bentley versus McKenna or feed Adames to Walsh to generate domestic buzz, but knowledgeable boxing audiences see right through internal round-robins that deliberately bypass the best fighter on the planet at 160 pounds. Hernandez is the legitimizer. He provides the genuine world-class credibility that transforms a manufactured stable into an authentic division takeover.

Until Zuffa opens the checkbook to bring Hernandez into the fold or puts their titleholders in front of him, their middleweight project remains a closed shop, avoiding its true acid test.

Sports.title: Armando Resendiz Steps Into Jermall Charlo Vacancy Against Koen Mazoudier
Sports.content:
Armando Resendiz faces a tricky rebuilding spot this weekend when he steps in against Koen Mazoudier. Coming off the loss of his WBA super middleweight belt to Jaime Munguia in May, Resendiz finds himself taking over a date originally booked as a tune-up for Jermall Charlo, positioned on a low-profile card that has struggled to grab fan attention.

Resendiz (16-3, 11 KOs) takes on Mazoudier (16-4-1, 6 KOs) over ten rounds on Saturday, October 17, at The Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas. An injury sidelined Charlo, creating an unexpected opening for the former champion on the Sebastian Fundora versus Ermal Hadribeaj undercard.

Mazoudier views the late swap as a genuine upgrade in credibility. In his eyes, taking down Resendiz carries far more weight than beating a faded name returning from another lengthy layoff.

“Beating Charlo would have come with excuses like, ‘He is old and inactive’, and all these different reasons why I’d beaten him,” Mazoudier told Fox Sports Australia.

Mazoudier makes a solid point for his own career, but the contrast is sharp for Resendiz. Dropping down from headline clashes against Caleb Plant and Munguia to face an opponent brought in to shake off Charlo’s ring rust represents a steep slide in stature. Resendiz went from pulling off a signature upset against Plant to dropping his belt, and now he is working to rebuild momentum on short notice.

The loss to Munguia stripped away plenty of momentum built from that Plant triumph. Munguia relied on steady footwork to keep Resendiz chasing throughout a flat contest, completely neutralizing the heavy pressure that troubled Plant. Resendiz fell back into the chasing pack without the kind of fire that sparks clamor for an immediate big money fight.

This matchup does not do much to alter that reality. Buzz around the event has remained quiet, with Fundora defending against Hadribeaj barely moving the needle. The Resendiz and Mazoudier clash sits even further below the radar.

A victory keeps Resendiz active, but handling Mazoudier will not instantly restore his top-tier status. He must look dominant, dictate the tempo, and deliver the kind of statement that forces people to pay attention again. Coasting to a decision over a fill-in opponent leaves him facing an uphill climb to secure elite competition down the road.

Sports.title: Moses Itauma’s January Opponent Must Test His Flaws
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma’s January return needs an opponent who can test the weaknesses Filip Hrgovic exposed. David Adeleye, Guido Vianello or Frank Sanchez would be more worthwhile choices than another overmatched opponent who disappears before Itauma has to work.

Frank Warren confirmed the comeback plans, although he did not name an opponent.

“We told him to just have a little bit of a break and then, as I say, we’ll get back into it in January 2027,” Warren said to talkSPORT.

Adeleye, Vianello, and Sanchez represent the absolute baseline for a legitimate heavyweight contender. They are tough, capable ring operators who know how to survive early pressure and exploit basic technical flaws. If Itauma cannot clear that bar, the entire operation is a facade.

If taking clean shots from a fighter like Vianello or Adeleye causes Itauma to fall apart, then all the early knockouts were simply empty performances against terrified sparring partners. Either he possesses the toughness to belong among the division’s top ten, or he gets exposed as just another manufactured heavyweight who folds the second the script gets ripped up.

“His work rate was tremendous for eight rounds. I mean, he just did not stop throwing punches,” Warren said. “He showed, even though he ran out of gas, he showed he’s got a big heart, and he showed he’s got a good chin. He took some big shots.”

Choosing a soft domestic foe or an over-the-hill name merely sets up an easy stoppage that teaches him nothing.

Finding out right now if Itauma is cut out for the sport saves everyone the illusion. If Itauma lacks the mental fortitude, the engine, or the punch resistance to survive a live opponent firing back, hiding it behind sacrificial lambs only delays the reckoning.

Serving fans another run of manufactured showcases against harmless names is an insult to the ticket-buying public. If Itauma possesses the genuine fiber of a world champion, throwing him into the fire against a gritty operator like Adeleye, Vianello, or Sanchez will prove it immediately.

If he folds under that pressure, it confirms the Hrgovic night was not an off night or a premature test, but an accurate exposure of a fighter whose reputation was entirely engineered by matchmaking.

Sports.title: Frank Warren Offers Ben Whittaker Buatsi Or Hutchinson
Sports.content:
Frank Warren is offering Ben Whittaker a fight with either Joshua Buatsi or Willy Hutchinson, saying he would happily put the unbeaten light heavyweight in with the winner or the loser of their upcoming bout.

Eddie Hearn has already mentioned the winner as a possible opponent before Whittaker challenges Dmitry Bivol. Warren’s offer goes further. He believes either man would provide a serious test, regardless of how their fight ends.

“For me, he’s got a long way to go. I’ve got guys over here he can fight if he wants to fight,” Warren told talkSPORT.

Turning his attention directly toward the Buatsi vs Hutchinson pairing, Warren made his stance clear: “The winner, I have no problem with the winner or the loser fighting him.”

Offering the loser, too, shows how Warren rates Whittaker. He believes either Buatsi or Hutchinson would give him a hard fight, even coming off a defeat.

Whittaker locked down the IBF mandatory slot with his October 3 win over Conor Wallace, yet his ragged finish exposed glaring doubts about his readiness for Bivol. Exhaustion stripped away his legs down the stretch, forcing him into survival mode as Wallace pushed forward.

The theatrical showmanship that looked slick against lesser fighters disappeared once the pressure intensified. Wallace wore Whittaker down, leaving him exhausted and holding on to get through the final rounds. Against Buatsi or Hutchinson, he would need enough stamina to keep throwing punches and defending himself when the fight gets hard.

Buatsi would bring pressure and heavy punches, testing whether Whittaker can hold his technique together when he cannot dictate the pace. Hutchinson would present a different challenge with his speed and boxing ability. Either would be a considerable step up.

“Ben’s a nice guy. Good luck to him. But you’ve got to have some substance, and the substance at the end of the day just isn’t there,” Warren said.

Hearn also concedes Whittaker requires another outing before facing Bivol, keeping the Buatsi vs Hutchinson victor in play. Both promoters see the need for a sterner test, even though Warren shows far less belief in Whittaker’s actual ceiling.

Warren goes further by offering the loser, too. That’s the sharper part of his challenge: in his view, either man would test Whittaker, regardless of the result. Beating one of them would give Whittaker stronger evidence that he’s ready for Bivol.

Sports.title: Robert Garcia Risks Missing Naoya Inoue Fight
Sports.content:
Naoya Inoue has no intention of waiting around for Jesse “Bam” Rodriguez and will begin preparing for a move to featherweight. His response puts pressure on trainer Robert Garcia’s plan for another bantamweight fight before facing Inoue in April or May 2027.

Garcia wants Rodriguez in the ring with Christian Medina at bantamweight first, pushing an Inoue clash back to spring 2027. Antonio Vargas tested Bam with pure speed. Now Garcia wants a heavy hitter to see how Bam handles power at 118.

“I want Bam to feel punches, you know, block, be able to absorb some of those punches at 118 from a very strong fighter,” Robert said to Fight Hub TV.

That sounds like a trainer who still doubts his guy is ready. Garcia believes Bam can challenge Inoue, but he wants extra proof before taking the leap. Inoue has zero reason to plan his schedule around Garcia’s hesitation.

Robert also questioned Inoue moving to 126 so quickly, claiming the Japanese superstar is physically mature enough to stay put.

“He’s already a man. He’s already built,” Garcia said.

Physical maturity doesn’t mean sticking around at junior featherweight makes sense. Featherweight brings fresh challenges. A division lacking marquee names gives Inoue no real motive to linger. Moving up while he has elite years left beats waiting around for Bam.

Garcia also floated the idea that Inoue wants this matchup fast because Rodriguez gets sharper with time.

“He might think if the longer he waits, the bigger chance Bam has.”

That logic assumes Inoue cares to wait around. He could simply leave the division behind.

Taking another fight at 118 might calm Garcia’s nerves. It won’t prepare Bam for the threat waiting at 122. Team Bam can keep hunting for tuneups, or they can embrace the danger of chasing a superstar. They don’t get to dictate Inoue’s timeline.

Robert is misreading who holds the leverage. Inoue is an undisputed champion, an international superstar, and a massive ticket seller. He dictates the terms, the timing, and the division.

Bam’s side wants Inoue to pause his career, pass on 126, and wait for them to finish test runs at bantamweight, which doesn’t make sense. If you want the monster, you take the shot when the door is open.

Sports.title: Tim Tszyu vs Erislandy Lara WBA Title Fight Announced in Australia
Sports.content:
Tszyu secured the middleweight title shot by defeating Errol Spence Jr and will pursue a championship in a second division.

Tim Tszyu will challenge Erislandy Lara for the WBA middleweight title in Australia. Promoters have not announced the fight date, host city, venue or broadcaster.

The matchup sends Tszyu back into a championship fight after he outpointed Errol Spence Jr in Sydney in July. That victory extended his winning streak to three bouts and lifted his record to 28-3 with 18 knockouts.

Tszyu will remain at the 160-pound limit rather than return to super welterweight.

“At 160 I feel strong, I feel sharp and I feel dangerous. Middleweight is my division now. Spence was just the appetiser,” Tszyu said in the official announcement.

Tszyu Targets Championship in Second Division

Tszyu previously captured the WBO super welterweight title. Dethroning Lara would add a middleweight championship to his record and make him the first member of the Tszyu family to claim world titles in two weight classes.

His father, Kostya Tszyu, unified the junior welterweight division and captured every world championship of his career at 140 pounds.

“I’ve carried the Tszyu name my whole life. It’s a privilege and it’s pressure. This is my chance to write a chapter that belongs to me, and it’s the legacy defining moment of my career,” Tszyu said.

Jeff Fenech will command Tszyu’s corner for the title challenge. The former three-division champion joined Tszyu’s team in April 2026 and guided him through the Spence victory.

Lara Brings WBA Belt to Australia

Lara enters the matchup with a 32-3-3 record and 19 knockouts. The Cuban southpaw captured the WBA “Regular” middleweight belt in 2021 before the organization elevated him to full champion in 2023.

The 43-year-old has completed four successful title defenses and has never lost by stoppage as a professional. He also previously captured WBA championships at super welterweight.

Lara’s title reign and southpaw craft give Tszyu a seasoned champion to crack. Tszyu will bring pressure, body punching and home support into his bid to seize the belt.

Promoters expect to announce the date, location, ticket information and broadcast details in the coming weeks.

Sports.title: VIDEO: Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley II Preview & Prediction
Sports.content:
Coming up this Saturday on the 17th of October, from The O2 Arena in London, in a heavyweight championship showdown that will be streamed live worldwide exclusively on DAZN PPV – reigning WBO heavyweight champion Daniel Dubois puts his title on the line in a highly anticipated immediate rematch against former champion Fabio Wardley.

BUY Dubois-Wardley 2 on DAZN

The heavyweight landscape is absolute chaos right now, turning into the Wild West ever since Oleksandr Usyk vacated his collection of alphabet belts. With the rest of the division fighting over the pieces, the stakes could not be any higher. For Dubois, a victory confirms that his reign is the real deal and cements his standing as one of the premier heavyweights in the world. For Wardley, it is entirely about redemption – proving his storybook run was no fluke and reclaiming the world title he worked so hard to win.

Their first encounter just five months ago in Manchester was an absolute barnburner. Wardley stunned everyone early, scoring two dramatic knockdowns and pushing Dubois to the brink. But Dubois weathered the early storm, leaned on his piston-like jab, and systematically took over before halting Wardley in the 11th round.

Heading into Saturday’s return bout, the prevailing consensus is that Wardley shot his bolt, and Dubois will simply repeat the feat. Most observers are writing the former champion off completely. But is it really that simple? If Wardley makes the necessary tactical adjustments, can he pull off the upset?

Who will win the upcoming heavyweight championship rematch between Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley?

This edition of Rummy’s Corner will contemplate the question while providing a quick preview and official prediction. This is Rummy’s Corner (written, narrated, and produced by Geoffrey Ciani).

Ghana News.title: Imagination Africa, Mentors Chess Academy to host second African Genius Chess Championship at Ghud Park
Ghana News.content:
Imagination Africa and Mentors Chess Academy will host the second African Genius Chess Championship on Saturday, 24 October 2026, at Ghud Park, Accra Mall.

The competition uses chess to develop young minds, promote inclusion and create equal opportunities for children from different socio-economic backgrounds.

“Talent and potential are not determined by a child’s social or economic circumstances. On the chessboard, every child starts with the same pieces and the same chances, and that is the opportunity we want to give them,” said Mariam Mahamah, co-founder of Imagination Africa.

The maiden edition, held at Legon City Mall in 2024, attracted more than 150 young players from over 15 schools across Ghana. Participants competed in age categories ranging from Under-8 to Under-20.

Twelve-year-old Dave Chief Quansah Acheampong was the standout performer, going unbeaten in four rounds against older players from Presec, the University of Ghana, DPS International and ARIS to win the Under-20 title.

The 2024 event was attended by a representative of the Ministry of Education and the High Commissioner of India to Ghana. Parents also praised the initiative for providing a conducive environment for children to learn and play chess.

This year’s competition will feature different age categories, with trophies, medals and gift prizes for top finishers and the best girl in each category.

The organisers say chess can help young people develop critical thinking, concentration, discipline, confidence and problem-solving skills. They have encouraged chess enthusiasts to participate.

Imagination Africa plans to make the championship an annual event and is seeking partners to expand its reach and support youth development, social inclusion and intellectual growth.

Imagination Africa is a non-profit organisation that identifies, develops and showcases young people’s talent in Ghana through sports, arts and academics, creating opportunities for underprivileged children to reach their full potential.

Ghana News.title: Nana B passport claims a diversionary tactic — Abu Jinapor
Ghana News.content:
The Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abu Jinapor, has dismissed allegations that the Member of Parliament for Bosome Freho, Nana Asafo-Adjei Ayeh, lobbied Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa over a passport for New Patriotic Party (NPP) Second Vice-Chairman Henry Nana Boakye, popularly known as Nana B, describing them as a diversionary tactic.

Mr Jinapor said the allegation was intended to distract from the Minority’s concerns over expenditure on Ghana’s evacuation of citizens from South Africa, for which it is demanding an independent audit.

Speaking on Eyewitness News on Tuesday, October 13, Mr Jinapor said Nana B had never held a diplomatic passport and had surrendered his service passport in accordance with a directive issued by the new government.

“Let me say that that allegation is a complete diversionary tactic, and it’s a rule in the old book, you know it, I know it, and we should not allow ourselves to be distracted,” he said.

Mr Jinapor said he had spoken to Mr Asafo-Adjei Ayeh, who told him that Nana B had formally requested the transfer of a valid visa from his old passport to a new one.

“He had a valid visa in the passport, and he made a requisition, a formal requisition, that the visa be transferred to his new passport, which the minister committed to work on,” Mr Jinapor said.

He added that Mr Asafo-Adjei Ayeh followed up with the minister once and was told the matter was still being processed, after which he did not pursue it further.

The comments follow allegations by the Majority Caucus on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee that Mr Asafo-Adjei Ayeh pressured Mr Ablakwa to allow Nana B to retain a service passport he was allegedly not entitled to hold.

Salaga South MP Hajia Zuwera Mohammed Ibrahimah made the allegation, claiming that Mr Asafo-Adjei Ayeh and Nana B had sought an exception from the minister.

She said Mr Ablakwa rejected the request because Nana B’s former positions as NPP National Youth Organiser and Board Chairman of the National Food Buffer Stock Company did not qualify him for a service passport.

Mr Jinapor also rejected attempts to link the passport issue to the Minority’s scrutiny of the South Africa evacuation expenditure, insisting that the caucus had not accused the minister of wrongdoing.

Ghana News.title: Pope Leo diagnosed with cancer as doctors remove lobe of lung, Vatican says
Ghana News.content:
Pope Leo was diagnosed with a common form of lung cancer after doctors removed ​a lower lobe of his right lung in surgery on Tuesday, the Vatican said in a medical bulletin.

The 71-year-old pontiff ‌has lung adenocarcinoma, with tissue tests conducted during the operation confirming what doctors had suspected from preparatory examinations, the bulletin said.

The pope was admitted to Rome's Gemelli hospital on Tuesday for surgery to remove a growth on his lung that doctors found in a recent health checkup.

The Vatican had said earlier on Tuesday evening that the ​surgery had been successful before providing a more detailed update from the pope's lead surgeon, Professor Stefano Margaritora, the chief of ​thoracic surgery at the Gemelli.

"In order to make the procedure curative, the lower lobe of the right lung was ⁠removed using a video-assisted technique," said Margaritora's update.

"A rapid intraoperative histological examination confirmed the diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, as had been suspected from ​the pre-operative tests," it said.

Tuesday's surgery lasted about 90 minutes and was successful with no complications, the Vatican said. The pope has woken up normally ​and is resting in his hospital room.

Ghana News.title: Legal Aid Commission takes free legal services to Techiman main lorry terminal
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Legal Aid Commission has launched its 2026 Legal Aid Week with a bold new approach to closing the country's access-to-justice gap, bringing free legal services directly to the people who need them most.

Under the theme "Justice at Your Doorstep," the Commission has rolled out a pilot outreach initiative that takes legal aid out of formal offices and into the heart of everyday Ghanaian life: markets and lorry terminals.

The program specifically targets traders, commercial drivers, and vulnerable citizens who cannot easily leave their workplaces to seek legal assistance.

For years, access to justice in Ghana has been hindered by a simple but stubborn barrier: geography and economics. Traders in busy markets and drivers at lorry terminals often cannot afford to abandon their livelihoods for a day to visit a legal aid office -assuming they even know such services exist.

"We see justice not to be a commodity to be sold to the highest bidder," said Justice Seidu Anafure, Senior Legal Aid Officer at the Commission's Bono East Regional Office.

"The traditional approach has been for people to come to us. But we realized the most vulnerable cannot leave their work to come to our offices. So we decided to reverse the equation; we are taking justice to them."

The initiative was officially launched in Accra, with planned stops at the Tema Station lorry terminal, Kaneshie Market, and Kasoa Market. But the program is not confined to the capital. Regional offices across the country are rolling out similar localized outreach efforts.

Today, the Bono East Regional Office stormed the Techiman Main Lorry Terminal, where citizens consulted directly with lawyers, received legal education, and got assistance with dispute resolution, including Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR)—all free of charge.

The ADR component is particularly significant. By focusing on out-of-court settlements, the Commission offers a faster, less adversarial, and more accessible path to resolving conflicts that might otherwise drag through Ghana's overburdened court system for years.

For many who attended the Techiman outreach, it was their first-ever interaction with a lawyer.

One commercial driver, who stopped to listen between loading trips, said the session had been eye-opening.

"I came here to load my vehicle, but I ended up getting free legal advice," he said.

"This is very helpful. I wish they could do this regularly, maybe every month. We have so many issues among ourselves, and sometimes we don't know where to go."

A trader who consulted with a lawyer on a long-standing dispute expressed similar gratitude.

"I didn't know I could get legal help for free," she said. "I thought lawyers were only for the rich. Today, I've registered my case, and they are going to help me. I'm very grateful."

The session also featured an open question-and-answer segment, where participants raised concerns ranging from landlord-tenant disputes to family and commercial matters.

The Commission's message is clear: justice should not be a privilege reserved for those who can afford it.

"Whether you are a driver, a trader, a farmer, or a vulnerable citizen, if you have a legal problem, we are here to help," Anafure said. "Justice at your doorstep is not just a theme. It is our commitment."

Ghana News.title: Nana B denies seeking passport favour, accuses Ablakwa of failing to account for GH¢16.4m
Ghana News.content:
National Vice Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) Henry Nana Boakye, popularly known as Nana B, has denied seeking a favour from Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa to retain his service passport.

He insisted that the controversy is being used to divert attention from questions over GH¢16.4 million allegedly spent on evacuating Ghanaians from South Africa.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, October 13, 2026, Nana B rejected claims by the Majority in Parliament that Deputy Ranking Member of the Foreign Affairs Committee, Nana Asafo-Adjei, was pursuing a personal vendetta against Mr Ablakwa over the passport issue.

The Majority had alleged that Mr Asafo-Adjei’s criticism of the Minister stemmed from his refusal to grant a request for a former NPP national organiser to retain his service passport.

However, Nana B described the allegation as “weak, diversionary, unreasonable and a red herring” intended to cover up what he said were concerns about possible corruption raised by Mr Asafo-Adjei.

He clarified that he had possessed only a service passport and had never held a diplomatic passport, adding that he surrendered the service passport in compliance with the President’s directive as published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

According to him, his request to Mr Ablakwa was for a formal letter to notify embassies whose visas were in the service passport so the visas could be transferred to his ordinary passport.

Nana B said Mr Ablakwa personally asked him to get Mr Asafo-Adjei to follow up on the letter, which he did.

“Okudzeto Ablakwa personally requested that I inform Hon. Asafo Adjei to follow up on the letter, which I did, but after one visit, Hon. Asafo Adjei was informed the letter was not ready; hence, I abandoned it and applied for new visas,” he said.

He maintained that Mr Asafo-Adjei had not sought any special favour from the Minister but had followed up on the letter at Mr Ablakwa’s request.

“I never requested to retain the passport because doing so would have been unreasonable as a national executive of the opposition party,” Nana B added.

The NPP official also expressed concern that the Majority had displayed the biographical data page of his service passport, which he said was in the custody of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Turning to the evacuation expenditure, Nana B accused the Majority of attempting to shield Mr Ablakwa from accountability over the GH¢16.4 million.

He argued that the concerns raised by Mr Asafo-Adjei were based on data submitted by the Minister himself and should not be dismissed as a personal dispute.

“The majority should not take discerning Ghanaians for fools by suggesting that a member of Parliament’s exposition on possible corruption to the tune of GHS16.4 million, based on data submitted by Okudzeto himself, is a personal vendetta,” he said.

Nana B called on the Majority to demand explanations from Mr Ablakwa over what he described as serious inconsistencies in documents relating to the evacuation expenditure.

“President Mahama promised Ghanaians accountability, and the majority should call Okudzeto Ablakwa to answer the serious inconsistencies in the documents submitted regarding the expenditure on the evacuation of citizens,” he said.

The statement did not provide a detailed breakdown of the alleged inconsistencies in the evacuation expenditure.

The claims of possible corruption and the alleged failure to account for the funds remain allegations in Nana B’s statement.

Ghana News.title: Young girls demand climate action, stronger protection against child marriage
Ghana News.content:
Young girls have called for increased investment in education, healthcare and protection as climate change exposes more of them to risks, including child marriage, during Plan International Ghana’s Girls’ Takeover Day on Tuesday, October 13, 2026.

The event formed part of activities to commemorate the 2026 International Day of the Girl Child, observed globally on October 11, and featured the launch of Plan International’s State of the World’s Girls 2026 report.

The report examines the links between climate change, sexual and reproductive health and rights, and child marriage.

The Girls’ Takeover initiative saw children and young people assume leadership roles at Plan International Ghana and UNICEF Ghana to amplify calls for girls’ rights and greater participation in decisions affecting their futures.

Speaking at the event, 14-year-old Priscilla, who took over as Country Director of Plan International Ghana for a day, said climate-related disasters were making life increasingly difficult for girls.

She said floods, droughts and extreme heat could disrupt education, limit access to healthcare and expose girls to violence, exploitation and pressure to marry at a young age.

“We are children. We should be learning, playing and dreaming about our future, not worrying about how climate disasters will affect our lives,” she said.

The children outlined five key recommendations to address these challenges, including keeping girls in school during climate-related emergencies, investing in girls’ health and ensuring access to essential services during disasters.

They also called for targeted support for girls at greater risk, including those with disabilities, girls from minority communities and those displaced from their homes.

The fifth recommendation urged leaders to include girls in climate-related decision-making, arguing that their experiences and ideas should inform policies affecting their lives.

“Even though we are young, we understand the challenges we face, and we deserve to be part of decisions about our future,” the children said.

Juliet, 21, who took over as UNICEF Ghana’s Officer in Charge for a day, said the initiative provided an opportunity for young people to demonstrate that their voices mattered in discussions about their rights and future.

The children also called for an end to child marriage and greater investment in girls’ rights as part of activities marking the 2026 International Day of the Girl Child.

They urged stakeholders to work towards a future in which every girl could access education, healthcare and protection, regardless of the climate challenges facing her community.

At the close of the event, the substantive Country Director of Plan International Ghana and UNICEF Ghana’s Officer in Charge assured the children that their proposals would be considered for action. The assurance followed the girls’ calls for stronger measures to protect their rights and ensure their participation in decisions affecting them.

“Our future matters. Our voices matter. And it is time to #ChangeHerForecast,” they said, as they formally launched Plan International’s State of the World’s Girls 2026 report.

Ghana News.title: Ex-gang boss sentenced to 40 years for orchestrating Tupac Shakur’s murder
Ghana News.content:
Former gang boss Duane "Keffe D" Davis has been sentenced to at least 40 years in prison for orchestrating the murder of Tupac Shakur.

A jury found Davis, 63, guilty in September of one count of murder with a deadly weapon for the rap superstar's death in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas on 7 September 1996. He has said he will appeal the verdict.

Prosecutors argued that although Davis did not fire the gun himself, he was the ringleader of the group that committed the murder. He admitted in his memoir that he had provided the gun used in the crime.

Davis' conviction was the first in a cold case that has intrigued hip-hop fans for nearly 30 years.

Prosecutor Marc DiGiacomo argued during Tuesday's sentencing hearing that Davis spent years "publicly grandstanding" and bragging about his role on Shakur's death, which he said, "had wide-ranging effects upon the world".

Ghana News.title: From near-deferral to three awards: UMaT graduate’s academic journey
Ghana News.content:
Solicity Amankwa-Taylor, a graduate of the University of Mines and Technology (UMaT), has earned three academic awards after financial difficulties nearly forced her to defer her studies, a challenge she says was eased by the MTN Bright Scholarship.

Solicity, who studied Environmental and Safety Engineering, faced growing financial pressure after her father lost his job, leaving her mother’s business as the family’s main source of income.

With her elder brother also pursuing tertiary education, meeting tuition, accommodation and other university expenses became increasingly difficult.

She said the situation left her considering external financial support or deferring her studies until her family’s circumstances improved.

“Things became tough financially to the point that I had to either find a means of financial support or defer. When I found out I had been selected as an MTN Bright Scholar, I had hope in achieving my dreams again,” she said.

The scholarship provided financial support for tuition and accommodation, easing the burden on her family and allowing her to concentrate on her academic work.

“The scholarship helped me channel all my focus on my studies. With a sound mind, I was also able to help some of my colleagues academically,” she added.

Solicity’s academic performance earned her three awards during her university journey.

At the 9th Ghana Mining Industry Awards, she was named Best Level 200 Female Engineering Student.

She also received the Prof. Newton Attah Amegbey Award for Best Graduating Student in the Department of Environmental and Safety Engineering and the Prof. Douglas Boateng Award for Best Graduating Student in the Faculty of Geosciences and Environmental Studies at graduation.

She is currently undertaking her national service as a Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) personnel at YILPORT-ATSL in Takoradi, where she is applying the knowledge and skills acquired during her studies.

Her experience forms part of stories highlighting the impact of the MTN Bright Scholarship as MTN Ghana marks 30 years of operations in the country under the theme, “30 Years of Progress, Power to You.”

The scholarship, an initiative of the MTN Ghana Foundation, supports brilliant but financially disadvantaged students in public tertiary institutions.

It covers tuition, accommodation, stipends for reading materials and a laptop to help beneficiaries pursue their education.

Solicity’s journey illustrates how financial assistance can help students overcome barriers to completing their education and prepare for professional careers.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
