CAPE TOWN — The best things to do in Cape Town in October 2026 run from free street art and a Mozart opera to a kite festival and a Gothic ballet. This guide lists seven events from Wednesday 14 October to the weekend of 1 November, with dates, venues and prices we could confirm.

It is written for people who live here or are staying for weeks. Prices are in South African rand (ZAR), converted at about R16.5 to the US dollar (RT, 13 October 2026).

14 to 17 October: Street Art and Ne-Yo

Wednesday 14 to Saturday 17 October Live Art Festival UCT campuses, KwaLanga and central Cape Town · Free The University of Cape Town’s Institute for Creative Arts stages about 30 performances and installations across four days. Dance, theatre, music and visual art move out of galleries and into public spaces. Central venues include the Cape Town Station forecourt, St Georges Mall and the Castle.

Saturday 17 October, from 18:00 Ne-Yo Live in South Africa Grand Arena, GrandWest, Goodwood · R990 to R1,890 (about US$60 to US$115) · Webtickets The American R&B singer plays Cape Town the night before a second show at the SunBet Arena in Pretoria. Prices exclude booking fees. GrandWest is a casino and entertainment complex in Goodwood, so most people arrive by car or ride-share.

22 to 25 October: Opera, Kites and Film

Thursday 22 to Sunday 25 October, evenings and a Sunday matinee Don Giovanni Pam Golding Theatre, The Baxter, Rondebosch · Webtickets Opera UCT stages Mozart’s opera with the Cape Town Philharmonic Orchestra in the pit. It is sung in Italian with captions in English and isiXhosa, and runs about three hours and 15 minutes with one interval.

Saturday 24 to Sunday 25 October, 10:00 to 18:00 Cape Town International Kite Festival Youngsfield Military Base, Ottery · Children R60, adults R90 (about US$3.60 and US$5.50) · Quicket The 32nd edition is organised by Cape Mental Health under the theme #ColourTheSky. Children under five enter free, a weekend pass costs R160 for adults (about US$9.70) and R100 for children and pensioners (about US$6.10), and dogs are not allowed. Quicket adds admin fees to the displayed prices.

Saturday 24 October, 18:00 to 22:00 Observatory Film Festival Observatory Community Recreation Centre, Observatory · Quicket The fourth edition showcases independent and student films alongside local art and craft vendors. The programme includes the African premiere of the experimental short Surrendered, by filmmaker Marie-Josée Desharnais. Children under 13 are not admitted.

24 October to 1 November: Sondheim and a Gothic Ballet

Opens Saturday 24 October, runs to Saturday 14 November Into the Woods Theatre on the Bay, Camps Bay · Webtickets LAMTA stages Stephen Sondheim and James Lapine’s musical, directed by Sylvaine Strike.

Wednesday 28 October to Sunday 1 November Cape Town City Ballet: Dracula Artscape Theatre Centre, Foreshore · R250 to R500 (about US$15 to US$30) · Webtickets David Nixon’s ballet of the Bram Stoker story returns for one Halloween-weekend run. Evening shows start at 19:30 from Wednesday 28 to Saturday 31 October, with matinees at 14:00 on Saturday 31 October and at 12:00 and 16:00 on Sunday 1 November. Children under 13 are not admitted, and Artscape Dial-A-Seat takes bookings on 021 421 7695.

What it means for you

For a reader in the United States, the rand keeps most of these tickets cheap. Apart from Ne-Yo, every ticket listed here costs less than US$35.

If you are planning a long stay, book Dracula and Don Giovanni early, as both are short runs. Foreign cards sometimes fail on local ticket platforms, so keep a second payment method.

Planning Your Cape Town October

October is spring in Cape Town, with mild days and cooler evenings. South Africa has no national public holiday in October 2026, so shops and offices keep normal hours.

Webtickets sells Ne-Yo, Don Giovanni, Into the Woods and Dracula, while Quicket sells the kite and film festivals. Check the organiser’s page before you pay, because platforms add booking fees.

Ride-share is the easiest way home from Goodwood, Ottery and Camps Bay at night. For more on the country, read our South Africa coverage and the explainer on South African history.

If you are in the city in December, French Montana plays Cape Town on 4 December. For the same month in a different city, see our Monterrey guide.

What We Could Not Confirm

Sources differ on the evening start time of Don Giovanni, so check the Baxter box office before you travel. We could not confirm performance times for Into the Woods or the day-by-day programme of the Live Art Festival.

We left out events whose date, venue or price we could not verify with the organiser or a ticket seller. Programmes can change, so confirm with the venue before you go.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is there a public holiday in South Africa in October 2026?

No, South Africa has no national public holiday in October 2026, so shops and offices keep normal hours all month.

Which Cape Town events in October 2026 are free?

The Live Art Festival from 14 to 17 October is free, and children under five enter the Kite Festival free.

Where can I buy tickets for Cape Town events in October 2026?

Webtickets sells Ne-Yo, Don Giovanni, Into the Woods and Dracula, while Quicket sells the Kite Festival and the Observatory Film Festival.

How much does the Cape Town International Kite Festival cost?

Children aged six to 12 pay R60 (about US$3.60) and adults R90 (about US$5.50) per day on Quicket, before admin fees.

Can children see Dracula at Artscape?

No, Cape Town City Ballet admits no children under 13 to Dracula, which runs from 28 October to 1 November 2026.

WINDHOEK · Culture

From a high-tea morning on 17 October to the 66th Windhoek Oktoberfest on 30 and 31 October, 9 ticketed events with dates, venues and prices in US$.

WINDHOEK, Namibia. Windhoek’s October calendar runs from a high-tea morning on Saturday 17 October to the 66th Windhoek Oktoberfest on Friday 30 and Saturday 31 October.

Of the 9 events below, 7 start at N$150 (about US$9) or less.

This guide lists 9 events that still lie ahead as of Tuesday 13 October 2026. For each one, the ticket seller or organiser lists the date, venue and price.

The featured listings we checked on Webtickets Namibia begin on 17 October, so nothing is listed here for 12 to 16 October. Events that were not clearly in Windhoek are left out.

For readers in the United States, the practical point is cost and booking. Events sell through local platforms in Namibian dollars, which trade at about N$16.50 per US$1 (RT, 13 October 2026).

Oktoberfest organisers say online tickets are cheaper than gate sales.

Key Facts Who: Residents, expats and visitors in Windhoek, Namibia’s capital

Saturday 17 October: high tea and polo

Saturday 17 October, 11:00 Polo Exhibition Match La Muela, 35 minutes south of Windhoek · From N$120 (about US$7) A polo exhibition match in the Namibian savannah. Food and drinks are sold on site. Allow time for the drive out of town.

23 and 24 October: choirs, motorsport and fashion

Friday 23 October, 16:00 High Octane Festival 2026 Tony Rust Race Track, Windhoek · From N$70 (about US$4) A motorsport weekend with spinning and drag racing on Friday, then gymkhana and drifting on Saturday. Friday tickets start at N$70 (about US$4).

Friday 23 October, 18:30 UNAM Choir Concert UNAM Main Campus, Main Hall, Windhoek · From N$100 (about US$6) A concert by the University of Namibia choir.

Saturday 24 October, 16:00 ARCHAUS Presents Margarita Sunsets La Leona Mexican Restaurant, Windhoek · From N$150 (about US$9) The second edition of the Archaus balcony series this season, at La Leona. The organiser promises an afternoon, sunset and night of cocktails and food.

Saturday 24 October, 18:00 Simply You Magazine Lifestyle and Fashion Awards 2026 Hilton Hotel, Windhoek · N$150 (about US$9) An awards evening.

29 to 31 October: the month closes with Oktoberfest

Friday 30 and Saturday 31 October Windhoek Oktoberfest 2026 (66th edition) Sport Klub Windhoek grounds, Olympia · Online adult tickets N$220 Friday, N$245 Saturday (about US$13, US$15) The Namibian reports that the 66th Windhoek Oktoberfest is a joint setup of Namibia Breweries, the O&L Group and the sports club. The Bavarian band Die Kirchdorfer returns for a 14th year, with the Rocktoberfest Dancers and the ÖK Beans Band. Early-bird tickets for the first 300 buyers were N$200 Friday, N$220 Saturday and N$400 for the weekend (about US$12, US$13 and US$24), so current prices may be higher. Children aged 7 to 13 pay N$60 (about US$4), and children under six enter free. Organisers advise buying online through NamEvents because gate sales will be limited and cost significantly more. The festival runs on a cashless wristband system.

Saturday 31 October, 14:00 2026 Restoration Concert 4.0 Hage Geingob Stadium, Windhoek · From N$50 (about US$3) A gospel and worship concert starting at 14:00, with the Namibia Tourism Board as a strategic partner. The Namibian reports that organisers expect 20,000 people, double the previous edition, and Webtickets lists tickets from N$50 (about US$3).

Planning your October in Windhoek

La Muela is about 35 minutes south of the city, so the polo match needs a car or a pre-arranged ride. The Tony Rust Race Track is also outside the centre, so check the route before you go.

Check the ticket page for the final venue, time and price before you travel, because organisers can change them. Most of these events sell through Webtickets Namibia, and Windhoek Oktoberfest sells through NamEvents.

What it means for you

If you are travelling from the United States, most tickets cost modest sums in dollar terms. A club night or a choir concert costs about US$6, and the Oktoberfest online prices of US$13 to US$15 a day are the main exception among the big events.

Residents can use the same list to plan around work and school. Most of the programme sits on Fridays and Saturdays.

What is not known

Several listings do not describe the programme. For ARCHAUS Margarita Sunsets and SoufSideChill, the pages give a venue, time and price but few details of what happens.

We have not confirmed current Oktoberfest ticket availability or whether the early-bird allocation has sold out.

What are the biggest events in Windhoek in October 2026?

The 66th Windhoek Oktoberfest on Friday 30 and Saturday 31 October is the largest, alongside the High Octane Festival at the Tony Rust Race Track on Friday 23 October and the Restoration Concert 4.0 at Hage Geingob Stadium on Saturday 31 October.

Where can I buy tickets for Windhoek events?

Most events in this guide sell tickets on Webtickets Namibia. Windhoek Oktoberfest organisers point buyers to NamEvents, and they say gate sales will be limited and cost significantly more.

How much do Windhoek events cost in US dollars?

Entry prices in this guide start at N$50 (about US$3) and most start at N$150 (about US$9) or less, at an exchange rate of about N$16.50 per US$1. Oktoberfest online adult tickets cost N$220 on Friday and N$245 on Saturday (about US$13 and US$15).

Is Windhoek Oktoberfest 2026 cashless?

Yes. The Namibian reports that the festival at the Sport Klub Windhoek grounds on 30 and 31 October runs on a completely cashless wristband system, and organisers advise buying tickets online through NamEvents.

The Restoration Concert 4.0 on Saturday 31 October has the lowest entry price, from N$50 (about US$3) on Webtickets. Friday tickets for the High Octane Festival on 23 October start at N$70 (about US$4).

World.title: Pope Leo Has Lung Cancer After Surgery
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

Pope Leo XIV, 71, had the lower lobe of his right lung removed at Agostino Gemelli Hospital in Rome on Tuesday 13 October 2026. The Vatican said the operation confirmed a lung adenocarcinoma, a common form of lung cancer that starts in gland-like cells.

Leo, elected in May 2025, is the first US-born pope, and his scheduled trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru runs from 6 to 17 November 2026. No change to that trip had been announced in the sources we reviewed.

Key Facts —Who. Pope Leo XIV, 71, the first US-born pope. —What. Lung cancer surgery that confirmed an adenocarcinoma; the lower lobe of the right lung was removed. —Where. Agostino Gemelli Hospital, Rome. —When. Tuesday 13 October 2026; the operation lasted about 90 minutes. —Outlook. About one week of hospital recovery expected; papal audiences cancelled through 20 October. —Trip. Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, 6 to 17 November 2026; no change announced. —Prediction markets. Kalshi last-traded prices for a papal visit in 2026: Peru 89%, Uruguay 87%, Argentina 83%. These are bets, not polls. —As of. 13 October 2026, 5:07 pm ET (21:07 GMT).

The Vatican called the intervention a success with no complications, as Vatican News and the Colombian outlets La República, El Espectador, El Tiempo and Semana reported. The pope announced the planned surgery at the Angelus on Sunday 11 October, as covered in our earlier report.

What We Know

The pope arrived at the hospital shortly after 13:00 Rome time on Tuesday. The thoracic surgical team was led by Professor Stefano Margaritora, according to El Tiempo and El Espectador.

The Vatican said tests before surgery had pointed to a lung adenocarcinoma and that the operation confirmed it. Surgeons removed the lower lobe of the right lung.

A lobe is one of the main sections of a lung, and the right lung has three. The lower lobe is the bottom section.

The operation lasted about 90 minutes. The Vatican described it as a success with no complications.

About one week of recovery in hospital is expected. All papal audiences are cancelled through 20 October, El Tiempo and Semana reported.

The Angelus is a short prayer that the pope leads from St Peter’s Square on Sundays. On 11 October he told the faithful that a localized nodule, found at a very early stage, would be removed.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What Is Not Known

More tests are under way to determine whether the cancer spread beyond the removed lobe, according to a Vatican source cited by El Espectador. That result is not yet known.

The sources we read do not say whether further treatment will be needed. They also give no timetable beyond the expected week in hospital.

Whether the November trip will change is also unknown. No change had been announced in the sources we read.

Archive photo: St Peter’s Square and Basilica, Vatican City.

What It Means for Travelers and US Readers

The scheduled trip covers Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from 6 to 17 November 2026. Gestión reported that the pope is due in Peru on 11 November, with stops in Lima, Chiclayo, Cusco and Pucallpa.

Our background is in coverage of the pope’s November visit to Peru and in our Peru visit report. For the two best-known stops, see our guide to Lima and Cusco.

Leo is the first US-born pope, so the news carries particular weight for American Catholics and for US pilgrims planning to visit Rome. Audiences through 20 October are cancelled.

Travellers with bookings should follow official announcements from the Vatican and local organisers. Nothing in the sources we read points to a change at this stage.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Kalshi, a market regulated in the US by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), traders bet on country-by-country markets for which countries Pope Leo will visit in 2026. As of 13 October 2026, 5:07 pm ET, the last traded prices were Peru 89%, Uruguay 87% and Argentina 83%.

The series, titled “What countries will Pope Leo visit in 2026?”, had 216,979 contracts traded across the countries. These prices are bets, not polls, they say nothing about his health, and they are not a statement from the Vatican.

Prices move as news arrives, so these figures are a snapshot rather than a forecast. They may differ by the time you read this.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Frequently Asked Questions

What happened to Pope Leo XIV?

The pope had surgery at Agostino Gemelli Hospital in Rome on 13 October 2026, and the Vatican said it confirmed a lung adenocarcinoma. Surgeons removed the lower lobe of his right lung, and the Vatican reported no complications.

Is the pope’s November trip still planned?

The trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru is scheduled for 6 to 17 November 2026, and no change had been announced in the sources we read. Whether it will change is not yet known.

Has the cancer spread?

That is not yet known. Further pathology tests are under way to determine whether the cancer spread beyond the removed lobe.

How long will the pope stay in hospital?

About one week of recovery in hospital is expected. All papal audiences are cancelled through 20 October.

World.title: Santiago Hailstorm Triggers Chile Red Alert
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

Chile declared a Red Alert for the Santiago Metropolitan Region on Tuesday, 13 October 2026, as an electrical storm hit the capital. Heavy rain and violent hail fell across the city, and the alert was in force by late afternoon.

About 36,000 customers had no power by 5 p.m., according to figures from the Superintendencia de Electricidad y Combustibles (SEC), Chile’s electricity and fuels superintendency. Metro de Santiago also closed several stations, and the reports we reviewed mention no injuries or deaths.

The storm matters to US travellers and residents in Santiago because Metro disruption affects daily movement across the city. It also follows the Las Condes mudslide earlier this month, which we reported on 8 October.

Key Facts —Who. Senapred, Chile’s national disaster prevention and response service, declared the alert. Residents, commuters and power customers across the capital are affected. —What. A Red Alert for an electrical storm with heavy rain and violent hail. It lets authorities mobilise all necessary and available resources. —Where. The Santiago Metropolitan Region, with flooding on main roads in Providencia, Ñuñoa, Las Condes and La Reina. About 36,000 customers lost power by 5 p.m. —When. Tuesday afternoon, 13 October 2026. More showers, hail and electrical storms are expected in the coming hours. —As of 13 October 2026, 20:40 GMT. Figures may change as the storm continues.

What We Know

Senapred, the national disaster prevention and response service, declared the Red Alert for the Metropolitan Region for a meteorological event on Tuesday afternoon. A red alert lets authorities mobilise all necessary and available resources.

Hail covered streets, and flooding hit main roads in eastern and central communes. Diario Financiero named Providencia, Ñuñoa, Las Condes and La Reina, while Megatiempo named Providencia, Ñuñoa and Vitacura.

La Tercera also named Quilicura, Lampa, La Reina and Peñalolén as affected. Communes are the local districts that make up the city and its surroundings.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Chile ranks 3rd of 14 with 63.6 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (86); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (38). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

About 36,000 customers had no electricity at 5 p.m. local time, based on SEC figures. Reported counts ranged from 36,155 to 36,928, and Diario Financiero later spoke of more than 40,000 homes.

The communes with the most outages were Quilicura, Quinta Normal, Providencia, Lampa, Pudahuel, Peñalolén, Colina, La Reina and Estación Central. Providencia and La Reina also saw flooding.

Metro de Santiago said some access points to its network closed because of the rain. Pedro de Valdivia station on Line 1 closed because of water accumulation, and Salvador station closed for entry.

Line 2 service was limited between Hospital El Pino and Franklin and between Los Héroes and Vespucio Norte. Salvador and Pedro de Valdivia stations are both on Line 1.

The Dirección Meteorológica de Chile, the national weather service, issued a strong weather alert for seven regions of central Chile. It runs from Tuesday afternoon into the evening and warns of heavy rain, instability and thunderstorms.

Sernageomin, the national geology service, rated landslide and debris flow risk in the Santiago foothills as moderate to high. Megatiempo meteorologist Catalina Cortés said intense showers, hail and electrical storms would continue for the coming hours.

Diario Financiero reported that the hail threatens farm output in the region. Megatiempo’s meteorologist said the storms could last until about 9 or 10 p.m.

Santiago’s Metropolitan Cathedral on the Plaza de Armas, in the capital where Senapred declared a Red Alert on 13 October 2026. (File photo)

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What Is Not Known

It is not yet known how long the storm will last. Total damage has not been counted.

The final outage count is unclear, and so is the time when power will return in full. The same applies to full Metro service.

Crop losses from the hail have not been measured. It is also unclear whether any injuries have occurred.

What It Means for Travelers and US Readers

Metro disruption is the clearest effect for visitors, with Pedro de Valdivia closed on Line 1 and limited service on parts of Line 2. Travellers should allow extra time for journeys across the city.

US residents and visitors in Santiago should follow guidance from Senapred and local authorities while the Red Alert stands. The alert covers the whole Metropolitan Region, not only the eastern communes.

The storm follows the Las Condes mudslide that swept cars through the commune on 8 October, as we reported in our first account. Chile declared Las Condes a disaster zone by 9 October with six people hurt, as we covered in our report on the declaration.

Classes were suspended in Las Condes schools after the mudslide, as we reported in our report on the closures. Our explainer on why Santiago flooding hits Las Condes and the foothills shows why the city’s eastern edge is exposed.

Chile is a major copper and fruit exporter, and Diario Financiero reported that the hail threatens farm output in the region. No wider economic effect has been confirmed.

The coming hours will show how long the storm lasts and how quickly power and Metro service return. Senapred and the national weather service remain the main sources for updates.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a Red Alert in Chile?

A Red Alert is declared by Senapred, Chile’s disaster agency, and lets authorities mobilise all necessary and available resources. Senapred declared one for the Santiago Metropolitan Region on 13 October 2026.

How many people lost power in Santiago?

About 36,000 customers were without electricity at 5 p.m. local time, based on SEC figures. Diario Financiero later spoke of more than 40,000 homes.

Is the Santiago Metro running?

Metro de Santiago has limited service because of the rain. Pedro de Valdivia station on Line 1 closed, Salvador station closed for entry, and Line 2 service was limited on two sections.

Were there any injuries?

The reports we reviewed mention no injuries or deaths. It is not yet known whether any occurred.

Sources Senapred · La Tercera · Diario Financiero · BioBioChile · Meganoticias · CNN Chile · Megatiempo · Superintendencia de Electricidad y Combustibles (SEC) · Dirección Meteorológica de Chile

World.title: Escondida Strike Deadline Hits Chile’s Top Copper Mine
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

CHILE · ECONOMY

Key Facts — What is happening BHP gave the supervisors’ union at Escondida in northern Chile, the world’s largest copper mine, a final offer of about US$28,700 (28 million pesos) per worker on Monday that expires on Tuesday, 13 October, Diario Financiero and Emol reported.

— Why it matters A stoppage at Escondida, Chile’s biggest single mine, would tighten supply of a strategic metal during a tense season that already includes a separate strike at Centinela and fatal accidents at Escondida and Codelco’s El Teniente.

— The numbers BHP’s offer totals about US$28,700 (28 million pesos) per worker, but the union counts only the US$25,600 (25 million pesos) in bonuses, since about US$3,100 (three million pesos) is a soft loan, Diario Financiero and Emol reported.

— Who is who BHP operates Escondida with partner Rio Tinto, while the Supervisors and Staff Union N°2, led by president Alexis Barrera, has about 1,020 members who backed a strike with about 95% of the vote, Diario Financiero and Redimin reported.

— What to watch Emol reported a strike would start with Wednesday’s first shift without a deal, though neither side has publicly confirmed that, and the two sides can instead agree to extend mediation before the labour directorate, which would delay any walkout.

— What it means for you Chile is the largest supplier of refined copper to the US, according to the US Geological Survey, and BHP and Rio Tinto both trade in New York, so a stoppage could tighten global supply and affect prices US buyers pay.

Supervisors at Escondida, the world’s largest copper mine, face a Tuesday deadline on BHP’s final contract offer. Their union says the headline payout of 28 million pesos per worker, about US$28,700, overstates what members would keep.

The Escondida strike threat in northern Chile reached its deadline on Tuesday, 13 October. The mine is a key source of copper for US wiring, cars and power grids.

Mine operator BHP gave its supervisors’ union a final offer on Monday that expires Tuesday, Diario Financiero and Emol reported. The union, which has about 1,020 members, says the 28 million pesos per worker, about US$28,700, overstates the real payout.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Chile ranks 3rd of 14 with 63.6 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (86); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (38). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What BHP Is Offering

Diario Financiero said 25 million pesos (about US$25,600) are bonuses and three million (about US$3,100) a soft loan. Emol, citing sources in the negotiation, described the same total as a bonus that includes a loan.

Both outlets also list a new holiday bonus of 1,500,000 pesos, about US$1,500. Staff living outside Antofagasta would get a monthly travel allowance of 350,000 pesos, about US$360.

The offer adds an education refund of 25 UF, Chile’s inflation-indexed unit of account, worth about US$1,050. Conversions in this article use 977.03 pesos per US dollar, the market rate late on 12 October 2026.

BHP also dropped a proposed 14×14 shift pattern and a multi-skilling incentive, Diario Financiero and Redimin reported. In a statement quoted by Emol, the company said its final offer improves pay, bonuses and benefits.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why the Union Says It Is Not Enough

Union president Alexis Barrera told Emol the end-of-negotiation bonus is 25 million pesos (about US$25,600), because the loans must be repaid. “The rest does not count for us because they are loans that the worker later has to repay,” he said.

Barrera said the union wants what other unions at the mine already have, such as a monthly production bonus. It also seeks a pay rise and changes to performance reviews, Emol reported.

Members backed a strike with about 95% of the vote late last month, Diario Financiero and Redimin reported. BHP then requested mediation before the labour directorate, which put any walkout on hold while talks continued.

A Tense Season in Chile’s Copper Belt

Workers at Antofagasta Minerals’ Centinela operation are holding a separate stoppage, which The Rio Times reported when it began. Talks at Centinela resumed this week, Emol and Diario Financiero said.

Safety is also a flashpoint after a fatal accident at Escondida last month, which supervisors say demands extraordinary inspections. State-owned Codelco confirmed on Sunday that two workers died in a slide at its El Teniente mine, the outlets reported.

What It Means for US Readers

Chile is the largest supplier of refined copper to the United States, according to the US Geological Survey. Escondida is the country’s biggest single mine, so a stoppage there would tighten supply of a strategic metal.

BHP and its Escondida partner Rio Tinto both have shares traded in New York. US investors therefore have direct exposure, although BHP has not said how it would run the mine during a strike.

Copper goes into homes, data centres, electric vehicles and defence equipment, and US buyers pay global exchange prices. Washington largely exempted refined copper cathodes from its 2025 copper tariffs, which keeps Chilean metal central to US supply.

What Is Not Known

It was not known at publication whether the union accepted the offer, rejected it or agreed to extend mediation. Emol reported a stoppage would start with Wednesday’s first shift without a deal, but neither side has publicly confirmed that.

BHP has not said how much output a strike could affect or what contingency staffing it would use. Figures cited by only one outlet, such as the estimated cost of union demands, are left out here.

What Comes Next

Chilean labour rules let the two sides extend mediation by mutual agreement, Diario Financiero noted, which would delay any walkout. If no deal is signed and no extension is agreed, the union can begin its strike.

BHP has said it hopes to close mediation with an agreement. The union says it will keep pressing for a production bonus, and other copper unions in Chile are watching.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Escondida?

Escondida is an open-pit mine in Chile’s Antofagasta Region, operated by BHP and described as the world’s largest copper mine. It is a major source of Chile’s copper exports.

Who is threatening to strike?

The Supervisors and Staff Union N°2 at Escondida, which has about 1,020 members, voted for a strike last month. The walkout has been on hold during mediation requested by BHP.

How much is BHP offering?

BHP’s final offer totals 28 million pesos per worker, about US$28,700, including three million pesos (about US$3,100) as a soft loan. The union counts only the 25 million pesos in bonuses, about US$25,600.

Why does it matter to the United States?

Chile is the largest supplier of refined copper to the United States, according to the US Geological Survey. A stoppage at its biggest mine could tighten global supply and affect prices.

When could a strike start?

Emol reported that a strike would begin with Wednesday’s first shift if no deal is reached. The two sides can also agree to extend mediation, which would delay any walkout.

Sources: Diario Financiero (12 October); Emol (13 October); Diario Financiero (5 October); Redimin; US Geological Survey (all accessed 13 October 2026).

World.title: Paraguay Vice President Defies Cartes on 13 October
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

PARAGUAY · POLITICS

Key Facts — What is happening Paraguay’s Vice President Pedro Alliana told ABC Color on Tuesday, 13 October, that his 2028 presidential bid “remains firm,” after ABC Color and Última Hora reported that Horacio Cartes favours minister Juan Carlos Baruja instead.

— Why it matters The quarrel opens a rift inside the ruling Colorado Party, which defends Paraguay’s recognition of Taiwan rather than China, a tie Washington watches as it competes with Beijing for influence in South America.

— The numbers Cartes was president from 2013 to 2018, the US Treasury sanctioned him for corruption on 26 January 2023 and lifted the sanctions on 6 October 2025, and the next general election is due in 2028.

— Who is who Alliana is vice president; Cartes, a former president and businessman, chairs the Colorado Party and built its Honor Colorado faction; Baruja is housing minister; Santiago Peña, a Colorado economist, has been president since August 2023.

— What to watch Alliana will consult party leaders and commission polls before deciding his next steps after the end of the year, while Colorado governors seek talks with Cartes, Alliana and Peña; Cartes has not publicly confirmed any preference.

— What it means for you Nothing changes soon for US travellers and businesses, since Peña’s term runs until August 2028, but banks and investors with ties to Cartes’s business group follow any shift in his influence.

Paraguay’s vice president, Pedro Alliana, said on Tuesday, 13 October, that he will not abandon his bid for the presidency. He spoke after reports that Horacio Cartes, the ruling party’s most powerful figure, now favours a cabinet minister instead.

The Paraguay vice president told the Asunción daily ABC Color on Tuesday that he will not quit the race for 2028. He said he had heard a great deal of noise about Cartes backing someone else, but nothing official.

Cartes, a former president once sanctioned by the US Treasury for corruption, chairs the ruling Colorado Party. The rift matters beyond Paraguay because the country is one of the few that recognise Taiwan rather than China.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Paraguay ranks 10th of 14 with 36.0 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (55); weakest: future resources (13). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What Alliana Said on Tuesday

ABC Color and Última Hora both reported that Cartes favours Juan Carlos Baruja, the minister of urbanism, housing and habitat. Alliana told ABC Color that officially he had received nothing, only “a lot of noise.”

Asked whether he would give up his ambitions, the Paraguay vice president answered with a string of firm refusals. “My candidacy remains firm,” he said, according to the paper.

He said he would first consult party leaders and commission polls, then decide on next steps after the end of the year. He added that he would not launch “an adventure” without the support of the party’s leadership.

Alliana also said he had spoken briefly with President Santiago Peña after Peña met Cartes. Peña, a Colorado economist who took office in August 2023, laughed at the news and invited him to talk, Alliana said.

The vice president said he was still weighing possible running mates. He also said loyalty to Cartes should not be confused with blind obedience.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Paraguay politics Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Allies Line Up Behind the Vice President

Raúl Latorre, president of the Chamber of Deputies, reaffirmed his public commitment to Alliana’s candidacy on Tuesday, both papers reported. He told Última Hora that the biggest tensions of the Asunción municipal campaign came from inside Honor Colorado itself.

Honor Colorado is the faction Cartes built inside the Colorado Party, and Peña won the presidency as its candidate. Latorre said he knew Peña and Cartes had met but lacked details of what they discussed.

Latorre praised Cartes for returning the party to power and described the faction as a family. “It is natural for the children to grow,” he said, adding that any split would be assessed if it came.

Última Hora also reported that César Sosa, governor of Guairá, pledged the Colorado governors’ support for Alliana after a council meeting. Sosa said the governors would seek talks with Cartes, Alliana and Peña that afternoon.

Sosa called Baruja “a great colleague” and wished him luck if he becomes the choice. The tone suggests the governors want to back Alliana without an open break with Cartes.

Why Horacio Cartes Matters to Washington

Cartes, a businessman whose group includes tobacco firms, was Paraguay’s president from 2013 to 2018. On 26 January 2023, the US Treasury sanctioned him for corruption and also designated four companies it said he owned or controlled.

The Treasury cited alleged monthly cash payments to loyal legislators and money used to buy votes for a constitutional reform. It said he kept influencing lawmakers after leaving office.

The Treasury removed Cartes and those companies from its sanctions list on 6 October 2025, OFAC records show. His lawyer, Pedro Ovelar, told Última Hora in July 2026 that a separate State Department “significantly corrupt” label had also been lifted.

That history explains why his role in choosing Paraguay’s next president draws attention in Washington. It also means any shift in his influence is followed by banks and investors with ties to his business group.

What It Means for US Readers

Paraguay recognises Taiwan rather than China, and its ruling Colorado Party has defended that tie. A split in that party matters to Washington, which competes with Beijing for influence in South America.

For investors, the dispute is about who leads the party, not economic policy, since all the rivals belong to the governing camp. No change of government is imminent, because the next general election is due in 2028.

For US travellers and businesses, nothing changes in the short term. Peña’s five-year term runs until August 2028, and the party quarrel does not affect his government’s authority.

What Is Not Known

Cartes has not publicly confirmed that he prefers Baruja, and Baruja has not announced a candidacy. Alliana himself said nothing official had reached him.

What Peña and Cartes discussed at their meeting has not been disclosed. The number of governors backing Alliana was given by only one outlet and is not confirmed by an official statement.

The State Department has not publicly confirmed his lawyer’s claim that its corruption designation was lifted. No US government statement on the dispute has been issued.

What Comes Next

Alliana said he would weigh polls and decide on his next steps after the end of the year. The governors said they would seek talks with Cartes, Alliana and Peña to keep the party together.

The dispute does not mean the Colorado Party has formally split or that the government faces a crisis. The date of the party’s primaries for 2028 was not given in Tuesday’s reports.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Pedro Alliana?

Pedro Alliana is Paraguay’s vice president, elected alongside President Santiago Peña in 2023. He wants to be the Colorado Party’s presidential candidate in 2028.

Who is Horacio Cartes?

Horacio Cartes is a businessman who was Paraguay’s president from 2013 to 2018 and now chairs the Colorado Party. The US Treasury sanctioned him for corruption in January 2023 and lifted the sanctions in October 2025.

Who is Juan Carlos Baruja?

Juan Carlos Baruja is Paraguay’s minister of urbanism, housing and habitat. Local reports say Cartes favours him as the ruling faction’s presidential candidate.

Are US sanctions on Cartes still in force?

No, the US Treasury removed Cartes from its sanctions list on 6 October 2025. His lawyer says a separate State Department corruption designation was also lifted, which Washington has not publicly confirmed.

When is Paraguay’s next presidential election?

Paraguay holds its next general election in 2028. President Peña cannot run again because the constitution limits presidents to a single term.

Sources: US Department of the Treasury, press release of 26 January 2023; ABC Color, Alliana interview; ABC Color, Latorre; Última Hora, Latorre; Última Hora, governors; OFAC, SDN list removals of 6 October 2025; Última Hora, Ovelar, July 2026 (all accessed 13 October 2026).

World.title: IMF Projects El Salvador Economy to Grow 4.5% This Year
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

EL SALVADOR · ECONOMY

Key Facts — What is happening On Tuesday, 13 October, the International Monetary Fund’s October World Economic Outlook projected El Salvador’s economy to grow 4.5% in 2026, up from an estimated 3.9% in 2025 and faster than any year from 2022 to 2025.

— Why it matters El Salvador uses the US dollar and has no currency of its own, so its growth is tied to US interest rates, jobs and remittances, and the forecast is among the strongest in Central America.

— The numbers The IMF sees growth easing to 4.0% in 2027, inflation of 2.7% in 2026 after about 0.3% in 2025, and gross government debt at 85% of output this year, rising to about 89% in 2027.

— Who is who The IMF lends to President Nayib Bukele’s government under a 40 month programme worth about US$1.4 billion, approved in February 2025, and released a further US$138 million earlier this month; businesses no longer have to accept Bitcoin.

— What to watch IMF staff reviews under the loan programme, each tied to further payments, and quarterly output data from the central bank, the Banco Central de Reserva, will show whether growth is on track, while lawmakers weigh the 2027 budget.

— What it means for you For US investors, a dollarised economy removes currency risk though high debt carries a cost, and stronger growth can ease migration pressure and lift demand for US goods sold under the Central America and Dominican Republic free trade agreement.

The International Monetary Fund’s new global outlook projects El Salvador’s economy to grow 4.5% in 2026. That would beat every year from 2022 to 2025 in the Fund’s figures, in a country that uses the US dollar.

The IMF projected 4.5% growth for El Salvador this year in its October World Economic Outlook, released on Tuesday, 13 October. The figure appears in the Fund’s World Economic Outlook database, published during its annual meetings in Bangkok.

El Salvador adopted the US dollar as legal tender in 2001 and has no currency of its own. That ties its economy closely to US interest rates, US jobs and the money Salvadorans in the United States send home.

What the October Outlook Shows

The Fund puts El Salvador’s real output growth at 4.5% in 2026, up from an estimated 3.9% in 2025. Growth is then seen easing to 4.0% in 2027 and to about 3.3% a year from 2028 in the same database.

The new figure marks a clear step up from recent years. The IMF’s series shows growth of 2.9% in 2022, 3.4% in 2023 and 2.6% in 2024.

The 2026 estimate is among the strongest in Central America in the same report. The Fund projects 4.0% growth for Guatemala and 3.3% each for Honduras and Costa Rica, while Panama is seen growing 5.0%.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on El Salvador economy Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Prices, Jobs and Debt

Consumer prices are expected to rise faster than last year but remain low. The IMF sees average inflation of 2.7% in 2026, after about 0.3% in 2025.

The unemployment rate is projected at 4.3% this year, close to the 4.2% estimated for 2025. On the Fund’s numbers, joblessness then drifts up slowly to 4.8% by 2030.

Public debt remains the heaviest weight on the outlook. The Fund estimates gross government debt at 85% of economic output in 2026, before a rise to about 89% in 2027.

The IMF Loan Programme and Bitcoin

El Salvador is in the middle of a 40-month loan programme with the IMF worth about US$1.4 billion, approved in February 2025. The deal ties each payment to targets on the budget, public debt and financial transparency.

The Fund’s board released a further US$138 million under the programme earlier this month. Under the deal, businesses no longer have to accept Bitcoin, though the state keeps adding it to reserves.

A Dollar Economy Tied to the United States

Because El Salvador uses the dollar, it cannot devalue to boost exports or set its own interest rates. Its borrowing costs and spending power therefore move with decisions taken by the US Federal Reserve.

The United States is El Salvador’s largest trading partner and home to a large Salvadoran diaspora. Money sent home by workers in the US is one of the country’s biggest sources of income and supports household spending.

Security has also changed the investment picture under President Nayib Bukele. His government credits mass arrests of alleged gang members for a sharp fall in homicides, while rights groups criticise the detentions.

What It Means for US Readers

A 4.5% forecast points to a faster-growing partner in Central America, a region close to US supply chains and migration routes. For US investors, a dollarised economy removes currency risk, although high public debt still carries a cost.

Stronger growth at home can ease some of the economic pressure that pushes Salvadorans to migrate north. It can also lift demand for US goods sold under the Central America and Dominican Republic free trade agreement with Washington.

What Is Not Known

The IMF database does not publish a written explanation for El Salvador’s 4.5% figure. It is not clear which assumptions on remittances, tourism, public investment or US demand drive the estimate.

The Fund’s April forecast could not be checked at the source on Tuesday, so no comparison is made here. The government’s own 2026 estimate and any official reaction were not available at the time of writing.

What Comes Next

IMF staff will keep reviewing El Salvador’s progress under the loan programme, with each review tied to further payments. Quarterly output data from the central bank, the Banco Central de Reserva, will show whether the economy is on track.

Lawmakers are also weighing the government’s budget bill for 2027. A projection is not a guarantee, and actual growth will depend on US demand, remittance flows and the global economy.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does El Salvador use the US dollar?

Yes, El Salvador adopted the US dollar as legal tender in 2001 and has no national currency. Bitcoin was added as legal tender in 2021, but a 2025 reform ended the obligation for businesses to accept it.

What growth does the IMF forecast for El Salvador?

The IMF’s October outlook projects El Salvador’s economy to grow 4.5% in 2026. It sees growth slowing to 4.0% in 2027.

What inflation does the IMF expect?

The Fund projects average consumer price inflation of 2.7% in 2026. That compares with about 0.3% in 2025.

Why does this matter for the United States?

El Salvador is a dollarised economy closely linked to US trade, investment and remittances. Its growth affects migration pressure and demand for American goods in Central America.

Is El Salvador’s public debt a concern?

The IMF estimates gross government debt at about 85% of economic output this year. That level is high for an emerging economy and is a core focus of the IMF loan programme.

Sources: IMF World Economic Outlook database, El Salvador; IMF World Economic Outlook, October 2026; Banco Central de Reserva de El Salvador (all accessed 13 October 2026).

World.title: Panama Jails 3 Foreigners Over 1.8 Tonnes of Cocaine
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

PANAMA · SECURITY

Key Facts — What is happening On Monday, 12 October, Panama’s Judicial Branch announced that a judge in Chiriquí province sentenced three foreign men to 12 years in prison for international drug trafficking after their boat was stopped carrying about 1.8 tonnes of cocaine.

— Why it matters Panama’s Pacific coast lies on sea routes carrying South American cocaine north, and the plea deal produced a sentence within five days of the seizure, though the cargo’s destination was not disclosed.

— The numbers Officers found 1,513 packages weighing 1,803,850 grams, about 1.8 tonnes or close to 4,000 pounds, the Judicial Branch said; the men are aged 42, 43 and 48, and no official estimate of the cargo’s value has been published.

— Who is who Guarantees judge Víctor Serrano validated a plea agreement between the defence and prosecutor Daniel Montenegro of the Public Ministry; the National Aeronaval Service (SENAN), Panama’s combined coast guard and air patrol force, intercepted the boat off Punta Burica on Wednesday, 7 October.

— What to watch The judiciary has not named the men or given their nationalities, and it is not known whether prosecutors are seeking further suspects or who sent or ordered the cargo; the boat and its equipment will be forfeited.

— What it means for you The United States is one of the largest markets for South American cocaine, though no US role in this case was reported; for Americans in Chiriquí, including retirees around Boquete, daily life is unchanged.

A court in western Panama has sent three foreign men to prison for 12 years over a large cocaine shipment. The judiciary announced the sentence five days after the boat was stopped at sea.

Three foreign nationals got 12 years in prison in Panama after their cocaine boat was stopped near Costa Rica. Panama’s Judicial Branch announced the ruling on Monday, 12 October, saying the men had accepted a plea agreement.

The boat carried 1,513 packages holding about 1.8 tonnes of cocaine, the judiciary said. For US readers, Panama’s Pacific coast lies on sea routes carrying South American cocaine north, but this cargo’s destination is unknown.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Panama ranks 11th of 14 with 34.2 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (64); weakest: military means (11). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What the Court Decided

Guarantees judge Víctor Serrano, who sits in Chiriquí province, validated a plea agreement reached between prosecutors and the defence. Under Sentence No. 674, he found the three men criminally responsible for international drug trafficking.

The men are aged 42, 43 and 48, the Judicial Branch said, without giving their names or nationalities. Panamanian law treats international drug trafficking as a crime against collective security, a category that carries long prison terms.

Prosecutor Daniel Montenegro represented the Public Ministry, Panama’s national prosecution service. Three public defenders represented the defendants at a hearing held under the accusatory system, the oral trial model Panama now uses.

At the prosecution’s request, the judge also ordered the forfeiture of the boat, its three outboard motors and its fuel tanks. Satellite communication equipment and other items found on board are covered by the same order.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

How the Cocaine Boat Was Stopped

Units of the National Aeronaval Service, Panama’s combined coast guard and air patrol force, intercepted the vessel on Wednesday, 7 October. The interception took place off Punta Burica, a peninsula in Barú district that Panama shares with Costa Rica.

Officers found 1,513 rectangular packages on board, according to the Judicial Branch. Once weighed, the drugs came to 1,803,850 grams of cocaine, or roughly 1.8 metric tonnes.

That is close to 4,000 pounds, about the weight of a large family car. TVN Panamá, a national broadcaster, reported the same figures, the sentence and the boat’s equipment, citing the judiciary.

A Remote Coast Next to Costa Rica

Punta Burica lies at the western tip of Panama’s Pacific coast, where the land border with Costa Rica reaches the sea. The area is thinly populated and far from Panama City, which makes patrols at sea the main line of control.

The nearest town of any size is Puerto Armuelles, a Pacific port town in Barú district. Chiriquí province, which includes the area, is better known abroad for its coffee farms and the highland town of Boquete.

The ruling came as Panama recovers from the earthquake of Friday, 9 October, which damaged homes, schools and clinics in several provinces. On 12 October, the Supreme Court kept court deadlines and work suspended in the provinces affected by the quake.

What It Means for US Readers

The United States is one of the largest consumer markets for South American cocaine. Much of that cocaine moves north by sea along Central America’s Pacific coast, but this cargo’s destination was not disclosed.

Panama is a long-standing US partner on drug interdiction at sea, though no US role in this case has been reported. The plea deal also produced a sentence within five days of the seizure.

For Americans living in or visiting Chiriquí, including the many retirees around Boquete, the case does not change daily life. The interception happened at sea off a remote peninsula, far from the main towns and tourist areas.

What Is Not Known

The Judicial Branch did not name the three men or give their nationalities. It also did not say where the boat set off from or where the cocaine was headed.

No official has said whether the crew belonged to a wider trafficking network or whether foreign agencies took part. The exact date of the plea hearing was not stated in the judiciary’s announcement.

No official estimate of the cargo’s value has been published. It is also not known whether prosecutors are seeking further suspects in the case.

What Comes Next

The three men face 12 years in prison, and the state will take the boat and equipment afterwards. In a plea agreement, defendants accept responsibility and a negotiated penalty instead of a full trial.

The sentence settles the case for these three men only. It does not mean that any inquiry into who sent or ordered the cargo is over.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did the Panama court decide?

A guarantees judge in Chiriquí sentenced three foreign men to 12 years in prison for international drug trafficking. He also ordered the forfeiture of their boat and equipment.

How much cocaine was on the boat?

Officers found 1,513 packages weighing 1,803,850 grams, or about 1.8 tonnes. The National Aeronaval Service intercepted the boat on 7 October.

Where is Punta Burica?

Punta Burica is a peninsula at the western end of Panama’s Pacific coast, in Barú district. Panama shares the peninsula with Costa Rica.

What is the National Aeronaval Service?

It is Panama’s combined coast guard and air patrol force, known by its Spanish initials SENAN. It patrols the country’s seas and airspace, including against drug trafficking.

Why does this matter to the United States?

The United States is one of the largest markets for South American cocaine. Seizures in Panamanian waters target routes that often lead north, though this cargo’s destination was not disclosed.

Sources: Órgano Judicial de Panamá; Corte Suprema de Justicia, communiqué of 12 October; TVN Panamá (all accessed 13 October 2026).

World.title: ICE Sent Two Costa Rican Children to a Texas Family Detention Center
World.content:
Two Costa Rican children, a 9-year-old and an 11-year-old, were picked up by U.S. immigration agents late at night near New Orleans at the end of July and driven about 900 kilometers (560 miles) to a family detention center in South Texas, according to U.S. government records made public by a university research project.

The information comes from the Deportation Data Project, run by researchers at the University of California, Berkeley, and the University of California, Los Angeles. The project obtains arrest and detention records from U.S. agencies and publishes them online. According to those records, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) took the 11-year-old into custody at 10:34 p.m. on Friday, July 31, in Kenner, a suburb of New Orleans, Louisiana. The 9-year-old was picked up in the same city.

The records list the younger child’s arrest at 4:46 a.m. on Aug. 1, but they also show that child being booked in at 11:46 p.m. the night before, so the exact time is unclear. Both children were first taken to a temporary ICE holding room in St. Rose, Louisiana. At 10:26 a.m. on Aug. 1, they were put on the road to the South Texas Family Residential Center in Dilley. They arrived at 10:38 p.m., about 12 hours later.

The children are not named in the records, and the records do not say whether a parent or guardian was with them. The Dilley center is built to hold families together. As of Aug. 5, the latest date in the data, both cases were still open. ICE classified the children as inadmissible, a legal label for people U.S. authorities say were not lawfully admitted to the United States, and their cases were waiting to go before an immigration judge.

The records also list both children under ICE’s Alternatives to Detention program, which usually lets people stay out of custody while their cases move forward, often with check-ins or electronic monitoring. The data does not explain why children being held at Dilley carry that label.

Across all ages in the records, most detention stays with that label ended with the person deported or leaving the United States voluntarily. A smaller share ended with a release. The Dilley center can hold about 2,400 people and has faced lawsuits and repeated complaints. A joint report by Human Rights First and RAICES, a Texas legal aid group, accused the facility of denying people a fair legal process and holding them in inhumane conditions.

Families held there say they have been kept far longer than 20 days, the limit for children set by a long-standing U.S. court agreement known as the Flores settlement. Lawyers and advocates have also reported insects, spoiled or moldy food, and staff taking away children’s drawings that showed sadness.

Records released by the office of U.S. Sen. Dick Durbin, an Illinois Democrat, describe delays in medical care, along with emergency calls for young children and babies having seizures or trouble breathing. ICE denies that conditions are poor. The agency says Dilley is a family center designed to keep families safe, with medical checkups, baby supplies, classrooms and play areas.

The two children are among 41 Costa Rican minors picked up by ICE between October 2022 and Aug. 5, 2026, according to the same records. Twenty-four were girls and 17 were boys, ranging from babies to 16-year-olds, and 33 were younger than 12. Of those 41, five left the United States for Costa Rica and five were released inside the country. The two children sent to Dilley were the only ones recorded as being held in detention.

The other 29 had no record of being detained or leaving the United States, and most of them still had an open immigration case. Across all nationalities, the records show 31,481 arrests involving people under 18 in the same period. That figure counts arrests rather than individual children, because the same child can be arrested more than once. Nearly four in 10 of those cases, 38.5%, involved children estimated to be between 4 and 9 years old.

Here at home, the case adds to mounting questions about how Costa Ricans are treated in U.S. immigration custody. In September, the Foreign Ministry said 77 Costa Ricans were being held by ICE and estimated that around 250 had been detained between January and September this year.

Those figures came shortly after a Costa Rican social media influencer was released from ICE custody in Florida. Costa Rica’s Ombudsman’s Office has since asked the Foreign Ministry to explain how it checks on detention conditions for Costa Ricans held by ICE, how it makes sure they can reach Costa Rican consular staff, and how it identifies people who need extra protection, such as children who depend on an adult.

The request came after the death of a second Costa Rican in ICE detention, and as Costa Rica takes on a growing role in the U.S. deportation program. The records only run through early August and are updated from time to time. Because the data counts arrests rather than people, the published figures cannot show where the two children are today, or what happened to most of the 41 Costa Rican minors.

World.title: Benjamin Garcia fined $3,005 after pleading guilty to discharging firearm in public; Charge against Mexican businessman Sergio Ramirez withdrawn
World.content:
Benjamin Garcia fined $3,005 after pleading guilty to discharging firearm in public; Charge against Mexican businessman Sergio Ramirez withdrawn

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Social media influencer and marketing consultant Benjamin Eduardo Garcia, 27, escaped a prison sentence on Tuesday after pleading guilty to discharging a firearm in public following a shooting incident outside Social Lounge on the Philip Goldson Highway over the weekend.

Garcia, a resident of Belama Phase 2, was fined $3,000 plus $5 in court costs following proceedings in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court. He has until November 30, 2026, to pay the fine or face two years in prison.

His co-accused, 36-year-old Mexican businessman Sergio Martinez Ramirez, walked free after the prosecution withdrew the charge against him. Ramirez maintained that he was innocent and had simply found himself in the wrong place at the wrong time.

Both men were represented by prominent attorney Richard “Dickie” Bradley, who told the court that Garcia was a first-time offender who had cooperated with police and admitted responsibility for discharging his licensed firearm.

In imposing the fine, the magistrate considered Garcia’s early guilty plea, his lack of previous convictions for a similar offence, and the fact that the firearm was legally licensed.

Garcia was also required to settle an outstanding court fine of $560 before leaving the courthouse, which he paid.

The charges stemmed from an incident around 1:35 a.m. on Saturday, October 10, when police conducting checks at Social Lounge observed a grey Ford F-250 pickup leaving the compound. According to the facts presented in court, a police officer witnessed the front passenger window being lowered before a black object was extended outside. The officer reported seeing sparks coming from the object, followed by four loud bangs consistent with gunshots. The area was illuminated by streetlights, allowing the officer to identify the same pickup that had just left the establishment.

Police pursued the vehicle and intercepted it near the Pallotti roundabout. Garcia subsequently disclosed that he possessed a licensed 9mm pistol, which officers recovered along with 12 live rounds. Four expended shells were also recovered from the shooting scene.

As previously reported by Breaking Belize News, both men were formally charged on Sunday following conflicting reports about Garcia’s detention and possible release.

The case attracted public attention because of Garcia’s publicly reported association with newly appointed Minister of National Security Michel Chebat. However, there has been no verified evidence of ministerial interference in the investigation.

Outside court, Martinez Ramirez described himself as an honest businessman who had been caught up in an unfortunate situation, reiterating that he had no involvement in the shooting.

World.title: International News: Taiwan warns Europe against overdependence on China
World.content:
International News: Taiwan warns Europe against overdependence on China

By Zoila Palma: Taiwan’s Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung has warned European countries that excessive dependence on Chinese suppliers could threaten their economic security, freedom and sovereignty, Reuters report.

Speaking at an event today, Lin urged Europe to strengthen its ties with Taiwan ahead of a European Union summit where trade relations with Beijing are expected to be a major topic of discussion.

“Because China’s authoritarian ideology is fundamentally incompatible with Europe’s democracy, dependence on China is not merely an economic risk, it’s a threat to European freedom and sovereignty itself,” Lin said.

He also cautioned that reliance on Chinese supply chains could undermine Europe’s independence, stating, “A Europe controlled through its supply chains would be a Europe that had surrendered part of its liberty.” EU leaders are expected to discuss ways to address the bloc’s trade deficit with China and reduce reliance on Beijing in sensitive sectors.

Lin emphasized that closer cooperation with Taiwan could benefit Europe economically and technologically, highlighting shared democratic values and opportunities for innovation. “Taiwan and Europe share the values that matter most – democracy, freedom, human rights and the rule of law,” he said. He added, “The Taiwan model has helped power innovation and prosperity in Silicon Valley, and it can do the same for Europe too.”

Taiwan has increasingly pursued stronger relationships with European countries, particularly since Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, as European governments also raise concerns about trade imbalances and China’s perceived support for Moscow.

World.title: International News: Pope Leo XIV diagnosed with lung cancer following surgery
World.content:
International News: Pope Leo XIV diagnosed with lung cancer following surgery

By Zoila Palma: Pope Leo XIV has been diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma after undergoing surgery to remove the lower lobe of his right lung, the Vatican announced.

The diagnosis was confirmed during the operation today after preoperative tests raised concerns about a lung nodule. The 71-year-old pontiff’s diagnosis marks the first publicly disclosed major health issue of his papacy.

According to a Vatican medical bulletin, the surgery was successful, with doctors reporting no complications. The procedure lasted approximately 90 minutes, while the pope spent about three hours in the operating room before returning to his room at Rome’s Gemelli hospital. The Vatican described the removal as “radical,” indicating that the affected portion of the lung and the suspected cancerous tissue were removed.

The Vatican has not announced what treatment, if any, the pope will require next.

Doctors are awaiting additional test results, including information that could establish whether the cancer has spread to the lymph nodes.

Pope Leo had publicly disclosed the discovery of a lung nodule during his Sunday noon prayer and said he would undergo a procedure to have it removed.

The Vatican subsequently cancelled his scheduled audiences through October 20 as he recovers.

World.title: TIDE Conservation Festival 2026 concludes with fishing tournaments and community competitions
World.content:
TIDE Conservation Festival 2026 concludes with fishing tournaments and community competitions

By Zoila Palma: The Toledo Institute for Development and Environment (TIDE) wrapped up its 2026 Conservation Festival on October 11 with a day of fishing tournaments, kayaking races, volleyball matches and traditional games along the Caribbean coast. The four-day celebration brought together fishers, volunteers and community members to promote local culture, community participation and the importance of protecting Belize’s natural resources.

The festival’s annual Fish Festival attracted 21 boats competing in fishing tournaments at the Port Honduras Marine Reserve and Sapodilla Cayes Marine Reserve. At Port Honduras, G Muerel secured first place with a 22-pound fish, while Mohack placed second in the category for the three largest different fish by weight, totalling 31 pounds.

AllPro Wave Ride took third place in the largest jack category. At Sapodilla Cayes, J Sparrow claimed first place with a 30-pound fish, followed by Laruni, whose three largest different fish weighed a combined 36 pounds. D Process placed third with a 12-pound unique fish.

Kayaking competitions also featured prominently, with Diane Alford and Dilcy Williams placing first and second in the adult female category, while George Alford Jr., Edwin Cabrera Jr. and Yazelle Choco took the top three positions in the youth race. James Alford won the adult male kayak race, followed by Jonathan Alford and Mark Lino. In the volleyball tournaments, Wakanda Kings, Challengers and Elites placed first, second and third, respectively, in the male division. D-Gala 1 claimed first place in the female division, followed by D-Gala 2 and Panthers.

Traditional competitions added to the festivities, with Moses Varro winning the hudut eating contest, Derony Williams taking the lime and spoon race, and Melisa Lopez winning the watermelon eating contest. Jauden Choco won the corn husking contest, Joe Myvette claimed the coconut husking competition, and Mynor Perez emerged victorious in the cast net competition. James Alford won the greasy pole grand prize and first station prize, while Zane Cacho secured the second station prize.

TIDE thanked the volunteers, sponsors, organizers, fishers and community members who contributed to the festival’s success.

World.title: Mayor Trapp challenges Habet’s claims on El Cayo Boardwalk Kiosk agreements
World.content:
Mayor Trapp challenges Habet’s claims on El Cayo Boardwalk Kiosk agreements

By Zoila Palma: San Ignacio and Santa Elena Mayor Earl Trapp has responded to comments made by Cayo Northeast Area Representative Orlando Habet regarding the El Cayo Boardwalk, questioning the authority under which kiosk rental agreements were signed and calling for consultation with the town council.

The exchange follows Habet’s statement outlining the boardwalk project and its potential to support small businesses and community activities.

Habet said there are four kiosks available for rental and claimed that prospective tenants had already signed agreements but were unable to begin operating because the town council refused to issue them trade licences.

He stated that “rental agreements have already been signed with different prospective tenants,” adding that the individuals had been unable to proceed despite their willingness to invest in businesses at the site.

Habet explained that the kiosks were designed for small businesses operating under a pop-up shop concept, offering products such as coffee, smoothies, desserts, souvenirs and locally made arts and crafts.

The area representative also defended the boardwalk’s value beyond its commercial potential, pointing to community events and recreational activities held at the location. Habet said the facility had hosted movie nights, Christmas celebrations, Mother’s Day programmes and gatherings during the annual La Ruta Maya Belize River Challenge, as well as a recent free yoga session.

He acknowledged that “there is still work to be done,” but maintained that the boardwalk was already serving the community. He further stated that the project’s success should not be defined by political differences, but by the opportunities it creates for residents and entrepreneurs.

But, Mayor Trapp questioned how rental agreements could have been executed without consultation with the elected municipal government.

He asked, “Who authorized these agreements, what legal authority was relied upon, and what role, if any, was afforded to the San Ignacio and Santa Elena Town Council before commitments were made to third parties?” Trapp also raised questions about who would manage the agreements, collect rental fees and assume responsibility for potential damage to infrastructure or loss of life during a natural disaster. He said the public deserves clarity regarding the ownership and administrative control of the land and facilities.

Trapp further raised environmental and operational concerns about the kiosks’ location near the river in an area known to experience frequent flooding. The mayor said the council needs information on waste collection and disposal, wastewater management, flood-related risks and safeguards to protect the river and public health.

He stressed that the council’s position was not opposition to development, stating, “Our position is not opposition to development. It is a demand for development that respects municipal governance, protects the environment, and serves the long-term interests of our residents.” He also warned against political committees assuming municipal management functions outside the proper legal and institutional framework.

The mayor called for disclosure of the legal basis for the rental agreements, clarification of the parties involved and any approvals obtained, a review of environmental safeguards, and a clear understanding of the respective responsibilities of the ministry and the town council.

Trapp said the council is willing to meet with Habet and the relevant authorities to resolve the outstanding issues, emphasizing that “dialogue must be accompanied by transparency, accountability, and respect for the institutions entrusted with serving our people.”

World.title: Super El Niño strengthens to unprecedented levels, setting new Ocean temperature records
World.content:
Super El Niño strengthens to unprecedented levels, setting new Ocean temperature records

By Zoila Palma: El Niño has continued to strengthen to what some scientists are describing as “unprecedented levels,” with several key ocean temperature measurements reaching record territory weeks before the phenomenon is expected to peak in December.

The Australian Bureau of Meteorology (BOM) reported that average weekly sea-surface temperatures in the central Pacific have reached their highest levels in its available records.

The latest development follows a new record for daily sea-surface temperatures in the central-eastern Pacific in September, surpassing the previous record set during the powerful 2015 El Niño. Temperatures exceeding 30 degrees Celsius have also been recorded for the first time in parts of the tropical Pacific, alongside exceptional subsurface warmth and record sea-surface temperature anomalies.

El Niño is a naturally occurring climate pattern that develops approximately every two to seven years and typically lasts around a year. However, scientists say long-term ocean warming caused by human-induced climate change is adding to the current temperature records.

The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) has noted that there is currently no evidence that climate change is making El Niño events stronger or more frequent, although the relationship remains an area of scientific research.

The strengthening El Niño is expected to contribute to unusually high global temperatures through 2026 and into 2027, as the phenomenon releases additional heat from the oceans into the atmosphere.

The WMO has reported drought- and flood-related disruptions in several regions, raising concerns about food security in parts of East Africa and the Asia-Pacific.

However, scientists caution that the severity of El Niño’s impacts varies by location and that no two events are exactly alike.

World.title: JC booted from Walker Cup for fielding ineligible player Jamone Lyle
World.content:
Jamaica College forward Jamone Lyle (third left) gets away from St Catherine High School’s Caiden Yen (on ground) while his teammates Jaquan Brown and Davill Jarrett (right) look on during their ISSA Manning Cup game at Ashenheim Stadium in St Andrew on Wednesday. (Photo: Naphtali Junior)

Jamaica College (JC) have been booted from the Walker Cup for fielding an ineligible player, bringing their championship hopes crashing down just days before a highly anticipated final showdown against rivals Kingston College (KC).

Additionally, the ‘True Blues’ have been banned from next year’s edition of the knockout tournament, and must forfeit the Manning Cup second round match against St Catherine which they had won 3 – 2, which means the result has been reversed to hand St Catherine a 3 – 0 win over the many-time champions.

The decision was made at an ISSA emergency meeting on Tuesday, following the revelation that JC star Jamone Lyle has a professional contract with Waterhouse Football Club, making him ineligible for schoolboy football under Inter-Secondary Schools Sports Association (ISSA) regulations.

Waterhouse, in a disciplinary letter dated October 9, said it had fined Lyle $60,000 for unauthorised participation in a Manning Cup match on October 7. The club alleged that Lyle ignored instructions from head coach Donovan Duckie and General Secretary Richard McCallum not to take the field for JC, in breach of his professional contract and the club’s rules.

ISSA’s decision to boot JC from the Walker Cup means that KC will now face Mona High in the final set for Friday. Mona had lost to JC in the semi-final via a penalty shootout.

World.title: BZR delayed! Concert postponed to December; patrons offered refunds
World.content:
File Photo BZR Weekend logo Cardi B

KINGSTON, Jamaica — BZR WKND Jamaica 2026 has been postponed from October 18 to December 20, following news that American rapper Cardi B will not be headlining the event as originally promoted.

In a statement issued to patrons and supporters, organisers attributed the postponement to circumstances beyond their control, while extending condolences to Cardi B and her family following the death of a loved one.

“First and foremost, we extend our heartfelt condolences to Cardi B and her family on the passing of their loved one. Our thoughts, prayers and deepest sympathies are with Cardi during this difficult time,” the statement read.

It followed days of speculation after the rapper’s publicly announced cancellation on October 8 and a follow-up video in which she maintained she was not at fault for the cancellation.

READ: ‘Just know it wasn’t me’: Cardi B addresses cancelled BZR WKND performance

However, on Tuesday, the promoters insisted they had fulfilled their financial and contractual obligations and made every effort to deliver the highly anticipated event.

“From the outset, BZR WKND has approached this event with the utmost professionalism, good faith and commitment, including fulfilling our financial obligations in full and honouring our contractual commitments,” they said.

Acknowledging the disappointment likely to be felt by patrons, particularly those who had already secured tickets, accommodation and travel arrangements, organisers apologised for the inconvenience.

Despite the setback, the promoters have assured fans that the show will go on, promising an even bigger, star-studded experience when the event returns in December.

“One thing is certain: we will not let you down. A show will happen. Our vision has always been bigger than one artiste,” the statement said.

“BZR WKND is about bringing world-class entertainment, music, culture, and an unforgettable festival experience to Jamaica,” it added.

All tickets purchased for the original October 18 date will remain valid for the rescheduled event on December 20.

However, patrons who are unable to attend on the new date or who no longer wish to attend may request a refund by emailing eventsteamjamaica@kanoopays.com. Refund requests must include the purchaser’s full name, ticket purchase confirmation, order or transaction reference number, and the email address used to purchase the tickets.

Organisers said further instructions regarding refunds and the rescheduled event will be communicated through official channels.
