World.title: Spartan Takes Over Hvar with 3,600 Competitors from 63 Countries
World.content:
October 12, 2026 – The third edition of Spartan 100m & Sprint World Championship took place this weekend, cementing an important relationship between the world-renowned obstacle race and Croatia’s premier island.

One of the pleasures of covering life and tourism on Hvar for more than 15 years now (and with almost 10,000 articles on the island written) is that I have been able to watch the island evolve and to see how longer-term strategies play out. Fames for its sun, nightlife, beaches, lavender and UNESCO culture, Hvar does not have to work too hard to attract tourists, but there has been plenty of effort to diversity and prolong the tourist season over the years.

https://www.facebook.com/reel/2526211701200292

One area which the island has encountered particular success in over the last decade has been in the area of adventure tourism, with a successful partnership between the town authorities, tourist board, and Suncani Hvar hotels.

Various eye-catching events and arrivals over the years highlighted Hvar’s shoulder-season credentials as an excellent adventure tourism destination. These included hosting one of the world’s leading cycling teams, Bahrain Merida for three years as the headquarters for their winter training, as well as the world-famous Othillo Swimrun for several years.

A very welcome addition to the Hvar calendar for the last three Octobers has been Spartan, the world-famous obstacle course race, attracting athletes from all over the world. The timing of the event, just as the shoulder season is starting to die down, injects new life into the town, as well as bringing some much-appreciated late-season revenue for the hospitality providers. There is a wonderful and very youthful energy around the town over those four days, and you don’t have to be competing to join in the fun.

This year’s event was no exception, and it was a pleasure to see how this chameleon of a destination which offers everything transforms its focus to summer and the beach into showcasing its beauty and terrain for hardened athletes. And it will change again later this week, as the inaugural HVARMONY gathering – focused on the original attraction of Hvar tourism back in 1868, wellbeing.

A full report on the event was covered below by Slobodna Dalmacija, all photos by Samir Kurtagic/Spartan Hvar:

More than 3,500 athletes from 63 countries participated in the third edition of the Spartan event on Hvar, held from October 8 to 11, 2026. The four-day program featured world championships in the 100m and Sprint 5K disciplines, the Beast 21K and Super 10K races, and the Spartan Kids event. A total prize purse of $100,000 was provided for the two world championships, while the Hvar Beast also served as the second stop of the regional National Adriatic Series.

The competition took place along the Hvar waterfront and on courses connecting the coast, city streets, and the ascent to the Fortica fortress. The short course, featuring head-to-head finishes, captivated the audience during the 100m championship, while the longer races took competitors beyond the city center onto terrain that demanded not only obstacle-clearing skills but also endurance on the climbs.

Alongside athletes arriving from all over the world, a large number of locals also competed on the courses. Šime Ravlić, the Mayor of Hvar, highlighted both the participation and the organizational challenges posed by the adverse weather conditions:

“This year’s Spartan weekend presented a unique challenge for both competitors and organizers, and we are delighted that it exceeded all expectations. Adverse weather was an additional hurdle that the organizers successfully overcame; we sincerely congratulate everyone on the ground who saw this demanding project through to the end. In just three years of the Spartan event in Hvar, the number of participating countries has grown from 35 to 63—a clear indicator of the rising interest in this sport and in Hvar as a host destination. There is no need to elaborate on the global promotion generated by enthusiastic competitors alongside the organizers’ official channels. We are particularly pleased with the response from the islanders: 59 locals participated in the 5km, 10km, and 21km races—with some successfully completing all three—while 246 of the 530 competitors in the children’s race were from the island. The message conveyed to young people and islanders through the energy, perseverance, and spirit of these exceptional athletes—whom we hosted for nearly a week—is unmistakable. The Spartan event in Hvar is a success story; we therefore extend our thanks once again to the organization’s founder and leader, Joe De Sena, for his trust; to the local organizer for excellent cooperation; to the Ministry of Tourism and Sport of the Republic of Croatia and the Croatian National Tourist Board for their support; and to all local…” …participants and collaborators. Together, we made this edition of Spartan spectacular.”

100M World Championship: a world title decided in mere seconds

Oliver Addy from England won the 100-meter world championship title. In the final, he clocked a time of 32.574 seconds, defeating Caleb Riley, who finished the course in 36.477 seconds. Third place went to Tommy Matthews, who recorded a time of 31.746 seconds in the bronze-medal race.

For Addy, who has been competing in OCR for four years, the victory in Hvar capped off a successful season, and he is already thinking about returning.

“I can’t believe this sport has brought me here. I’ve had a great season and can’t wait to see what’s next. I definitely want to come back next year and defend my title. I’m ready—I can’t wait!” said Addy.

In the women’s final, Poland’s Kasia Jonaczyk triumphed with a time of 40.882 seconds. May Yahalom from Israel took the silver with a time of 1:05.297, while the bronze went to American Jaleesa Himka, who clocked 32.740 seconds in the race for third place. Jonaczyk described what the title means to her immediately after the final:

“I can’t stop smiling; I still can’t believe it. Spartan was the most important race of the year for me. This title was the one thing I was missing. Honestly, for half the year I didn’t believe I could win it, and now here I am, talking to you. I feel like I’m in heaven,” said Jonaczyk.

In the final rounds of the 100m championship, placement is determined by head-to-head duels, meaning the times recorded by the finalists and bronze medalists were achieved in separate races.

The awards were presented by Josip Pavić, State Secretary at the Ministry of Tourism and Sport; Rob Stull, President of the International Modern Pentathlon Union (UIPM); and Šime Ravlić, Mayor of Hvar.

The prize fund for this discipline totaled $70,000, split equally between the men’s and women’s competitions. The winners received $18,000 each, the runners-up $10,000, the third-place finishers $5,500, and the fourth-place finishers $1,500.

Sprint 5K World Championship: a fast start isn’t enough for gold

At the Sprint 5K World Championship—which featured a five-kilometer course and 20 obstacles—the fastest of the 56 competitors in the men’s field was the Dutchman Frank Oosterom. He won gold with a time of 39:54, ahead of Frenchman Gregory Basilic, who finished in 40:26, and Czech Richard Hynek, with a time of 40:39.

In the women’s competition, Zuzana Kocumova won the world champion title with a time of 47:35. The silver medal went to Sabrina Daolio, who finished the race in 48:00, while Henriette Bardrum took the bronze with a result of 48:43.

A prize fund of $30,000 was secured for the Sprint Championship, also split equally between the two categories. First place earned $7,000; second, $4,000; third, $2,000; fourth, $1,500; and fifth, $500.

The Beast race held on October 10 held additional significance for competitors in the Adriatic Series. Following the initial Super race in Sveta Nedelja, athletes gathered points on Hvar—over a 21-kilometer course featuring 30 obstacles—ahead of the series finale at Krvavec on October 17.

Italian athlete Claudia Bongiovanni won the women’s race on Hvar with a time of 2:41:37, while Norwegian Espen Berget triumphed in the men’s category with a time of 2:13:53.

The Adriatic Series combines three races into a single ranking for the Elite and Age Group categories. Points are awarded based on placement, with a victory earning 300 points. The final tally counts the two best results, meaning that even competitors for whom Hvar was their first race in the series can contend for the overall ranking by participating in the final Beast race at Krvavec. A Great Race and Over 500 Children on the Course

The Super 10K—featuring a 10-kilometer course and 25 obstacles—brought together competitors of varying experience levels, ranging from those for whom Hvar was their first Spartan race to seasoned participants with numerous races under their belts. At the starting line, the pre-race atmosphere was filled with dancing and laughter, as the group warm-up quickly turned into a social gathering before hitting the course.

The youngest participants had their own races, too; over 500 children took part in the Spartan Kids events. The shortest course, spanning one kilometer, was recommended for children aged four to six. The 1.5-kilometer race was open to children aged seven to 14, while the three-kilometer race was for those aged nine to 14.

Age-appropriate obstacles included climbing, crawling, and jumping, and every finisher was awarded a medal. Parents and friends cheered the children on from the sidelines, meaning the program for the youngest participants also brought together many families.

Over 300 Team Members and 143 Volunteers

More than 300 team members and 143 volunteers took part in executing the four-day program. Organization and production crews, race officials, and security teams managed the race operations, while volunteers assisted competitors and provided support on the ground. The arrival of athletes, along with their families and teams, generated additional demand for accommodation, hospitality services, and transport in October—well after the peak summer season. Josip Pavić, State Secretary at the Ministry of Tourism and Sport, highlighted the event’s contribution to extending the tourist season:

“The Spartan World Championship Hvar is an excellent example of how major international sports events can contribute to the development of year-round tourism and create added value for a destination outside the main tourist season. We are particularly pleased that, in mid-October, Hvar once again brought together thousands of participants and their supporters from over 60 countries, confirming the event’s strong international character and Croatia’s status as a sports-tourism destination. This year, the Government of the Republic of Croatia and the Ministry of Tourism and Sport recognized the project’s significance and provided €1,350,000 in co-financing. We are proud of this year’s results, as well as the growth the Spartan World Championship Hvar has achieved over the past three years.”

Hvar and Spartan to Continue Partnership in 2027

Spartan returns to Hvar from October 7 to 10, 2027. The fourth edition will offer an opportunity to experience the island from a new perspective. Organizers invite past participants to return and aim for a new personal best, and encourage those who watched the races from the sidelines this year to step up to the starting line themselves next autumn.

World.title: Hvar Tourism Returns to Its Wellbeing Roots with HVARMONY Gathering
World.content:
October 12, 2026 – Croatia’s premier island of Hvar prepares to mark 158 years of organised tourism in Europe by returning to its roots – meet HVARMONY.

Long before “wellbeing” had a name, Hvar was already living it.

Carl Honoré, Kristina Kuzmič, and Ivana Paradžiković are among the headliners of HVARMONY, a four-day gathering focused on how to live better, longer, and happier lives, taking place in Hvar from October 15 to 18.

From October 15 to 18, Hvar becomes a venue for discussing a seemingly simple yet increasingly important question: how can we live better, longer, and happier lives?

HVARMONY – The Art of Living is a new four-day event that bridges modern insights into health, longevity, movement, nutrition, mental resilience, and quality of life with the Mediterranean’s generations-old wisdom on the good life.

The idea behind HVARMONY is not to offer yet another list of rules for becoming a “better version of yourself.” Quite the opposite. In an era where wellbeing and longevity have evolved into global trends and massive industries, HVARMONY shifts the focus back to a simpler question: what do we truly need to live well?

The answers won’t be sought solely on stage. Over the course of four days, lectures and discussions will alternate with movement, workshops, outdoor activities, the sea, food, sound, and experiences that transform Hvar from a mere backdrop into an active participant in the event.

Among the headliners of this inaugural edition is Carl Honoré—the internationally acclaimed author of the bestseller In Praise of Slowness and a leading figure of the Slow Movement—who will speak about the value of slowing down in a world that constantly pressures us to speed up. Kristina Kuzmič—an international speaker and author followed by millions for her open and direct approach to topics such as parenting, mental health, life challenges, and self-relationship—is also coming to Hvar.

Joining the program alongside her are Ivana Paradžiković and a host of domestic and international authors, experts, and facilitators specializing in nutrition, movement, mental resilience, longevity, and quality of life.

Among them are Maja Brekalo, Dalibor Petrinić, Andrea Solomun, Goran Sajko, Mirela Anić, Mia Šoškić, Miriam Mack, Sebastian Orlić, Petra Hisinger, Mirta Primorac Šejić, TLEX Institute experts Neringa Thariani and Aleksandra Jovanić-Sinko, Nina Kraljić, and other program participants.

Hvar returns to its original tourism roots—in October.

The choice of Hvar and the timing is no coincidence.

Hvar’s organized tourism story began back in 1868 with the founding of the Hygienic Society, at a time when the island’s greatest assets were highlighted as its mild Mediterranean climate, sunshine, clean air, sea, and opportunities for rest and recovery.

The Hygienic Society’s first hotel opened on October 15, 1868—the very same date that, 158 years later, marks the start of the inaugural edition of HVARMONY. “Hvar began its organized tourism journey during the very time of year we would today call the off-season. The Sanitary Society’s first hotel opened on October 15, 1868, and Hvar’s comparative advantage back then was precisely its Mediterranean climate—sun, sea, clean air, rest, and recovery. That is why, for us, HVARMONY is not merely a reminder of the beginnings of tourism nearly 160 years ago, but also a message that Hvar is just as beautiful—and perhaps, in a unique way, even more so—outside the peak summer months, when its natural rhythm comes to the fore once again.

We did not envision HVARMONY as just another conference on well-being or longevity, but rather as a reminder that the art of living often lies in simple things: time spent with loved ones, good food, physical activity, being in nature, quality sleep, and the ability to simply slow down from time to time. The island teaches you this almost naturally. And perhaps that is precisely the link between a quality life and quality tourism: neither should be a race to accumulate more, but rather a quest for better balance.

I am particularly delighted that this idea was recognized right from its inaugural edition and that we will be joined in Hvar by a host of fascinating local and international authors, speakers, and experts—including Carl Honoré, Kristina Kuzmič, and Ivana Paradžiković. Their diverse perspectives embody exactly what we want HVARMONY to be: a place for exchanging ideas and experiences, and for finding simpler answers to the question of how to live better.” Director of the Hvar Town Tourist Board

A program that does not require following a strict schedule

HVARMONY does not follow a traditional conference format. Visitors can attend a single lecture, participate in a workshop, start the day with movement by the sea, discover Hvar through the story of its origins in health tourism, join a discussion in the historic Hvar Theatre, or simply take a few hours for themselves.

The program takes place at various locations across the town, including the Arsenal and Hvar Theatre, Bonj, and open-air seaside spaces. Each visitor can experience HVARMONY in their own way—whether by attending a single lecture or practice session, or by participating throughout all four days.

The event is organized by the Hvar Town Tourist Board as an initiative open to the general public. Most of the program is free of charge, though registration is required, as is advance sign-up for specific workshops and sessions with limited capacity.

HVARMONY aims to open up a conversation about health and longevity—without adding the pressure to live a perfect life. Because perhaps the art of living isn’t about constantly doing more. Perhaps it means recognizing what is enough for us, what is worth holding onto, and the pace at which we want to live. HVARMONY – The Art of Living October 15–18, 2026

For more info, visit www.hvarmony.com

World.title: Isamaa rakes in €229k in 3rd quarter as party donations surge ahead of election
World.content:
Opposition party Isamaa collected by far the most donations among parliamentary parties in the third quarter of 2026 (Q3 2026), taking in €229,301.

The non-parliamentary Parempoolsed raised more than two major parties, the coalition Reform Party and the opposition Centre Party. Reform reported the highest overall revenue in the quarter, at over half a million euros.

Parties' main sources of revenue are donations and state support, the latter issued to all parties who polled above 2 percent at the preceding election, in proportion to votes received. Membership dues make up a smaller proportion of revenue.

According to the Political Parties Financing Surveillance Committee (ERJK), Isamaa's largest donors in Q3 2026 were Bigbank owner Parvel Pruunsild (€100,000), energy and real estate entrepreneur Janek Veeber (€50,000), transport entrepreneur Hugo Osula (€25,000), and Postimees owner Margus Linnamäe (€15,000). Membership fees brought in €3,360. With state funding included, Isamaa's Q3 2026 revenue totaled €326,090.

Reform collected €70,179 in donations and €1,700 in membership fees. Its total revenue was €505,562, the highest of any party. Its largest donors were casino magnate Armin Karu (€25,000), real estate businessman Marek Mägi (€15,000) and wind farm entrepreneur Andres Sõnajalg (€15,000).

Centre took in €64,112 in donations and €14,727 in membership fees. Total revenue came to €266,015. Its largest donation, €3,977, came from Jaak Madison, one of the party's two MEPs.

The opposition Conservative People's Party of Estonia (EKRE) raised €5,791 in donations and €1,103 in membership fees in Q3 2026. Total revenue came to €207,627 once state support is included. Its largest single donation, €1,500, came from Evelin Poolamets, one of the party's MPs.

The other coalition party, Estonia 200, collected €167,633 in total, almost all of it from state funding (€163,383). Donations amounted to €2,132, with the largest, €600, from MP Diana Ingerainen. Membership fees brought in €1,665.

The Social Democrats (SDE), in opposition since spring 2025, received €44,250 in donations and €6,439 in membership fees. Total revenue was €155,722. Their largest single donation, €5,000, came from entrepreneur and local politician Pille-Riin Raidsepp.

The non-parliamentary Parempoolsed does not collect membership dues. It reported €138,043 in donations in Q3 2026, and total revenue of €145,568. Businessmen Rain Lõhmus and Raul Kirjanen each provided €30,000.

The Riigikogu elections take place March 7, 2027, meaning parties will be spending on campaigning in the intervening months.

World.title: Tallinn says no to motorcycles, e-scooters in bus lanes
World.content:
Tallinn is pushing back against plans to let motorcycles and e-scooters use bus lanes, warning they could slow public transport and increase crash risks.

In a submission to the Riigikogu's Economic Affairs Committee, the city reiterated its opposition to a bill allowing motorcycles to use public transport lanes. It also rejects a separate proposal to allow light electric vehicles, including e-scooters, in the lanes.

Deputy Mayor Joel Jesse (Center Party) said adding more traffic would make it harder for buses to stay on schedule and increase the risk of crashes.

E-scooters, he said, pose particular concerns due to the sheer difference in size and mass, and large vehicles' blind spots also increase both the likelihood and severity of collisions.

"In spots where buses share the lanes with rams, there's the added risk of getting caught in the tracks," the deputy mayor continued, adding that wet and icy roads can worsen conditions from fall through spring in particular as well.

Cycle and bus lane in Tallinn. Source: ERR

EV explosion

Tallinn also wants to revoke the existing right under the Public Transport Act for taxis and electric vehicles (EVs) to use public transport lanes, saying fewer vehicles would help public transport run faster and more reliably.

Traffic in public transport lanes has increased significantly, the city said, with the number of registered EVs rising from 1,649 in 2020 to more than 13,000 this year, about two-thirds of them in Harju County.

This rapid increase in EVs has already slowed public transport in the dedicated lanes, making it harder for them to remain on schedule. "This shows that access to public transport lanes should be narrowed rather than expanded," the city added.

World.title: Foreign ministry: The state cannot directly control Silmet's business decisions
World.content:
Although the Ministry of Foreign Affairs says it has pressured Silmet to stop using Russian raw materials, the company has yet to do so.

Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) said the ministry has pressured chemical and metallurgical manufacturer Silmet to stop using Russian raw materials. The minister has now promised to set a deadline for the company to end its use of Russian raw materials. Tsahkna believes the company could stop using Russian raw materials as early as the beginning of next year.

ERR asked the Ministry of Foreign Affairs what specific pressure it had exerted, why the company had not complied and whether the ministry or the minister bears responsibility for the fact that, in the fifth year of the war in Ukraine, an Estonian company continues to purchase raw materials from Russia.

In its response, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs noted that the company's dependence on Russian raw materials has been publicly known for a long time. According to the ministry, Estonian media were reporting on the issue as early as 1995.

"However, dependence on Russian raw materials is not only a business risk but also a strategic vulnerability that Russia could exploit for its own benefit. It is therefore important to eliminate this dependence as quickly as possible," the ministry emphasized.

The ministry said it maintains regular contact with Estonian companies, including Silmet, stressing the need to find alternatives to Russian raw materials and end dependence on them.

"Silmet is a privately owned, publicly traded company that belongs to an international group based in Canada. The state cannot directly influence the company's business decisions or continuously monitor the details of its operations. Nor can the state independently assess when and to what extent the company has worked to identify alternative sources of raw materials," the ministry said.

At the same time, the ministry emphasized that it has consistently worked to support Silmet in identifying and establishing supply channels for raw materials from outside Russia. "To this end, we have, among other things, cooperated with the European Commission, which is responsible for the European Union's common trade policy."

According to the ministry, an important step in this direction was taken on October 9 when the European Commission selected Silmet's development project, Silmet 2.0, as one of 46 new EU strategic projects. The project aims to modernize the plant's production capabilities, enable the use of alternative raw material sources and reduce European industry's dependence on Russia.

The ministry noted that strategic project status will put Silmet in a better position to carry out its development plans and reduce its dependence on Russian raw materials.

According to the ministry's information, potentially suitable sources of raw materials for Silmet can be found in Latin America, Asia and Africa. The company itself is best placed to assess the technical suitability of specific raw material sources, taking into account the particular requirements of its production processes and technology.

"Silmet itself should explain to the public as soon as possible how it intends to end its dependence on Russian raw materials," the ministry emphasized.

The ministry also noted that growing international competition is making it more difficult to find alternative supply channels. Major industrialized countries are actively competing for limited raw material resources, affecting both their availability and supply opportunities.

"Estonia's goal remains to support Silmet's efforts to diversify its raw material supplies and reduce its dependence on Russian raw materials. Achieving this goal will require investment and technological changes by the company itself, as well as cooperation at the European Union level to improve access to alternative supply channels and strengthen Europe's security of supply for strategic raw materials," the ministry said.

ERR News reported on Thursday that a Russian company supplying rare earths to Estonia's Silmet was removed from the European Union's proposed 22nd sanctions package at Estonia's request.

World.title: Over 70 unexploded aerial bombs uncovered in Jõgeva nature reserve
World.content:
Dozens of Soviet-era aerial bombs, many of them live, have been excavated and safely disposed of in Jõgeva County, Maaleht reported .

The safety work was planned and covered a known danger zone at a former Soviet military facility.

On the penultimate weekend of September, Rescue Board and Defense League bomb disposal teams removed dozens of explosives from the former Utsali training ground in Jõgeva County.

They recovered more than 70 items from the area over the three days, including explosive devices and their components.

Most of the finds were aerial bombs, including both training and live versions.

The site was selected because the Soviet Air Force had once used it extensively for bombing exercises. Bomb disposal specialists had previously been called to the area, so it was a known danger zone.

Over 30 bomb disposal specialists and assistant specialists, along with more than 50 members of the Estonian Defense League and other support personnel, took part in the search operation.

Hazardous items were transported to a demolition site.

Marti Mereäär, head of the Southern Estonia bomb disposal unit, noted that explosive devices can remain dangerous for many years, and under no circumstances should they be handled. Members of the public should call 112 in such cases.

This is even the case with items of war memorabilia in the home, if there is reason to fear they are explosives. "Calling out bomb disposal specialists is free of charge, and there is no penalty for reporting an artillery shell found at home," Mereäär added.

What should you do if you find suspected explosives?

Under no circumstances should you touch the object

Move to a safe distance immediately

After moving a safe distance away, call the emergency number 112 as soon as you can

Note the location of the found object

World.title: Estonian court convicts gas station clerk who stole 67,000 liters of fuel
World.content:
A court has convicted a former Olerex employee who, according to the charges, stole a total of 67,000 liters of diesel fuel from storage tanks while working at a gas station in Jüri.

The Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs announced last week that a court had recently ruled on a case involving the theft of nearly 67,000 liters of diesel fuel from a gas station in dozens of separate incidents.

Toomas Tomberg, a prosecutor with the Northern District Prosecutor's Office who handled the case, told ERR that the thefts took place at the Olerex gas station in Jüri.

Prosecutors accused Igor Sorokin of using his access to the gas station's systems while working as a customer service representative to repeatedly steal diesel fuel from a storage tank.

According to the charges, he committed a total of 51 thefts between December 9, 2022, and January 25, 2024. To conceal the thefts, he switched off the gas station's video surveillance system before pumping diesel fuel into tanks installed in a vehicle he was using. Prosecutors accused him of stealing nearly 67,000 liters of diesel fuel worth almost €108,600.

The court found Sorokin guilty of large-scale, systematic theft and sentenced him to two years and six months in prison, suspended for a three-year probationary period. He was also ordered to compensate Olerex for €108,589 in financial losses. The ruling has not yet entered into force.

"The court proceedings confirmed that this was not an isolated act but a series of systematic thefts committed over an extended period. Although the defendant was caught in the act during one incident in January 2024, work schedules, video surveillance logs, storage tank records, witness testimony and other evidence gathered allowed the court to find that the remaining incidents described in the charges had also been proven," Tomberg said.

He added that the court agreed with prosecutors that the evidence formed a coherent and reliable body of proof establishing the defendant's actions throughout the period covered by the charges.

According to Tomberg, the case is notable both for the amount of fuel stolen and the length of time over which the thefts took place.

"It also demonstrates that prolonged, concealed activity causing financial losses to a company can be proven even when direct evidence relates to only part of the criminal activity, while the remaining incidents are established through a body of mutually corroborating circumstantial evidence," he said.

Recurring fuel theft on the rise

According to statistics from the Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs, more than 2,000 fuel thefts have been recorded so far this year, nearly 50 percent more than a year ago.

The ministry noted that this does not necessarily mean people across Estonia have suddenly become twice as inclined to steal. Rather, the statistics suggest that thieves have become more systematic in their activities and that some incidents are being classified as criminal offenses because of their repeated nature.

A single theft may constitute a misdemeanor, but when someone repeatedly and knowingly engages in the same behavior, it becomes a criminal offense.

Fuel thefts are largely responsible for the more than 6 percent year-on-year increase in property crimes, the ministry said.

World.title: PPA: Migrants more visible in Tallinn's Nõmme, not more numerous
World.content:
The latest group of illegal migrants apprehended in Tallinn's Nõmme district does not mean that neighborhood has seen more cases than other parts of the city, authorities say.

The Police and Border Guard Board has detained two groups of illegal migrants in recent months, most recently on Sunday evening.

Overall, the PPA has detained 83 migrant groups in Estonia since mid-summer, and 352 individual illegal migrants since July 21, amid heightened migratory pressure on the Belarus-EU border.

In both reported cases in Nõmme, the PPA acted on neighbor tip-offs, as well as in other cases close to the nearby Tallinn University of Technology.

Rainis Sinikas, head of the PPA North Prefecture's border and migration supervision department, noted that the detained migrants are spread across different districts. It is largely Nõmme's character, he said, that makes detentions more likely for those accommodated there.

As a leafy suburb on the southern outskirts of the capital, Nõmme is a place where local residents tend to recognize each other by sight, Sinikas said. Outsiders, still more so those of a different ethnic background from the majority, tend to stand out more than they might in more central areas of Tallinn.

"The point of detention is largely connected to where migrants live. Through a trafficker, they find accommodation somewhere in a Tallinn district. Since Nõmme is a small garden suburb where many neighbors know each other, a number of people of another nationality attracts attention," Sinikas said.

"In the city center, people moving around during rush hour may not be noticed. But in a small garden suburb, far more attention is paid to who is moving around, and so more reports come in," he continued.

Sunday evening's operation in Nõmme began when residents reported what they said were two dark-skinned men outside a building. The men appeared not to be familiar with the area.

PPA officials went to the scene and detained both men. Checks revealed they were Sudanese nationals staying in Estonia illegally. During conversations, it emerged that several other illegal migrants were hiding in the area. Police then launched a search involving patrols, service dogs and the Rescue Board.

This led to eight additional men, also of Sudanese origin, being apprehended. They had been hiding in wooded areas.

"Generally the practice has been that running away and abandoning belongings doesn't happen very often, but this time it did," Sinikas said.

In the July case, it emerged that migrants had congregated at a short-term rental building. The PPA is still establishing the circumstances of Sunday's incident.

"In practically every case we establish whether they have already stayed overnight in Estonia. If they have, we check the accommodation or apartment used as short-term let. We also establish their route in detail: how many came in and where they came from. Through continuous and consistent procedural steps, we establish their background and whether we can apprehend more migrants at that address. Practice has shown that sometimes we do," Sinikas added.

October has so far seen no let-up for the PPA in detaining migrant groups, mainly in Tallinn but also in Pärnu and central Estonia.

On Monday, the PPA detained a group of seven illegal migrants in the city center. Migratory pressure is likely to continue and possibly rise ahead of winter, the PPA said.

The PPA says it receives constant tip-offs about possible illegal migrants. Sinikas denied that tip-offs had been primarily race-based. Actions and behavior stand out, he said — and even dirty clothing in the autumn weather.

"Since the weather is muddy, many of the detained groups get muddy too," Sinikas said.

Not only the PPA but other agencies are coming under heavy pressure. Over 250 people are now in the Tallinn detention center. The courts are overworked too, since detaining people is a legal process, on top of sentencing human traffickers caught in Estonia.

"The situation is difficult and could turn into a crisis situation. Various institutions, including administrative courts and local governments, are overloaded. We order interpretation and our entire network of cooperation partners is under great strain," Sinikas said.

The situation is complicated by the fact that different nationalities are placed in the detention center together, which has led to conflicts.

"It doesn't take much — there have been disagreements and pushing, even over a TV remote. So far we have managed to prevent and avert larger conflicts, but there are still such scuffles and quarrels," Sinikas said.

Sunday's group consisted of Sudanese nationals. The group apprehended Monday in central Tallinn were Somalis. "There are a lot of Bangladeshi, but also Pakistani and Afghan citizens. The circle is quite wide, and people from Ethiopia and Eritrea have also been detained," Sinikas said.

Regardless of country of origin, the migrants mostly arrive in Estonia from Belarus via Latvia, which it borders. They then make their way northwards.

Processing the return of one migrant usually takes over a month, including establishing that they did indeed cross the border illegally from another state. Estonia has so far sent 105 migrants back to Latvia.

The migrants themselves have said during proceedings that their intended destination was a western EU country, for instance Finland, Germany or Spain.

Sinikas said that while some have stated a desire to remain in Estonia, it is not clear whether this is their genuine wish or a script they have been taught.

That "also has to be established during proceedings," Sinikas noted.

Interior Minister Igor Taro (Eesti 200) discussed the Belarus-backed migration pressure on Latvia's border with his Polish counterpart Marcin Kierwiński at the ongoing Warsaw Security Forum. Taro said the migratory pressure should be treated as an attack on the whole EU, and that escalation must carry a cost beyond the existing sanctions on Minsk.

"All our allies are ready to support Latvia, just as we have previously stood alongside Poland and Lithuania. Responsibility lies entirely with the Belarusian regime, which supports and incites illegal border crossings and contributes to damage to Latvia's border infrastructure," Taro said.

Taro is set to take part in a panel discussion on Tuesday about government resilience in the era of hybrid attacks.

World.title: Despite Rail Baltica delay, Tallinn's Ülemiste terminal on track for 2028
World.content:
The new Ülemiste passenger terminal in Tallinn is still due to open in late 2028, despite Rail Baltica's completion being pushed back to 2034.

Although Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania agreed to complete Rail Baltica by 2034, making maximum use of the next EU budget period, construction already underway will continue, Infrastructure Minister Kuldar Leis (Reform) said last week.

Work on the main building and outdoor areas at Ülemiste Linda Terminal is progressing as planned, Rail Baltic Estonia communications chief Silvia Pärmann told ERR.

One platform is already in use by passenger rail operator Elron, she noted, and trains to Tartu and Narva will continue serving the terminal via the existing railway ahead of its full completion in late 2028.

"Even before Rail Baltica is completed, the terminal will bring together trams, connecting passengers to destinations including the airport and port, as well as buses and domestic rail connections," Pärmann said.

Render of Tallinn's future Ülemiste Terminal. Source: Rail Baltic Estonia

The structure's concrete frame is due to be completed by the end of this year, making its overall scale and architectural design more clearly visible, she added.

Tallinn's Rail Baltica terminal was designed by Zaha Hadid Architects.

Major urban center plans

This February, Rail Baltic Estonia, Tallinn Airport and Mainor Ülemiste also unveiled plans to develop the area into a new urban center, with nearly €500 million in combined investments over the coming years.

Projects include a new high-rise with a conference center and a European-themed park, while Tallinn Airport also pursues its own more than €66 million expansion project.

The city has also proposed building a 10,000-seat multifunctional arena in Ülemiste.

World.title: Experts: Full damage of Germany's August Hanning scandal yet to be revealed
World.content:
Former German foreign intelligence chief August Hanning's detention on suspicion of espionage has raised concerns about damage to Germany's national security and the credibility of its intelligence services, Estonian experts find.

Last week, police searched the home of August Hanning, the former head of Germany's foreign intelligence service, in Nordwalde, western Germany, near the Dutch border. Hanning was detained on suspicion of espionage amounting to treason.

The allegations concern a period after Hanning had stepped down as head of the foreign intelligence service and begun providing consulting services. It emerged that he had enlisted the help of his former chief of staff, Manfred Dankesreiter, who was still working for the foreign intelligence service.

"Specifically, it is alleged that Mr. Hanning received nearly 2,000 documents from Manfred D. up until June 2022, some of which were confidential, meaning they were intended exclusively for use by the leadership of the foreign intelligence service. In one case, Mr. Hanning is suspected of using classified information to prepare an analysis for an employee of a foreign intelligence service. In another case, he is alleged to have passed information to an employee of another intelligence service following an extensive exchange of information," said German prosecutor's office spokesperson Ines Peterson.

Prosecutors have not specified which two countries' intelligence services were involved. German media have speculated about China and Azerbaijan, while Hanning's previous ties to Russia have also been highlighted. The leaked materials reportedly included primarily security assessments and documents concerning matters such as Iran's nuclear program and an analysis of the Russian armed forces.

"I think the extent of the damage is impossible to comprehend at this stage. The fragments that have appeared in the media do not allow us to properly assess its scale, partly because it is unclear which country Hanning was working for. Russia, China and Azerbaijan have all been mentioned. The timing is also important — whether he was recruited while he was still in office or after he left. When all this could have happened is extremely significant," said Arnold Sinisalu, former director general of the Estonian Internal Security Service (ISS/KAPO).

The precise extent of the damage remains to be determined. Germany's foreign intelligence service is a large organization, but its powers have so far been relatively limited. It is therefore possible that the information leaked was not particularly sensitive. However, other countries' secrets are also at stake and the overall reputational damage is enormous.

"The damage to the foreign intelligence service, the BND, is enormous. That is simply because a betrayal of this kind causes long-term damage to the BND's credibility, particularly among the intelligence partners on which it relies," said ARD journalist Michael Götschenberg.

"The other aspect is the purely symbolic damage that has been done. This affects not only Germany's intelligence service but German state institutions more broadly. How can these institutions be trusted if the head of an intelligence service has engaged in secret cooperation? At the same time, it must be emphasized that the very fact that something like this was uncovered is extremely positive," Sinisalu said.

"The Germans used to be very self-assured and believed they understood how Russia and China operated far better than we did and so on. History has made its own corrections. Perhaps this is partly a consequence of overconfidence and a sense of infallibility. I hope the substance of the case is not too serious. We will see. At present, too little is known," said Eerik-Niiles Kross, member of the Riigikogu Foreign Affairs Committee.

Hanning headed Germany's foreign intelligence service from 1998 to 2005, more than 20 years ago when Gerhard Schröder was German chancellor. Prosecutors say his alleged espionage activities took place between 2010 and 2022. How far has today's Germany moved on from that era?

"Germany is undergoing enormous change, with different forces pulling it in different directions. We are all concerned that the AfD, a far-right party that is at times openly pro-Putin, is the most popular political force. It has won some local elections. Whether that means a major shift at the next German Bundestag elections is too early to say, but the political atmosphere there is somewhat turbulent. The major established parties are doing rather poorly. At the same time, Germany is trying to move away from its highly restrained post-World War II approach. On the military front, the Germans have spent decades trying to prove to the world that they have learned from their mistakes. They have, of course, started making different kinds of mistakes, as tends to happen. Where Germany is headed is now one of the key questions for Europe's future," Kross said.

Germany is currently debating whether to grant its foreign intelligence service greater powers. Footage from last week also illustrates the contrast between the present and the past. In one clip, the current head of Germany's foreign intelligence service warns of the threats facing the country.

"Germany is at risk of being drawn into a violent conflict by Russia. The attempted attack in Leipzig is one example of this. No other country currently poses such a direct, extensive and concrete threat to Germany," said Martin Jäger, head of Germany's foreign intelligence service.

Meanwhile, former Chancellor Gerhard Schröder celebrates Russian President Vladimir Putin's birthday and visits a store belonging to a Russian retail chain on whose supervisory board he now serves.

World.title: Nvidia says to invest in French medical website
World.content:
Paris – AI chip giant Nvidia will take a minority stake in French medical website Doctolib that plans to use the technology to improve health care, its chief executive Jensen Huang said Tuesday.

Doctolib is a private website that allows patients to book appointments with doctors, but has also begun to allow patients to store medical information to more easily share their records.

In August it launched a research program using artificial intelligence to study the data of its 50 million users to improve navigation of the healthcare system.

The amount of the planned investment was not disclosed, but Huang said at a press conference in Paris that Nvidia invested at least $8 billion in Europe last year.

Doctolib chief executive Stanislas Niox-Chateau told AFP that the funds will help it speed up hiring and development of its in-house AI models that will power personal assistants for both patients and doctors, as well as help with administrative tasks.

Niox-Chateau said it would use Nvidia chips to power AI models that it will be able to retain control over, as well as patient data, instead of using proprietary AI models like those offered by OpenAI or Anthropic.

Doctolib was valued at 3.6 billion euros ($4.0 billion) during its last funding round earlier this year.

World.title: Real Madrid’s Mourinho has ‘trust’ in referees despite complaints
World.content:
Rome – Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho said Tuesday he has faith in officiating in Spain and in Europe despite his heavy criticisms of them this season.

Mourinho refused to take part in his obligatory post-match press conference on Saturday after Real Madrid beat Villarreal 1-0 in La Liga, in protest a decision to rule out a goal scored by Vinicius Junior and then send off the Brazil international for hair-pulling.

After a league derby defeat against Atletico Madrid, Mourinho brandished printed pictures of challenges in the game he thought the Rojiblancos should have been punished for.

However ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League clash at Roma, Mourinho tried to avoid controversy.

“I trust all the referees… whether it’s the league or Champions League, before the game I always have the best feelings about the referees,” Mourinho told reporters.

“I have confidence and I hope everything goes well for all three teams (both sides and the officials) — I don’t have any negative feelings.”

Mourinho said he might expand more on the subject when back in the Spanish capital.

“There are Italian media here that are more interested in the match than in that kind of thing,” added the veteran coach.

“You’ll have me (speaking) again on Saturday, I think it’s best if we move on to something else.”

Madrid midfielder Aurelien Tchouameni, also speaking before the Roma clash, said the squad was not happy with calls that had gone against them.

“I don’t want to speak about the referees… right now we have a lot of frustration with the decisions,” said Tchouameni.

Mourinho, 63, led Roma between 2021-2024, winning the Conference League with the Italian side in 2022 and finishing runners-up in the Europa League the following year.

Mourinho said Roma fans were “special people” and looked back fondly on his days in the city.

“It’s not as if we won the Champions League… but we did win a European competition, we played a second European final in two years, and I think everything came together,” added Mourinho.

World.title: Anthropic warns of AI ‘worms’ spreading across smart gadgets
World.content:
San Francisco – Small artificial intelligence models may be only months away from being able to behave like a computer worm, copying themselves from one internet-connected gadget to the next without human help, AI giant Anthropic said.

The finding potentially opens a new front in the cybersecurity threats emerging from AI, which have rattled governments and the companies rushing to adopt the technology.

The research, posted on an Anthropic blog late Monday, comes as tech companies race to build ever more powerful AI directly into phones, laptops, cars and household devices, rather than running it only in distant data centers.

A computer worm is malicious software that spreads between machines on its own. Researchers at Anthropic said an AI version would no longer need powerful data centers to operate.

Instead, it could hop from device to device across networks of cheap, poorly secured consumer hardware such as smart TV boxes and kitchen appliances.

The researchers based their calculations of how far such a worm could spread on Kimwolf, a botnet — a network of hijacked devices controlled by hackers — that infected more than two million devices at its peak, mostly off-brand Android TV boxes.

An AI worm of the kind described in the research would likely be slow, taking days to copy itself, William Zhou and Daniel Freeman of Anthropic said, comparing it to a slowly multiplying swarm of fruit flies.

Once created, it would be hard to stamp out, because there would be no central switch to turn off.

Anthropic’s researchers said their estimate of how fast and how far AI-fueled malware could spread was rough, since it was based on one type of gadget and one past botnet.

But over time, the amount of computing power sitting in everyday gadgets is expected to keep growing, while the AI models needed to pull this off are likely to keep getting smaller, the researchers added.

Varun Chandrasekaran, an assistant professor of electrical and computer engineering at the University of Illinois, said the research was unsurprising and matched similar recent findings, though he cautioned that Anthropic’s work had not been independently verified.

He also noted that security on devices like thermostats or home cameras “has historically been very weak.”

But when it came to AI, the biggest current threat was human bad actors using artificial intelligence to sharpen their hacks, rather than AI systems themselves going rogue, he said.

“A malicious human being is now supercharged with AI to perform bad things and we are seeing this happen at scale,” he added.

The rogue AI debate came to the fore in July, when AI programs running on OpenAI models escaped an internal company test and broke into the systems of AI platform Hugging Face — apparently hunting for the test’s answers.

The incident and subsequent reports like it have sparked international pressure for closer regulation of AI, even as the Trump administration resists the idea and urges the industry to police itself.

Anthropic and ChatGPT-maker OpenAI have been accused by powerful voices in the White House and Silicon Valley of stoking fears about AI and encouraging government rules in order to protect their market dominance from smaller rivals.

Brad Smith, OpenAI investor Microsoft’s president, warned Tuesday that industry and governments must “act with urgency” to create “real and effective safety standards” in order to rein in the risks of artificial intelligence.

World.title: Goldman Sachs profits jump as CEO says no plans to exit
World.content:
New York – Goldman Sachs reported higher third-quarter profit on Tuesday, sending shares higher as CEO David Solomon said there were no plans for a leadership transition.

Profit at the New York financial heavyweight during the July-September period was $5.1 billion, up 33 percent from the year-ago level but down 20 percent from the second quarter when business conditions were especially robust.

Revenue rose 23 percent to $18.7 billion.

Like rival JPMorgan Chase, which reported earlier Tuesday, Goldman saw muted activity in some parts of its markets business, such as fixed income, currency and commodities, where revenues were “essentially unchanged,” the firm said in a press release.

But net revenue in equities trading soared 72 percent from the year-ago level.

Goldman also scored higher investment banking fees, citing increases in completed mergers and an elevated level of initial public and secondary equity offerings.

The Wall Street Journal reported on September 28 that Goldman’s board had discussed a plan for Solomon to step down as CEO and be replaced with Chief Operating Officer John Waldron around the end of 2027 or in 2028.

A Goldman spokesman said in response that there was no timetable for a transition.

Solomon reiterated that on Tuesday, saying he was “super pleased” with the firm’s progress.

“I’m really enjoying the job, but more importantly, as a team, we’re super excited about what’s in front of us in the coming years and how we can continue to grow the franchise and really accelerate the earnings potential of the firm,” Solomon said.

“I just want to be clear: there is no succession transition or timeline underway at Goldman Sachs,” Solomon said.

“The board and I are singularly focused on our strategy to grow the firm and continue to serve our clients with excellence.”

Goldman shares rose 0.2 percent in early afternoon trading.

World.title: Big US banks report strong earnings and stay bullish on AI
World.content:
New York – Major US banks offered a largely upbeat outlook Tuesday, expressing confidence that the artificial intelligence investment boom will continue despite public pushback to the technology.

JPMorgan Chase and Goldman Sachs were among the banking heavyweights reporting higher third-quarter profits due in part to solid trading and financial advisory revenues while describing continued US consumer health despite inflation.

Executives face shifting challenges that include the grinding US-Iran war that has raised energy prices and recent moves by the Federal Reserve and other central banks to lift interest rates in light of inflation and rising US Treasury yields.

But perhaps the biggest question facing the industry’s medium-term outlook concerns the durability of the AI boom, which has spawned a growing list of public worries, most recently over the risk that potentially dangerous AI rogue agents could harm or even destroy human life.

That is on top of other difficult questions over potential job loss due to AI and the impact of massive data centers on energy prices and water supplies.

Bankers acknowledged the resonance of these issues but see no appreciable impact on the momentum behind the buildout.

“No one knows the exact line of travel but at its base, this technology is real,” said Goldman Sachs Chief Executive David Solomon.

“Lots of things can go wrong and slow it down,” said Solomon, who describes the current period as a “very strong technology super cycle.”

The push behind big AI ventures is “very much still in effect,” said JPMorgan Chase’s Chief Financial Officer Jeremy Barnum.

“The capex is still getting spent,” Barnum told a media conference call. “The deals still need to get done. People still want access to the market.”

– Healthy job market –

The comments came as JPMorgan reported a six percent increase in profits from a year ago to $15.3 billion, lower than the $15.85 billion forecast by FactSet analysts.

An earnings press release pointed to $658 million in securities investment losses and a 12 percent uptick in expenses, primarily driven by higher compensation and greater spending on technology and marketing.

After huge increases in the second quarter in markets-related business, revenue growth was expected to moderate somewhat in the just-finished July-September quarter.

JPMorgan still posted a 13 percent rise in markets securities service revenue, led by hefty growth in equity markets revenue that offset lower sales in trading for commodity and interest rate products.

Barnum described consumer spending as “sort of robust” despite persistent inflation. But monetary policy decisions remain a watch item.

“The consumer is currently very healthy, primarily because of a healthy labor market,” Barnum said. “But if the central bank needs to cool things off and that involves an aggressive extended rate cycle, almost by definition, that’s going to involve higher unemployment, which will produce weaker consumer credit results.”

At Goldman Sachs, profits during the July-September period was $5.1 billion, up 33 percent from the year-ago level but down 20 percent from the second quarter when business conditions were especially robust.

Goldman saw muted activity in some parts of its markets business, such as fixed income, currency and commodities, where revenues were “essentially unchanged,” the firm said in a press release.

But net revenue in equities trading soared 72 percent from the year-ago level.

Goldman also scored higher investment banking fees, citing increases in completed mergers and an elevated level of initial public and secondary equity offerings.

Solomon cited recent studies that estimate the US data center build-out as costing more than $10 trillion in investment through 2032. That prospect is a key element in what he describes as the current “top quartile” market.

While not every data center project will move forward, “there is going to be a lot of financing to do and we’re going to be in the middle of that,” he said. “It may be over time, as the financing needs growth, that there’s pressure on rates and that will affect the returns and viability of certain projects.”

But “one thing is clear, there’s a lot of demand for compute at the moment,” he said.

Among other big banks, Citigroup reported a 40 percent jump in profits to $5.2 billion, while Wells Fargo reported a 6.5 percent increase to $6.0 billion.

In early afternoon trading, JPMorgan shares rose 0.4 percent while Goldman Sachs climbed 0.8 percent. Citigroup dropped 3.4 percent while Wells Fargo lost 1.8 percent.

World.title: Apple unveils HomeView smart display in renewed home push
World.content:
San Francisco – Apple on Tuesday unveiled HomeView, a voice-driven smart display built around its revamped Siri AI assistant, as the iPhone maker makes a fresh bid for a place in living rooms and kitchens.

The device, which pairs a square seven-inch touchscreen with a speaker base, will sell for $299 in the United States starting November 13.

Apple has struggled for years to gain ground in the smart home, where its HomePod speakers have trailed Amazon’s Alexa and Google AI-amped devices.

Analysts see the new hardware as an effort to deepen customers’ ties to the Apple ecosystem as AI rivals, including OpenAI, eye devices of their own.

The launch is one of the first under John Ternus, Apple’s former hardware engineering chief, who took over as chief executive from Tim Cook on September 1.

HomeView is meant to act as a family command center, controlling connected features such as lights, locks, thermostats and cameras.

It also handles FaceTime video calls, plays music and video and doubles as a digital picture frame when idle.

In addition, Apple has also formed partnerships with South Korea’s LG and France’s Schneider for door locks and thermostats.

The release’s centerpiece is Siri AI, the overhauled version of Apple’s assistant powered by Apple Intelligence, which the company is pitching as a more conversational helper than the original Siri.

Siri AI is central to Apple’s effort to catch up with rivals in generative artificial intelligence, and it is built on AI technology from Google Gemini.

The company said that HomeView would not be sold in the European Union for the time being as the company finds ways to make Siri AI compliant with Europe’s competition rules.

Apple stated that it is working constructively with the EU to find a way for these products to enter the European market.

World.title: Al Zawraa secures 1-1 draw against Qatar SC in Gulf Club Champions League opener
World.content:
Iraqi powerhouse Al-Zawraa opened their campaign in the AGCFF Gulf Club Champions League 2026–2027 season with a 1–1 draw against Qatari outfit Qatar SC on Tuesday evening, October 13, 2026.

The opening Group B clash, hosted at Suheim bin Hamad Stadium in Doha, kicked off at 5:45 PM Baghdad time (+03:00 GMT) and ended in a draw after a tightly contested tactical affair.

The Baghdad-based side claimed an early lead in the 21st minute when forward Mohammed Sherif found the net, capping off an organized attacking sequence. Qatar SC intensified offensive pressure in response, eventually leveling the score four minutes into first-half stoppage time through striker Yohan Boli.

A guarded second half produced limited clear-cut opportunities for either side, with both defensive structures remaining firm until the final whistle to secure a point apiece.

Al-Zawraa competes in Group B alongside Qatar SC, the UAE’s Al-Nasr, and Bahrain’s Al-Riffa. Meanwhile, fellow Iraqi representative Erbil SC features in Group C, grouped against Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ettifaq, UAE’s Ajman Club, and Kuwait’s Kazma SC.

Under tournament regulations, the winners and runners-up from each group advance to the quarter-finals alongside the two best third-placed finishers. The knockout stages are scheduled to unfold in spring 2027, with the two-legged quarter-final ties set between March 2 and March 17, followed by the semi-finals and final matches between April 23 and April 30, 2027.

World.title: Iraq’s Electricity Ministry and JICA weigh financing for residential solar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Electricity convened bilateral discussions on Tuesday, October 13, 2026, with the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) to expand technical and financial cooperation across national solar energy initiatives.

The talks centered on the ministry’s strategic renewable roadmap, including grid-connection protocols, while the Japanese agency signaled concrete intentions to conduct a comprehensive feasibility assessment aimed at financing residential solar installations across Iraqi households.

According to a ministerial statement received by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), the working session was chaired by Hussein Mohammed Badr, Director General of the Ministry’s Planning and Studies Department, alongside Murtadha Hussein Mahdi, Director of the Renewable Energy Center, and senior departmental deputies.

Talks addressed the operational implementation pipeline for utility-scale solar projects, alongside institutional contracting frameworks and regulatory standards governing distributed solar integration into the national electricity grid.

During the proceedings, JICA representatives expressed the agency’s interest in financing and executing key solar ventures currently listed within the ministry’s capital investment portfolio.

The Japanese development body confirmed its intent to conduct a targeted study evaluating viable financing mechanisms for rooftop residential solar photovoltaic systems, modeling the program after the Central Bank of Iraq’s green energy lending initiative to alleviate capital constraints for domestic homeowners.

The Ministry of Electricity highlighted that expanding international development partnerships of this caliber accelerates the adoption of clean energy, hedges against peak load deficits on the national power transmission grid, and provides decentralized power solutions capable of directly meeting citizens’ daily residential electricity requirements.

World.title: Missing head of Khajuraho idol will be restored soon: ASI chief
World.content:
The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) has found the missing head of an 11th-century Vishnu idol at Khajuraho, whose restoration became the subject of a recent controversy involving the Supreme Court, and plans to reattach it after expert examination.

ASI has also introduced a three-year deadline for archaeological excavations to curb delays in research and cut approval times for most conservation projects to 15-20 days, director general Yadubir Singh Rawat told TOI in an exclusive interview. He also revealed plans for a preliminary excavation at Ujjain's Vaishya Tekri, where a Buddhist stupa could be larger than Sanchi's, although its actual scale and significance remain to be established.

Controversy over the beheaded Vishnu idol at Khajuraho's Javari temple reached the Supreme Court last year when advocate Rakesh Dalal sought restoration, replacement or reconstruction of the seven-foot statue. While dismissing the petition, then CJI BR Gavai had said, "Go and ask the deity itself to do something now." Though Gavai later said he respects all religions and that his statement was taken out of context, a lawyer had tried to throw a shoe at him inside the courtroom.





Rawat said the missing head had been found in an ASI store. "During a visit to Bhopal for the Brics summit, I learnt that the statue's head - which had been kept in our store - had been found. The person in charge informed me that someone likely tried to break off the head to steal it but failed to do so. We are having experts examine it and will soon reattach it to the statue."

On encroachments at protected monuments, Rawat said "The root of this problem lies in the list prepared by British rulers in 1904 under the 'Ancient Monuments Preservation Act' - a list that the then govt adopted post-Independence without any review.

The British had included cemeteries and graves of their obscure soldiers, horses and pets - which they deemed highly significant - among protected monuments." Rawat said a review in 1953 incorporated state monuments into a definitive list, but the central list remained unchanged.

The resulting difficulties led to 17 monuments being removed from it.

Regarding funding disparities, he said allocations depended on visitor numbers, maintenance requirements, security expenses and public facilities. Taj Mahal and Red Fort, he said, served as showcases for ASI, while Taj Mahal's maintenance required substantial expenditure because of its delicate structure and heavy tourist footfall. ASI paid around Rs 3 crore monthly for more than 200 CISF personnel deployed there.He said ASI circles had been instructed to prepare conservation and tourism development proposals for lesser-known sites like Bareilly's pyramid-like Bhim ki Gada structure.

NEW DELHI: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has barred a particular powerbank from being carried on aircraft in either passenger or cargo flights to, from and within India.The decision came in view of the "recent fire incident involving the MOBIKINS MK-PB-04 powerbank, and considering the potential safety risks associated with it", the regulatory body said.An IndiGo flight from Delhi to Chennai was diverted to Hyderabad Sunday after a passenger's personal electronic device caught fire.An order issued by DGCA chief Vir Vikram Yadav said the "travelling public and airlines" were advised to ensure that the MOBIKINS MK-PB-04 powerbank was not carried or transported on board the aircraft."Airlines are further advised to take appropriate measures to identify and prevent the carriage of the aforesaid powerbank and to disseminate this safety advisory to the passengers through suitable communication channels," the order said.Over the past year, several countries, including India, have started restricting powerbank usage on aircraft due to the possibility of them catching fire. Apart from limiting the number of powerbanks and their battery capacity, they can neither be used to charge personal electronic devices nor be charged via the in-seat power source on aircraft.Instances of PED and powerbank fires have been on the rise globally. The biggest scare here remains airlines taking cabin bags from passengers at the boarding gate to be kept in the baggage hold. If a fire breaks out in the belly baggage hold, it may be a while before it is detected.

NEW DELHI: Amid allegations of delayed medical assistance following the death of a first-year student at IIIT Ranchi, the education ministry Tuesday constituted a three-member committee to examine the circ-umstances surrounding the incident and possible gaps in the institute's student support and emergency response systems.The decision comes amid protests by students, who have accused the administration of failing to provide timely medical assistance and demanded the resignation of institute director Rajiv Srivastava.The student, Aditya Kumar (20), was found hanging in his hostel room Saturday.The committee, headed by Delhi University South Campus director Rajni Abbi, will include a senior psychiatrist and a senior education ministry official. The panel will examine whether the institute has adequately implemented guidelines concerning institutional support, counselling, mentoring and student grievance redress mechanisms.It will also interact with stakeholders, examine institutional records and identify systemic gaps, besides recommending measures to strengthen student welfare and prevent similar incidents. World.title: Bill to tweak FCRA similar to UPA-era law: JPC chief
World.content:
NEW DELHI: BJP MP Sanjay Jaiswal, who heads the joint parliamentary committee examining Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, Tuesday said major provisions of the proposed legislation had the same clauses that were incorporated in the law enacted by UPA govt in 2010.

He said this after a meeting of the committee, which interacted with Hindu, Christian and other groups and listened to their views on the proposed legislation facing stiff opposition from certain sections and opposition parties.

Jaiswal said the 2010 Act had given power to the home secretary and the principal secretary of the state to confiscate properties of an NGO receiving foreign funding under

if there were irregularities while the new bill proposed to give the same power to a designated authority.

"The law brought by the UPA govt had decided that if irregularities were found under FCRA, all the assets would be handed over to the home secretary or principal secretary concerned of the state. However, today, there is a designated authority in place of that arrangement," he added.

He said those who gave their views to the committee Tuesday included representatives of Syro Malabar Church, Ramakrishna Math and ISKCON among others.





"Everyone presented their views. We listened carefully to what everyone had to say. When we sit in our committee meeting, we will discuss these matters. We have heard everyone out, and subsequently, we will deliberate on all these points during the committee meeting. We will take the decisions together," Jaiswal said.

The bill was introduced in Lok Sabha on March 25 and referred to the JPC on Aug 12 following consistent demands of the opposition parties, which alleged that certain provisions of the legislation were highly objectionable.

Opposition parties allege that the FCRA Bill targets minorities as certain provisions will choke legitimate funding for Christian NGOs and minority-run social welfare and educational institutions.

Govt has rejected the charges and challenged the opposition to identify even one provision that discriminates against minorities. It has also maintained that the proposed legislation is not religion-specific and is aimed at regulating foreign contributions.

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Tuesday said that if China wants a normal relationship with New Delhi, the border between the two countries has to be stable.During a conversation at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum, Jaishankar said that India and China do not have an agreed border and that the issue has persisted for decades."We don't have an agreed border between India and China. This is not a new issue; it's been going on for multiple decades... From 1975 till 2020, a good 45 years, no blood was shed on that border. The last time there were fatalities was in 1975. In this period, India-China relations did grow," he said."Then in 2020, when we were in the midst of the Covid lockdown, we had a series of border issues, and it culminated in a clash in which a number of soldiers were killed on either side," Jaishankar added.Jaishankar said that if peace and tranquillity in the border areas are disturbed, then the relationship will have consequences."For us, what it represented was a very profound departure from the situation that was prevailing since 1975. If the peace and tranquillity in the border areas are disturbed, then the relationship will have consequences. Those consequences were very visible for the next five years until we were able to restore the peace and tranquillity.It took four years of negotiations," he added."The point we make to the Chinese is: 'If you want a normal relationship, if the rest of the relationship is to move, it's common sense. It's a no-brainer that the boundary has to be stable, that we need peace and tranquillity in the border areas.' As the border areas are settling down, they have settled down to a great extent since 2024; the relationship is commensurately moving towards normalcy," he further said.This comes after the ministry of external affairs reiterated that the Union territory of Ladakh is an integral and inalienable part of India after the Chinese foreign ministry opposed the naming of certain strategic locations in Ladakh."The announcement mentions that the twenty-eight (28) places/features located in the UT of Ladakh have been identified with standard place and feature names on the official map of Survey of India, and it has been done in consultation with the Union Territory of Ladakh and local stakeholders," MEA said."Identifying these places formally on the Survey of India map of UT of Ladakh is aimed at facilitating their accurate recognition and better awareness among the public at large," the ministry said.On October 2, India formally identified 28 strategic locations and geographical features in Ladakh on its official map, including key border friction points along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), such as Gogra and Hot Spring.The move, undertaken in consultation with the Ladakh administration, aimed to improve official mapping, ensure precise identification and raise public awareness of the sensitive border region.

World.title: India reaffirms Ladakh status as China says it doesn’t recognise the UT
World.content:
Diplomatic tensions flared again between India and China after Beijing strongly opposed Indiaâs decision to officially map and standardise 28 places in Ladakh, including some in Aksai China, and reaffirmed that it does not recognise the Union Territory (UT) of Ladakh.

In a swift rebuttal, New Delhi reiterated no amount of Chinese denial can change the established fact that the Ladakh UT is an integral and inalienable part of India.

According to the ministry of home affairs (MHA), which announced the standardisation in a press release on October 2, identifying the places/ geographical features formally on the Survey of India map was aimed at facilitating their accurate recognition and better awareness among the public at large.

MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal reiterated the same, saying the MHA statement was self-explanatory.

âThe announcement mentions that the twenty-eight (28) places/features located in the UT of Ladakh have been identified with standard place and feature names on the official map of Survey of India, and it has been done in consultation with the Union Territory of Ladakh and local stakeholders,â he said.

The Chinese foreign ministry described the Indian move as illegal saying it doesnât change the fact that the western sector of the China-India boundary belongs to China.





âChina has never recognized the so-called Union Territory of Ladakh unilaterally and illegally established by India, and firmly opposes the so-called standardized names publicised by India,â said spokesperson Mao Ning.

However, China itself has renamed places in Arunachal Pradesh on at least half a dozen occasions in the past 10 years, including twice in 2026, to reinforce its claim over the Indian state.

The fresh cartographic tussle comes in the middle of the ongoing normalisation of the bilateral relationship after a military standoff in eastern Ladakh.

The Chinese response was a throwback to its statement in 2019 â a day after India revoked the special status of J&K in 2019 â accusing New Delhi of undermining China's territorial sovereignty by unilaterally changing its domestic law and establishing Ladakh UT.

âSuch practice is unacceptable and will not come into force,â it had then said, warning India to exercise prudence in words and deeds on the boundary question.

It was perhaps no coincidence that the military conflict in eastern Ladakh started 8 months later.

Beijing maintains that it has always opposed India's inclusion of âChinese territory in the western sector of the China-India boundary into its administrative jurisdictionâ. For China,
