However, the border situation has remained stable since PM Narendra Modi and President Xi Jinping met in Kazan in 2024. India and China have since held 3 rounds of Special Representatives talks on the boundary question, with the last round in August resulting in 8 outcomes, including a decision to advance talks for an âearly and substantialâ harvest of boundary delimitation and border management.

World.title: Protest fundamental to democracy: Karnataka Govt; Then don’t cage us in Freedom Park: Activists
World.content:
BENGALURU: Karnataka home minister Priyank Kharge and chief minister DK Shivakumar Tuesday reiterated that peaceful protest is fundamental to democracy and promised a review of police action against anti-SIR demonstrators in Bengaluru.

Activists, however, said assurances were not enough and demanded the withdrawal of the police licensing order restricting protests to Freedom Park and restoration of the 2009 order governing assemblies and processions.

The demand follows Mondayâs detention of protesters who had gathered near KR Circle to march to the chief electoral officerâs office against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Police detained them after they refused to move to Freedom Park, while photojournalists covering the action were also allegedly manhandled.

Kharge said he had instructed police to ensure peaceful demonstrations were not disrupted. Shivakumar said he had sought a full report on the circumstances leading to the police action and warned that accountability would follow if there had been unnecessary use of force or excess.





âThe right to peaceful protest is fundamental to our democracy. We cannot demand that right for ourselves in Delhi and deny it to others in Bengaluru,â Shivakumar said, adding that there would be âno double standardsâ. He, along with Kharge, was in Delhi on Monday to protest against SIR.

Activists welcomed the assurances but said the govt must address the restrictions that, they argue, make it difficult to protest at the site of an issue or draw public attention to local grievances.

âThe Licensing Order, 2021 by the commissioner of police restricting protests to Freedom Park must be withdrawn, just as any restriction to designated venues for protests in any city. Protests cannot be caged in Freedom Park; holding placards and shouting slogans cannot be criminalised; peaceful marches cannot be met with police violence,â advocate and activist Clifton Rozario said.

He added that police power could not be used against legitimate struggles in defence of the Constitution.

My Vote, My Right, which had organised Mondayâs protest march, welcomed Khargeâs decision to review the police handling of protesters and journalists, but urged the govt to withdraw the 2021 licensing order and restore the â2009 assemblies orderâ. The organisation also questioned Shivakumar over what it saw as a contradiction between his participation in a protest in Delhi and the action against demonstrators in Bengaluru, asking: âOne law for you, one law for us â why?â

A woman protester who was forcibly dragged away by police on Monday said restricting demonstrations to Freedom Park curtailed citizensâ rights.

âThis rule is what allows the police to deem any protest outside the said venue, even if it is barely a kilometre away, illegitimate,â she said.

Activists under the Horatada Hakkigagi Janandolana said the restriction had also affected people seeking to raise local issues. A protest over a neighbourhood grievance, they argued, loses its immediate relevance when residents must travel to a central venue to be heard.

They have cited workers, farmers, pourakarmikas, Dalit activists and residents protesting civic issues among those whose demonstrations have been affected.

The coalition was, as of late Tuesday, preparing a fresh memorandum to the govt. On the same as the CM and Khargeâs assurances, Bengaluru police commissioner Seemanth Kumar Singh said KR Circle was a heavily congested junction and police had asked protesters to shift to Freedom Park.

He said the protesters refused and blocked the road, following which police removed the blockade and made preventive arrests.

Acknowledging a confrontation involving protesters, police and media personnel, Singh described it as unintentional and said officers had been instructed to exercise utmost care. He maintained that the right to protest in Bengaluru was, under the courtâs order, limited to Freedom Park, and said police were prepared to provide protection when informed in advance.

Activists insist that reviewing Mondayâs police action must go hand in hand with changing the rules governing where people can demonstrate. World.title: TOI explains: Why can’t Bengaluru protest outside Freedom Park?
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

A Karnataka high court order and a police licensing regime have made Freedom Park Bengaluruâs default protest venue. But the governing police order also gives the police commissioner discretion to designate another suitable venue, meaning the legal position is more nuanced than an absolute ban on demonstrations elsewhere. Hereâs everything you need to know about why Bengaluru cannot protest outside Freedom Park:Bengaluru has confined protests to Freedom Park. The practice emerged from a suo motu Karnataka High Court case initiated in 2021 over the effect of demonstrations on traffic and the rights of people not participating in them.How did the restriction begin?On March 3, 2022, a division bench of the Karnataka High Court passed an interim order directing the state government to ensure that no protests, processions and similar activities were held anywhere in Bengaluru except at Freedom Park, Gandhinagar. The court also directed that such activities be organised without adversely affecting traffic, especially during rush hours, and that action be taken where traffic was disrupted.On August 1, 2022, the High Court disposed of the case. In paragraph 4, it recorded a submission that protests, marches and dharnas would be permitted only at Freedom Park, and that the state was obliged to ensure compliance with the 2021 licensing order.In paragraph 5, the operative direction required authorities to ensure compliance with that order âin letter and spiritâ and to continue action against those violating it.What does the police order say?The Licensing and Regulation of Protests, Demonstrations and Protest Marches (Bengaluru City) Order, 2021, published in the state gazette in January 2022, is the rule currently governing protests in Bengaluru. It says no protests, demonstrations, dharnas or protest marches may be held in the city without a licence under the order.Clause 4.1 identifies Freedom Park as the venue for protests in Bengaluru. However, it also says that, depending on the situation, the commissioner of police may designate any other suitable place in the city for that purpose. The licensing authority may approve the number of participants at Freedom Park based on the type of programme, duration and available capacity.So, are protests outside Freedom Park illegal?Not necessarily in every circumstance. The 2021 order does not expressly prohibit protest marches, nor does it state that Freedom Park is the only possible venue: it identifies Freedom Park while preserving the police commissionerâs discretion to designate another suitable location.A legal backgrounder prepared by activists argues that the High Courtâs final order did not itself direct that protests be held only at Freedom Park; it directed compliance with the licensing order. On that reading, the courtâs judgment does not prevent rallies and does not mandate Freedom Park as the sole venue.The distinction matters because the March 2022 interim order did expressly restrict protests and processions to Freedom Park, while the August 2022 final order required enforcement of the 2021 licensing rules. The two must be read alongside the licensing order before drawing a definitive legal conclusion.Why does this matter?Activists argue that concentrating demonstrations at one venue reduces their visibility and makes it harder for groups to draw public attention to local grievances. The backgrounder says the restrictions have affected workers, farmers, Dalit activists, sanitation workers and residents seeking to protest on issues in their own localities.The debate is ultimately about balancing traffic management and public convenience with the constitutional right to assemble peacefully and express dissent. For now, Freedom Park remains Bengaluruâs designated and practically dominant protest venue. Whether the police commissionerâs discretion to permit demonstrations elsewhere is exercised, and on what terms, remains central to the controversy.

World.title: Patna High Court acquits 13 accused in 1996 Jehanabad quadruple murder case
World.content:
The Patna High Court on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) set aside a trial court’s conviction order and acquitted 13 appellants in a 1996 quadruple murder case.

A Division Bench comprising Justice Rajeev Ranjan Prasad and Justice Kumar Manish delivered the ruling, citing grave lapses in the police investigation, lack of credible identification and a failure by the prosecution to prove guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.

​The case dates back to the intervening night of August 8-9, 1996, in the Karpi area of Jehanabad (now Arwal) district. According to the prosecution, a group of 30 to 40 armed individuals stormed a hut (jhopri) near the Keyal Aahar, where villagers were keeping watch over a water meant for irrigation.

The violent attack claimed the lives of four persons — Bharat Singh, Manger Singh, Ram Niwas Singh, and Nawlesh Singh — while injuring others, including Pramod Kumar.

Initially, an FIR was lodged against unknown extremists of the Mazdoor Kisan Sangram Parishad (MKSP). However, through subsequent supplementary statements and trial proceedings, several residents from the neighbouring Asadhi tola were implicated.

​In April 2023, the Additional District and Sessions Judge-II, Jehanabad, had convicted the appellants under Sections 302/34, 307/34, and 148 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), alongside Section 27 of the Arms Act, sentencing them to rigorous imprisonment for life.

​Challenging this verdict, senior counsels and advocates representing the appellants argued that the prosecution’s case suffered from vital contradictions.

They pointed out that none of the accused was named in the initial FIR despite the informant and witnesses claiming acquaintance with them. Furthermore, crucial material objects—such as torches, blood-soaked soil, and empty cartridge shells (khokha) — were never seized or produced before the court, and no Test Identification Parade (TIP) was ever conducted.

Defence teams also highlighted that the post-mortem reports and doctors who conducted them were never examined during the trial.

​Accepting these contentions, the High Court strongly criticised the investigating agency for a “lacklustre” and compromised investigation. The Bench noted that the sole reliance on dock identification after an 8-year gap, without prior TIP or proper corroboration, violated settled rules of judicial prudence.

​”We are living in an adversarial system of law where hundreds of culprits may go scot-free, but one innocent cannot be hanged,” the Court remarked, invoking the classic jurisprudential principle.

​Expressing deep dismay over recurring shoddy police work in high-profile criminal trials, the High Court issued strict directives to the State administration.

It ordered the Director General of Police (DGP), Bihar, to constitute a three-member committee of senior police officers to probe the gross negligence of the initial investigating officers and take appropriate administrative action within three months.

Additionally, the Home Department was directed to review its policy on handling acquittals caused by investigative lapses. With the convictions annulled, the Court ordered the immediate release of the appellants unless they are wanted in any other case.

World.title: Pope Leo has lung cancer, lower lobe of right lung removed: Vatican
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV's surgery confirmed that he has lung cancer, and he had the lower lobe of his right lung removed, the Vatican said Tuesday (October 13, 2026).

The tests confirmed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, the Vatican said in a medical bulletin after the surgery. It said the diagnosis had been suspected by preoperative tests and was confirmed during surgery.

The 71-year-old was in the operating room for about 3 hours, the statement said. The surgery itself lasted approximately 90 minutes. “The surgery was successful, and there were no complications,” the statement said.

Leo had walked into Rome's Gemelli Hospital through the main entrance earlier in the day and waved to dozens of well-wishers who had gathered to greet him. The Vatican said the surgery would be performed by a team led by Gemelli's chief thoracic surgeon, Dr. Stefano Margaritora.

The American pontiff has offered a rare level of transparency about the first publicly disclosed major health problem of his 17-month papacy. He revealed the discovery of the small, localised nodule during his Sunday noon prayer and announced that he would have it removed.

The Vatican on Monday cancelled all Leo's audiences through Oct 20.

But the decision to have the operation clearly came as a surprise: While Gemelli has a specific papal apartment that past popes have used, complete with a private chapel on the 10th floor, Leo will actually be staying in a nearby room since the papal apartment is currently undergoing renovations, according to the Vatican press office.

World.title: Former Madhya Pradesh CM Shivraj Singh Chouhan’s twin remarks fuel buzz of rift within State BJP unit
World.content:
Two statements from former Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan on Sunday — one a sharp rebuke and the other a soft political reminder — were enough to heat up the State’s politics and fuel speculation that all may not be well within the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The latest row hints at mounting pressure on Chief Minister Mohan Yadav amid reports of differences between him and other senior party leaders, including Cabinet Ministers and State BJP president Hemant Khandelwal.

Mr. Chouhan, now Union Agriculture Minister, sharply criticised the State government over the demolition of houses of 12 tribal families and destruction of their crops at Kosmi village in Vidisha, his Lok Sabha constituency. The remarks are being seen as a message of his discontent with his successor’s administration. The eviction drive, carried out on grounds of alleged encroachment on forest land, was undertaken despite Mr. Chouhan having intervened in the matter on Sunday morning.

However, another statement made by him at an event in neighbouring Raisen district on the same day may hold greater political relevance. It centred on women, who form a large part of his personal support base as well as the BJP’s voter base, and is being seen as a direct response to Mr. Yadav’s recent comments on the BJP’s flagship Ladli Behna scheme, which provides a monthly allowance of ₹1,500 to eligible women.

Referring to the scheme that he launched in his final year as Chief Minister in 2023, Mr. Chouhan said, “The Chief Minister has continued this scheme and every government will have to keep it going. Sabko pata hai ki behenein gussa ho gayi toh phir khair nahi hai [Everybody knows that if sisters get angry, you are done for].”

He then sought a response from the women in the gathering on how much they wanted the allowance to be raised. “Yes, ₹3,000. It will increase gradually. Brothers, don’t be troubled, let the sisters move ahead. This is a campaign to change lives. Thanks to the Chief Minister too,” he said, in his familiar style of engaging with supporters. The remarks came a week after Mr. Yadav had said in jest at an event on October 4 that the scheme had proved to be a “very expensive affair”.

Mr. Chouhan has often intervened in matters concerning tribal people and women in the past.

Political observers who have followed Mr. Chouhan’s politics see various women-centric schemes as his legacy, which earned him the sobriquet ‘Mama (maternal uncle)’. A day after Mr. Chouhan extended his support to the tribals of Kosmi and joined their sit-in, his son Kartikeya Singh Chouhan also joined the protest on Monday night and spent hours with them.

‘Calculated move’

Observers and BJP insiders believe that the timing of Mr. Chouhan upping the ante and the variation in tone of his two remarks could be a “deliberate and calculated” move by the former Chief Minister, who is known for his soft, conversational style while addressing gatherings.

A senior BJP leader in Bhopal explained, “Shivrajji is well aware of the current power dynamic in the State BJP and that resentment is rising against the man who replaced him [Mr. Yadav]. So, his statements could be a calculated move to put his weight behind that resentment and add to the Chief Minister’s pressure. He also specifically said that he spoke to the State [BJP] president [on the razing of tribal houses] because he knows of the recent rumours of differences between him and the Chief Minister.”

The leader, who requested anonymity, also pointed out that Mr. Chouhan’s “unusually harsh words” for Forest Department officials over the eviction drive hold significance as Mr. Yadav himself heads the department.

While reports of various Ministers being disgruntled with Mr. Yadav’s style of functioning have surfaced frequently during his almost three-year tenure, rumours of differences between him and Mr. Khandelwal have emerged recently, including over the invitee list for a State BJP core committee meeting held earlier in October. Several senior leaders such as Narottam Mishra and Gopal Bhargava were missing from the meeting attended by the recently appointed Madhya Pradesh BJP in-charge Biplab Kumar Deb.

Senior journalist and political observer Rashid Kidwai also linked Mr. Chouhan’s recent remarks to his efforts to remain “relevant in the State while growing his stature in the national BJP”.

“This seems to be an interplay of what is happening in State and national politics. Shivraj knows that he is only important in Delhi as long as he remains relevant in Madhya Pradesh. He is known to be an obedient BJP karyakarta (worker) who barely breaches the discipline line set by the party. So, he seems to be trying to stay connected to State politics and protect what he sees as his legacy without baffling anyone in the party high command,” Mr. Kidwai said.

He also pointed out that while the BJP has many regional satraps in Madhya Pradesh, Mr. Chouhan could be the only leader with a pan-State appeal. “And he wants to keep it that way.”

Mr. Kidwai also said that a power tussle within the ruling party was “natural where the Chief Minister, though he enjoys the BJP high command’s backing, has many heavyweights and leaders senior to him across the State”.

He said the CM’s relevance, including his ‘Yadav’ credentials, should be seen in view of the important 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly poll. “Mohan Yadav’s relevance will depend on the U.P. election results, whether they are in the BJP’s favour or not. Till then, he may continue to enjoy Delhi’s backing as he has these past three years,” he said.

Mr. Yadav, however, has not condemned the eviction drive but said that an inquiry would clear the air.

“I am seeing a report from the officials and have also told the Chief Secretary [about it]. Our government is a sensitive one and if our senior has raised something, there is nothing wrong in conducting an inquiry. Doodh ka doodh aur paani ka paani ho jayega (The truth will come out),” he said, responding to a question on Mr. Chouhan’s remarks.

The Opposition Congress, meanwhile, has linked the Kosmi incident directly to a “power tussle”. “This action, taking place on the orders of those in power, is a new chapter in the open conflict brewing between the Chief Ministers of the BJP. The former Chief Minister had already instructed the district administration and Forest Department not to take any action. Despite this, the homes of the poor have been torn down,” State unit chief Jitu Patwari said.

“The poor tribals will not pay the price for the internal strife and tug-of-war within the Madhya Pradesh BJP,” he said.

World.title: Saudi coalition strikes Yemen oil sites after Houthi attacks
World.content:
The Saudi-led coalition battling the Iran-backed Houthis struck oil sites across western Yemen on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) including in the capital Sanaa, in response to the deadliest attack on the Kingdom’s soil in years.

Blasts were heard shortly after in Saudi capital Riyadh and at an oil giant Aramco facility in eastern Saudi Arabia, witnesses and journalists told AFP.

The coalition said it intercepted several Houthi missiles targeting the Kingdom, including Riyadh, adding that debris fell in a residential area in Dhahran, which hosts Aramco’s headquarters.

Tuesday’s (October 13, 2026) coalition strikes in Yemen’s Sanaa and the western provinces of Dhamar and Saada targeted facilities used to “supply the war effort” by the Houthis to “threaten the kingdom, Yemen, the southern Red Sea and waterways”, coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki wrote on X.

A powerful explosion then rang out in the Saudi capital, with a phone alert sent to residents saying “the city of Riyadh is facing a hostile aerial threat”.

While walking down a major avenue in Riyadh, a witness told AFP he “saw a projectile cutting across the sky” above a mall, saying it left “a yellowish trail of light followed by a trail of smoke. Then, we heard an explosion.”

“People were calm; no one was speaking. We were scared and all looking up at the sky,” he added, requesting anonymity.

After Houthi strikes on Saudi airports and energy sites in recent days, the coalition issued its first evacuation order in the Yemeni capital since the war flared in July, before attacking the Yemen Petroleum Company facility on Sanaa’s outskirts.

An AFP correspondent in Sanaa reported an explosion, while a breaking news alert on the Houthi-affiliated Al-Masirah TV channel said “Saudi aggression” targeted the oil firm.

Renewed threats

A strike on Riyadh’s international airport on Saturday left 13 people dead and operations suspended in the worst attack since 2015.

The Saudi cabinet vowed in a meeting earlier Tuesday (October 13, 2026), led by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, that it “will not allow its security or freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab Strait to be threatened”.

An AFP correspondent reported that many civilians in Sanaa fearing shortages rushed to queue in front of fuel stations after the coalition warning.

The Houthis had earlier issued a new threat to target Riyadh’s international airport, a refinery, and an Aramco facility in Dammam if the strike went ahead, calling for citizens to avoid them.

Many countries have issued travel warnings to their citizens in Saudi Arabia, most recently France, which told its citizens to avoid Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam airports.

The Saudi-led coalition has supported Yemen’s government militarily against the Houthis since 2015 in a long-running civil war that has created a dire humanitarian crisis.

Economic woes

Traffic in perennially gridlocked Riyadh was noticeably lighter this week, as remote learning for all schools and work-from-home orders for some companies took effect, according to AFP journalists.

Saudi Arabia faces a major economic contraction this year with GDP expected to shrink 3.3%, the International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday, predicting a regional drop over Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

The Kingdom was already facing headwinds from Iran’s chokehold on the Hormuz strait since the start of the West Asia war in February, when the US and Israel attacked Iran.

But the restart in July of Yemen’s frozen war has further roiled the kingdom and brought the fight to its own soil.

Houthi attacks have also targeted oil tankers in the Red Sea — Saudi Arabia’s alternative export route.

In Yemen, the renewed fighting was fuelling the risk of infectious disease outbreaks.

Suspected cholera cases tripled there in three weeks, the World Health Organization said Tuesday, warning that the growing disease burden was straining hospitals already treating war casualties.

‘Behaving very badly’

The Riyadh airport attack had prompted U.S. President Donald Trump to say he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis.

He wrote on his Truth Social platform on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) that “the Houthis are behaving very badly”, accusing them of acting “probably at the behest of Iran”.

“I’ll be there after the elections, and I will never forget!” he wrote, referring to next month’s midterms.

The Houthis warned the U.S. against intervention, with political bureau member Mohammed Al Bukhaiti telling AFP they would target American interests in the region.

Bukhaiti said the purpose of the campaign against Saudi targets was to send a message to the crown prince “that he can no longer wage aggression against Yemen from a safe position”.

World.title: Over a dozen children dead after boat capsizes in Bihar’s Vaishali
World.content:
At least 13 children died after a boat capsized in the Ganga River in Vaishali district of Bihar, under Raghopur police station area on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) night.

The boat was ferrying villagers to another village, where they were to attend a feast. According to locals, the feast had been organised at the home of a person named Singheshwar Rai, near the Mata Maharani Sthan in Bhagtan Tola (Rampur Shyamchand Panchayat), and around 20 people were travelling on a small boat.

VIDEO | Vaishali, Bihar: Boat carrying 15–20 people capsizes in Ganga near Raghopur; Several feared dead. More details awaited. (Source: Third Party) #Bihar https://t.co/ZMVLjjT9yV — Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) October 13, 2026

According to Vaishali District Magistrate Varsha Singh, seven people have been rescued and referred to Nalanda Medical College and Hospital (NMCH). She added that all the children on the boat were aged 15 or younger.

“The rescue operation will continue throughout the night. The SDRF team and local divers are also on site. So far, 13 dead bodies have been recovered,” she said.

Some of the rescued have been referred for better treatment to Patna.

When Varsha Singh reached the local hospital to check on the situation, she was met by angry locals, who shouted slogans against the district administration.

PM Modi, Bihar CM announce ex-gratia

Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary expressed grief over the incident in a post on X. He also announced ex-gratia for the family members of the deceased.

“The news of the innocent lives lost in the boat accident in Raghopur, Vaishali, is extremely heartbreaking and soul-wrenching. In this difficult time, my deepest condolences are with the bereaved families. May God grant peace to the departed souls and provide the families with the strength to bear this immense sorrow,” Mr. Choudhary wrote.

He further wrote, “From the State government, an assistance of ₹4-lakh each [ex gratia amount] will be provided to the families of the deceased. Instructions have been given to the administration to swiftly complete relief and rescue operations and ensure better treatment for the injured.”

Separately, Prime Minister Narendra Modi also announced an ex-gratia of ₹2 lakh from the PMNRF to be given to the next of kin of each of those who lost their lives. The injured would be given ₹50,000

“The loss of lives in the boat capsizing incident in Vaishali, Bihar, is deeply painful. My thoughts are with the bereaved families in this difficult time. I pray for the speedy recovery of all those injured. The local administration is assisting those affected,” the Prime Minister said in a post on X.

Raghopur MLA and Leader of Opposition in Bihar Legislative Assembly Tejashwi Yadav also expressed deep grief over the incident by posting a video message on X. “I am deeply shocked by the heart-wrenching incident of the boat capsizing in Raghopur. May God grant peace to the departed souls and strength to the grieving families to bear this sorrow. At present, I am in Delhi to take part in the INDIA bloc meeting and tomorrow, as soon as I reach Patna, I will go to my constituency to meet the aggrieved family members,” Mr. Yadav said.

World.title: Delhi govt. makes Aadhaar mandatory for electricity subsidy
World.content:
The Delhi government has made it mandatory for domestic consumers to share Aadhaar details to avail of the benefits under the power subsidy scheme.

A notification issued by the Power Department on September 30 states that those seeking electricity subsidy must furnish their Aadhaar number through a government portal or any other mode prescribed by the government. Those who don’t yet have an Aadhaar can apply using their Aadhaar Enrolment ID.

It directs the implementing agencies to publicise the information so that beneficiaries are aware of the new condition.

The electricity subsidy scheme is administered through five power discoms — BSES Rajdhani Power Limited, BSES Yamuna Power Limited, Tata Power Delhi Distribution Limited, the New Delhi Municipal Council and the Military Engineer Services.

The notification states that the expenditure on the electricity subsidy scheme is met from the Consolidated Fund of Delhi and that Aadhaar-based identification is necessary to establish the identity of those receiving the benefit.

The move is aimed at simplifying the delivery of benefits, reducing the need for multiple identity documents and promoting transparency and efficiency in the subsidy system, the department said.

The notification does not specify a deadline for existing beneficiaries to submit their Aadhaar details nor does it spell out a separate procedure for consumers already receiving the benefit.

In August, the government tabled a Comptroller and Auditor General report in the Assembly on “lapses” in the scheme under the Aam Aadmi Party. The scheme’s cost rose from ₹2,405.59 crore in 2019-20 to ₹3,161 crore in 2022-23, accounting for up to 70.39% of Delhi’s total subsidy expense, it stated.

World.title: Jantar Mantar denotified as protest site based on SC order: police to High Court
World.content:
The Delhi police on Tuesday told the Delhi High Court that the decision to denotify Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site was taken based on the Supreme Court’s directions.

Representing the police, Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma told Justice Amit Mahajan, who was hearing a plea by the Indian Youth Congress seeking permission to protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar, that the “entire petition is about peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar. All other prayers flow from it. Today, we have denotified Jantar Mantar pursuant to orders of the Supreme Court”. He added that a plea had been filed in the apex court challenging the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a protest site.

Sidharth Luthra, the counsel for the petitioner, said he would amend the plea in view of the development and urged the court to seek the police’s stand on the other plea, which is against “automatic, mechanical, unguided or disproportionate prohibition of peaceful assembly”.

It also challenges the requirement to apply for a protest at least 10 days before the proposed date.

Meanwhile, hundreds of protesters from several youth organisations staged demonstrations in Connaught Place against the decision to denotify Jantar Mantar as a protest site.

The outfits included Bhim Army, Revolutionary Workers’ Party of India and Disha Students’ Organisation (DSO).

‘Reclaim Jantar Mantar’

Two other outfits — the Students’ Federation of India and the Democratic Youth Federation of India — condemned the order in a joint statement, denouncing the “blow to democratic dissent and the constitutional right to peaceful assembly”. They would mobilise the youth and democratic forces to “reclaim Jantar Mantar”, it added.

“Jantar Mantar belongs to people. Denotifying it as a protest site would not stop the public from protesting there. The government wants to send protesters off to places such as Burari far away from Parliament,” said Naureen from DSO. “It is time for all organisations to come together on the issue,” said Chiranshu from Naujawan Bharat Sabha.

World.title: After route diversions, commuters face reduced DTC services with hundreds of buses pulled for protest duty
World.content:
Commuters in Delhi are facing a twin challenge due to the protest-related restrictions: diversions that have disrupted vehicular movement and reduced Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) services, with hundreds of buses deployed for police duty.

‘600 buses taken off’

The government has not shared details on how many buses have been withdrawn from regular routes for deployment with security agencies in central Delhi. However, the DTC Ekta Karamchari Union, which comprises contractual and outsourced employees of the public transporter, said at least 600 buses had been deployed to transport security personnel or detainees.

“The bus service has reduced over the past two days. The service is irregular anyway as buses either don’t stop or are delayed. If this is due to the protests, then the DTC should have made separate arrangements for passengers,” said Ram Gopal, who works at an establishment in Karol Bagh.

Route diversions near Jantar Mantar also caused problems for commuters.

Ankita, a third-year Delhi University student, said she had to walk to reach her destination at Patel Chowk after the DTC bus dropped her 2 kilometre away from the designated bus stop.

Since October 2, specific routes around Connaught Place, Patel Chowk and Janpath have been diverted owing to security restrictions.

The union president, Lalit Chaudhary, said, “Some routes around Jantar Mantar, Bangla Sahib Gurdwara, Patel Chowk, Sansad Marg and Janpath have been diverted. Buses from depots of Rani Khera and Dichaon Kalan in Najafgarh have been pulled in for protests, to transport security personnel and detainees or to be used as barricades in restricted areas where prohibitory orders have been enforced.”

‘Own workers affected’

While the drivers have been asked to work for the police, conductors have been deployed for various other duties.

“Some have been deputed far away from their homes and are facing difficulty in commuting to their workplaces,” Mr. Chaudhary said. Major service disruptions have been reported on DTC routes such as 433, 445A, 415, 417, 423 and 930.

World.title: PM Shehbaz takes allies into confidence on KP governor's rule, says Centre made every effort to avoid 'extreme step'
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday took the allies of the ruling PML-N into confidence on the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, saying that the Centre had made every effort to avoid this “extreme step”.

The Centre on Sunday imposed governor’s rule in KP and emergency in 12 of its districts, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.

PM Shehbaz held a meeting with leaders of the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P), as well as a separate huddle with a parliamentary delegation comprising representatives of PML-Q, Balochistan Awami Party (BAP), Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party (IPP) and PML-Zia.

During the meeting with the MQM-P delegation led by Education Minister Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui, the two sides exchanged views on the country’s overall and political situation, the PM Office (PMO) said.

The prime minister said the government had to take this “most difficult decision” in the interest of the people of KP.

“We made every effort to avoid taking this extreme step in any way. We engaged in negotiations with an open heart, but did not receive a positive response from the other side,” he was quoted as saying.

The premier noted that rising terrorist attacks in KP were targeting ordinary citizens and security forces, while the provincial government “failed to openly raise its voice against terrorist groups”.

PM Shehbaz also termed the PTI’s long march a “conspiracy to destroy the country’s improving economy”.

According to PMO, the MQM-P delegation assured the prime minister of its full support for the government’s decisions regarding KP.

On the MQM’s side, the delegation included Health Minister Mustafa Kamal, Senator Amir Waliuddin Chishti, Senator Khalida Ateeb, MNA Farooq Sattar, Syed Waseem Hussain, Aasia Ishaque Siddiqui, Javed Hanif Khan, Muhammad Moeen Aamir Pirzada, Muhammad Iqbal Khan, Hassan Sabir, Sadiq Iftikhar, Arshad Abdullah Vohra, Syed Hafizuddin, Syed Aminul Haque, Khawaja Azharul Hassan, Ahmad Saleem Siddiqui, Farhan Chishti, Nighat Shakeel Khan, Sabheen Ghoury, Rana Ansar, Sofia Saeed Shah, and Sanjay Perwani.

In the second meeting with other parties, PM Shehbaz explained the reasons behind the federal government’s decision to take constitutional measures, state-run APP reported.

He said the conduct of the PTI-led KP government in the province and its failure to adopt an unequivocal stance against terrorism had posed risks to Pakistan’s growing economy.

The premier highlighted that the federal government had provided more than Rs800 billion to KP under the National Finance Commission (NFC) arrangements to support efforts against terrorism.

However, he said, the provincial government had failed to take effective measures to strengthen the capacity of its Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) and establish Safe City projects to improve its counterterrorism capabilities.

According to the PM’s Office, the parliamentary delegation expressed its support for the federal government amid the prevailing situation and appreciated the prime minister’s leadership during what it described as difficult circumstances.

The delegation also said the people of KP had remained deprived of adequate development in health, education and infrastructure during the PTI’s tenure in the province.

It expressed confidence that, with the federal government’s cooperation, development and prosperity in KP would advance in line with other parts of the country.

The delegation included BAP President and Science and Technology Minister Khalid Magsi; former Senate chairman Sadiq Sanjrani of BAP, senators Manzoor Kakar, Abdul Qadir Baloch, Dinesh Kumar and Samina Mumtaz Zehri; PML-Q President and Human Resource Development Minister Chaudhry Salik Hussain; and representatives of the IPP and PML-Zia.

From the government, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry and PM’s Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah attended both meetings.

‘What other path did we have?’

Later, he addressed a parliamentary meeting of his PML-N and said, “When terrorism is spreading, sacrifices are being made day and night, and this party (PTI) is exhausting all its resources and time round the clock to create instability.”

The premier emphasised that the people of KP had been wanting “projects of development and prosperity for the past 13 years”, such as schools, universities, hospitals, better law and order, and an end to corruption.

However, he contended, there was “not zero, but negative attention” towards these matters, and “all attention and resources” were instead diverted towards long marches and protests.

“Can any respectable society tolerate this? Even the question does not arise. So what other path did we have?” he asked, quipping if the Centre should have remained as “silent spectators”.

The prime minister noted that the Centre was “compelled to make this decision” after the Oct 3 talks between the government and the opposition collapsed.

Elaborating on the dialogue process, PM Shehbaz said, “There was a moment when it was set in stone that an agreement was about to be reached, all demands were settled.”

He added that a consensus-based draft was ready, but the PTI team sought some more time to consult Sohail Afridi — the KP chief minister whose role now stands non-functional.

“The rest is history. […] They were ordered that you have to create another May 9, even go beyond it and wreak havoc; you must not accept anything,” the premier added.

He went on to recall his engagement with Jamiat Ulemai-i-Islam–Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman to reduce tensions, which was followed by the Oct 11 cabinet meeting.

“After all consultations and arguments, it was decided that this is the moment to save Pakistan. We must not wait any further, else everything will be set on fire and we will be left with regret.”

PM Shehbaz reiterated, “We were compelled to make the decision of imposing emergency. This is no other choice because Pakistan is first.”

He expressed his hope that the newly appointed KP Advisory Council, which will work under the governor, would work to improve the living conditions and safety in the province.

The prime minister asserted that terrorism had been eradicated in most parts of the country several years ago, but had resurged recently.

He lamented that law enforcers were being martyred daily in KP and Balochistan. “If this bloodshed is not brought to an end like it was in 2018, then the journey of development made in the past 2.5 years… this journey is continuing gradually.”

“If one provincial government is not only determined to end that journey […] but that party is determined on destruction and comes to thinking that if they make progress, what will be our value; how regrettable it is.”

The prime minister recalled the November 2024 protest by the PTI in Islamabad, as well as its 2014 rallies at the federal capital’s D-Chowk.

“When someone is bent on ending the country’s progress, they are engaged in sit-ins, verbal abuse and allegations, instead of standing with the Centre and the armed forces and empowering the police and CTD,” he said.

PM Shehbaz said even an enemy would not make the remarks made by Afridi in recent weeks. He criticised the PTI leader for not expressing sympathies with the martyrs’ families and for “not willing to say a single word” against terrorists.

At the outset of his address, the premier highlighted his government’s efforts to cooperate with the PTI-led governments in KP.

He recalled his meeting with former KP chief minister Ali Amin Gandapur, saying, “We told him in every way that we will cooperate with them … combatting terrorism is our shared responsibility.”

He noted that he had also met with Sohail Afridi — whose role as the KP CM is currently non-functional due to governor’s rule — and asserted that the Centre tried its best to work with the KP government.

At one point, the premier said International Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva recently told him, “This is a new Pakistan”, as she praised the country’s economic reforms.

He recalled his meetings last month with international financial institutions and stressed that praise from such independent firms for Pakistan “restored” his faith in the country’s progress.

World.title: PTI protest in KP's Bara turns violent as demonstrators clash with police
World.content:
KHYBER: A protest demonstration by the PTI workers in Khyber’s Bara tehsil turned violent on Tuesday as protesters clashed with police and government buildings were set ablaze.

There were reports of police firing live rounds and tear gas and protesters manhandling law enforcers. Dawn was able to confirm injuries to at least five protesters, based on accounts by eyewitnesses, who asked not to be named, while police said 50 people had been arrested.

However, a doctor at Hayatabad Medical Complex, one of the city’s three major hospitals, told Dawn that more than a dozen injured, including four policemen, had been brought to the facility.

The protest was held against the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkwa — a move that has rendered PTI’s Sohail Afridi non-functional as the province’s chief minister — and emergency in 12 of its districts, including Khyber.

Scores of PTI workers assembled at the Khyber Chowk in Bara Bazaar in the afternoon for the protest, following which police reached the site.

There were reports of police initially resorting to baton-charge and tear gas shelling to disperse protesters. Eyewitnesses told Dawn that police managed to disperse some protesters but later local MPA Abdul Ghani Afridi also reached the site with more PTI supporters.

The protesters forced police to retreat, with some of the law enforcers taking shelter in nearby shops and commercial buildings, according to eyewitnesses. Reports received from the area said protesters manhandled police and dragged them out of shops, following which law enforcers fired tear gas shells and live rounds in the air.

There were also reports of the nearby National Database and Registration Authority’s office and a portion of the Rescue 1122 building being torched.

Police eventually dispersed the protesters from Khyber Chowk but all roads leading to Bara Bazaar were closed even as the demonstration ended.

Meanwhile, leaders of the Bara Siyasi Ittehad urged both PTI workers and police to avoid violent confrontation.

Arrests

Capital City Police Peshawar said in a statement that 50 “miscreant elements” in Bara who “attempted to spread unrest” had been arrested.

Separately, the newly appointed adviser on information and broadcasting in KP, Samar Haroon Bilour, said, “Forty-two PTI-affiliated miscreants associated with vandalism and unrest have been arrested, of whom 25 are illegal Afghans.”

She accused the protesters of damaging public and government property.

The adviser alleged that some individuals, reportedly led by PTI leaders, attempted to create unrest at Bara Chowk.

She added that police made arrests over the incident and brought the situation under control.

Dawn could not independently verify the number of arrests, the extent of the damage and the nationality and immigration status of those detained.

World.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs2.71 per litre, high-speed diesel rate by Re0.03
World.content:
The government on Tuesday reduced the price of petrol by Rs2.71 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs0.03 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs392.66 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs396.82 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 14 (Wednesday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: PTI's Ali Zafar terms governor's rule in KP 'political crisis disguised as security solution'; ministers defend move
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Treasury and opposition members in the Senate debated the governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Tuesday, with PTI’s Barrister Ali Zafar terming the development a “political crisis disguised as a security solution” while federal ministers defended the move.

The Centre on Sunday imposed governor’s rule in KP and emergency in 12 of its districts, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The proclamations now require Parliament’s approval.

It was against this backdrop that National Assembly and Senate sessions were convened on Tuesday.

In the Senate, PTI’s Parliamentary Leader in the Senate Barrister Ali Zafar remarked that what was happening in KP was not merely an administrative decision but a “test of Pakistan’s Constitution”.

“The Constitution must be our shield in a crisis, not a casualty of the crisis. The question is: are we using the Constitution to protect Pakistan, or are we using an emergency to change the political order of Pakistan?” he said.

Zafar said no political party or patriotic Pakistani wanted terrorism to flourish and that terrorism must be defeated with full strength. “But we must defeat terrorism without allowing the fight against terrorism to become a fight against constitutional democracy,” he said.

Referring to the constitutional provisions related to governor’s rule and emergency, he said Article 232 was to be employed in the situation of emergency and not as a “political weapon”.

Similarly, Article 234 provided for extraordinary arrangements intended for extraordinary circumstances, he added.

“Their existence does not mean they could be exercised without limits. The government must demonstrate that the constitutional conditions [for emergency and governor’s rule] have genuinely been met, that the action is necessary and proportionate, and that every applicable procedure has been followed. The existence of an emergency power does not place its exercise above the Constitution,” he said.

Zafar further argued that the Centre could not simply declare that a provincial government could no longer function constitutionally and treat that declaration as the end argument. The legal basis, evidence, scope and consequences must withstand scrutiny, and courts must remain free to determine legality, he asserted.

“If the government’s case is that terrorism has created an extraordinary situation in particular districts, it must explain why its response extended to the entire province and what safeguards protected the rest,” he added.

The PTI alleged that “this is a political crisis disguised as a security solution”, pointing to the timing of the measure that came amid heightened political tensions and a breakdown of the dialogue between the government and the opposition, including the PTI, in the Centre.

“You cannot restore public confidence by making people believe that their elected mandate can be taken away in the name of security,” he said.

Zafar said the issue concerned provincial autonomy, federalism, elected representation, fundamental rights and the balance between the federation and its units.

“Once extraordinary powers are normalised against one political opponent, no province and no party can assume it will never be the next one. Today it may be KP; tomorrow the precedent may be used elsewhere,” he warned.

Calling on the Senate not to become a “rubber stamp”, he said Parliament, which represented the federation and gave every province an equal voice, must examine legal grounds, demand evidence and scrutinise necessity and proportionality for the measures in KP.

“You may control the administration, but you cannot command democratic legitimacy. You may suspend a government, issue notifications and deploy the machinery of the state, but you cannot manufacture public trust by force.

“If emergency is genuinely about protecting citizens, prove it through lawful, targeted and accountable action. If it becomes an instrument to suppress an elected mandate, the damage will outlast this government,” he said.

Zafar added, “The Constitution is not an obstacle to national security; it is the foundation of national security. Break that foundation in the name of protecting Pakistan, and you may win control for a day but you will weaken the state for years to come.”

Leader of the Opposition in Senate Raja Nasir Abbas termed Oct 11, when emergency and governor’s rule was imposed in KP, a “black day”, ruing celebrations by the “champions of democracy over the removal of a democratic government elected with two-thirds majority”.

He maintained that an agreement between the Centre and the opposition had been reached on political issues, claiming that differences arose over linking security issues with political issues.

He warned that “unnecessary violence” created hatred against the state among youth and urged the immediate withdrawal of the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency, as well as the resolution of issues through dialogue.

Political matters could have been resolved by giving more time to negotiations, he added.

Ministers defend governor’s rule

For his part, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi maintained that imposition of governor’s rule and emergency in KP was not in violation of the Constitution.

“The PML-N and PPP sat together and examined every clause to ensure that no provision was violated,” he said, adding that the decision was not an easy one.

He said talks between the Centre and the opposition had focused on terrorism from the first day.

The minister added that the Centre had contacted the PTI leadership, including party Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan, on Oct 10, asking him to suggest amendments in the draft that was to be signed between the two sides after the talks. “Had an agreement been reached, this step would not have been taken,” he said.

Naqvi said the government made six amendments in the draft, which was sent to KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, who has become non-functional as the provincial chief executive following the imposition of governor’s rule. The interior minister alleged that Afridi forwarded the draft to PTI leader Murad Saeed, after which the matter was “sabotaged”.

Referring to security situation in KP, he said law enforcement and security personnel were laying down their lives while the “chief minister was delivering speeches against them”. He alleged that some in the PTI were in “contact with the Taliban and the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan”, adding that evidence of this would be presented when required.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar also spoke in the House, saying that the federal cabinet had “rightly decided” last week to end the process of political reconciliation with the PTI.

He stressed that the PPP and PML-N had both made efforts to reach a point of understanding with the PTI.

Regarding arguments that terrorism was also prevalent in Balochistan while emergency and governor’s rule were only in KP, he highlighted that the Balochistan government was “fully on board” with the Centre in fighting terrorism.

“Whatever has happened is according to the law and Constitution,” he contented.

Parliament approval for governor’s rule

President Asif Ali Zardari had on Sunday issued proclamations of emergency and governor’s rule under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, respectively.

According to Article 232, in case the president “acts on his own” — which was not the case for KP as he acted on PM Shehbaz’s advice — the proclamation of emergency is to be placed before both houses of Parliament for approval by each house within 10 days.

It also empowers Parliament “to make laws for a province, or any part thereof, with respect to any matter not enumerated in the Federal Legislative List” during emergency.

Meanwhile, a proclamation for governor’s rule issued under Article 234 “shall be laid before a joint sitting and shall cease to be in force at the expiration of two months, unless before the expiration of that period it has been approved by resolution of the joint sitting and may by like resolution be extended for a further period not exceeding two months at a time”.

In the upper house, Senator Kamran Murtaza of the Jamiat Ulemai-i-Islam–Fazl (JUI-F) had submitted a resolution on Monday opposing the imposition of governor’s rule in KP.

NA session

An NA session was also held on Tuesday, but concluded without any significant development.

When the session began at around 7pm, NA Speaker Ayaz Sadiq administered the oath of membership to PML-N’s Malik Munir Iqbal Channar, who won the Bahawalpur polls last month held to fill the seat of his late father Malik Muhammad Iqbal Channar.

Lawmakers then offered prayers for late MNA Chaudhry Mahmood Bashir Virk, who died last month after a prolonged illness.

As MNAs from various parties took their turns to recall the services of Virk, there was slight commotion, which prompted the speaker to urge PTI Chairman Gohar Ali Khan to respect the late MNA.

Gohar remarked that sessions are usually adjourned after prayers for a deceased member. Referring to the governor’s rule in KP, he said the “funeral of this house was also held on Oct 11”.

“We tried to give you very much in dialogue, but you (PTI) were not ready to take what we had offered,” the speaker replied, then switched off Gohar’s mic.

The speaker said political discussion will not be allowed today, but tomorrow (Wednesday).

PPP’s Syed Naveed Qamar also urged the PTI chairman to acknowledge the services of Virk, who had stood by the Constitution. He said the PTI could raise its issues later as well.

Lawmakers then continued to pay tribute to Virk, with Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal among those who highlighted his professional life.

The proceedings were then adjourned till 11am on Wednesday.

PTI seeks production orders for 9 MNAs

Earlier in the day, the PTI requested the NA speaker to issue production orders for its nine “detained” MNAs ahead of NA and Senate sessions on Tuesday.

In a letter to NA Speaker Sadiq, Chief Whip Amir Dogar claimed that the nine MNAs were “currently detained” and requested him to issue production orders for them to enable them to attend the 30th session starting today.

The lawmakers comprised Haji Imtiaz Ahmad Choudhry (ΝΑ-68), Muhammad Jamal Ahsan Khan (NA-89), Mian Ghous Muhammad (ΝΑ-170), Sanaullah Khan Mastikhel (NΑ-91), Dawar Khan Kundi (NA-43), Junaid Akbar (NA-09), Amjad Ali Khan (NA-02), Fazal Muhammad Khan (ΝΑ-25) and Adil Khan Bazai (NA-262).

“As the speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan, the impartiality of your esteemed office requires that production orders be issued for all detained members, irrespective of their political affiliation, to ensure that no constituency remains unrepresented during the proceedings of the House,” the letter read.

It requested Sadiq to issue the production orders under Rule 108 of the 2007 Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the National Assembly.

World.title: Kusal Mendis' blistering 87 leads Sri Lanka to consolation win over Pakistan in third T20I
World.content:
Sri Lankan captain Kusal Mendis produced a blistering unbeaten 87 off 48 balls to steer the visitors to an eight-wicket consolation victory over Pakistan in the third Twenty20 International at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Tuesday.

Chasing 169, Sri Lanka cruised to 172-2 in 17.1 overs, with Kusal and Kamindu Mendis combining in an unbroken 98-run partnership for the third wicket to complete the chase with 17 balls to spare.

Kamindu remained unbeaten on 40 off 27 deliveries, striking four fours, as Sri Lanka ended the series on a winning note after Pakistan had secured the first two matches.

The visitors never looked in trouble once the two batters settled at the crease, maintaining a scoring rate of more than 10 runs an over through much of the latter half of the innings.

Kusal’s commanding knock included nine fours and four sixes, as he repeatedly found gaps and punished Pakistan’s wayward bowling. His innings featured a mixture of powerful drives, deft improvisation and clean hitting down the ground, leaving the hosts unable to stem the flow of runs.

Sri Lanka suffered an early setback when Lahiru Udara was trapped leg-before-wicket by Imran Randhawa for one in the second over. Imran produced a delivery that swung sharply from wide of off stump to strike the left-hander on the back pad, giving Pakistan an encouraging start.

However, Sineth Jayawardena and Kusal quickly shifted the momentum. Jayawardena attacked from the outset, striking Salman Mirza for a six over deep midwicket and carving another delivery over point for four. Kusal joined the charge with a straight six off Razaullah before delicately ramping a short ball over the slip cordon.

The pair took Sri Lanka to 59-1 at the end of the powerplay, their best such return of the series, with Jayawardena contributing 30 off 18 balls and Kusal 24 off 16.

Jayawardena continued to find boundaries, pulling Imran over deep midwicket for six and driving over extra cover for four. But his entertaining 38 off 26 balls ended in the eighth over when he attempted to loft Arafat Minhas over the infield and picked out Razaullah at long-on, leaving Sri Lanka at 74-2.

The dismissal proved to be Pakistan’s last breakthrough. Kusal and Kamindu took control with a blend of calculated aggression and smart running, exploiting gaps in the field while capitalising on loose deliveries. Pakistan’s bowlers struggled to maintain their lines, while missed opportunities and lapses in execution allowed the required rate to fall steadily.

Kusal brought up his half-century in 33 balls with a jab through the off side in the 13th over. He celebrated the milestone by dancing down the track to launch Arafat over long-off for six, with fielder Abdul Samad unable to complete the catch after losing his balance near the boundary.

Kamindu complemented his captain’s power with elegant strokeplay. He drove crisply through extra cover, sent a lofted cover drive racing to the boundary off Salman and pierced the infield with a straight drive against Razaullah. The pair brought up Sri Lanka’s 100 in the 11th over, with the visitors already well ahead of the asking rate.

Pakistan’s errors compounded their difficulties. Sufyan Moqim failed to hold a return catch offered by Kusal in the 15th over, while the bowlers repeatedly offered scoring opportunities through short deliveries and loose balls outside off stump. Poor execution at the death further underlined the hosts’ inability to contain the Sri Lankan batters.

Kusal shifted through the gears in the closing overs, upper-cutting Salman over the wicketkeeper for four before launching a regal straight drive over the bowler’s head for six. Kamindu, meanwhile, kept the scoreboard moving with well-timed strokes and quick singles as the target came within reach.

The foundation for Sri Lanka’s victory had been laid earlier by their bowlers, led by Dasun Shanaka’s miserly three-wicket haul. Shanaka returned figures of three for 21 in four overs, removing Khawaja Nafay, Imran and Samad to prevent Pakistan from building momentum through the middle overs.

Pakistan had been reduced to 86-5 before captain Sahibzada Farhan and Arafat mounted a recovery. Farhan top-scored with 76 off 47 balls, hitting seven fours and three sixes, while Arafat remained unbeaten on 34 from 20 deliveries.

The pair added 66 runs for the seventh wicket, rescuing Pakistan from 102-6 and lifting them to 168-8. Farhan reached his third consecutive half-century before falling to Nuwan Thushara for 76 in the penultimate over, while Arafat’s late assault included two fours and two sixes.

Despite their efforts, Pakistan’s total proved insufficient against Sri Lanka’s clinical chase.

World.title: Saudi-led coalition strikes oil site in Yemen's capital
World.content:
Yemen’s Houthis said Saudi Arabia struck an oil facility in Sanaa on Tuesday, after the Riyadh-led coalition told civilians to leave the surrounding area in its first evacuation order for the Yemeni capital since the war flared up again.

The Saudi-led coalition said military operations were conducted against “vital assets” used by the Houthis to wage war in Yemen.

In a statement posted on X, coalition spokesperson Major General Turki Al-Maliki says the targets included the Al-Sabaha central station in the capital Sanaa, underground fuel reserves and fuel tanks, and energy terminals in Hodeidah, Sanaa and Dhamar.

Earlier, the coalition’s spokesman said people should leave an oil facility belonging to the Yemen Petroleum Company on the western outskirts of Sanaa before it was attacked.

An AFP correspondent in Sanaa reported hearing an explosion, while a breaking news alert on the Houthi-affiliated Al-Masirah TV channel said, “Saudi aggression targets the oil company in Al-Sabaha, west of Sanaa”.

The Saudi-led coalition had not yet confirmed the reported strike.

Swiftly responding to the earlier coalition warning, the Houthis had issued a threat to target Riyadh’s international airport, a refinery, and an Aramco facility in Dammam if the strike went ahead.

“The Yemeni Armed Forces urge all citizens to immediately evacuate and move away from targets that our forces will strike should the Saudi enemy target,” military spokesman Yahya Saree wrote on X, identifying the three targets.

An attack at Riyadh’s airport on Saturday left 13 people dead and operations suspended, rocking the world’s top crude oil exporter and deepening the war in Yemen, where the kingdom backs the internationally recognised government.

An AFP correspondent reported that many civilians in Sanaa, fearing shortages, rushed to queue in front of fuel stations after the coalition warning.

The Yemen Petroleum Company sought to reassure the public, saying it had taken all necessary precautions in the event of an emergency to “meet people’s needs”.

Petroleum stocks were “available in safe facilities and locations, and in sufficient quantities” to meet demand for long periods, it said.

Saudi Arabia was still weathering fresh attacks on Tuesday, with the coalition saying its forces intercepted three drones north of the kingdom’s capital Riyadh.

Many countries have issued travel warnings to their citizens in Saudi Arabia, most recently France, which told its citizens to avoid the airports in Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam on Tuesday.

The Saudi coalition has supported Yemen’s government militarily against the Houthis since 2015 in a long-running civil war that has created a humanitarian crisis.

Economic woes

Traffic in perennially gridlocked Riyadh was noticeably lighter this week, as remote learning for all schools and work-from-home orders for some companies took effect, according to AFP journalists.

Saudi Arabia faces a major economic contraction this year, with GDP expected to shrink 3.3 per cent, the International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday, predicting a regional drop over Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

The kingdom was already facing headwinds from Tehran’s chokehold on the Strait of Hormuz, vital for oil and gas trade, since the start of the Middle East war in February, when the US and Israel attacked Iran.

But the restart in July of Yemen’s frozen war has further roiled the kingdom and brought the fight to its own soil. Houthi attacks have also targeted oil tankers in the Red Sea — Saudi Arabia’s alternative export route.

In Yemen, the renewed fighting was fuelling the risk of infectious disease outbreaks. Suspected cholera cases tripled there in three weeks, the World Health Organisation said on Tuesday, warning that the growing disease burden was straining hospitals already treating war casualties.

Houthi warning

Blasts were heard over the Saudi capital again late on Monday, with the Saudi coalition saying it intercepted a Houthi missile and the group announcing it had again targeted the airport.

On Monday evening, Human Resources Minister Ahmad bin Sulaiman Al Rajhi remained defiant.

“We’re not going out,” he told the crowd at the Riyadh Economic Forum. “We are safe. With God’s will. May God turn their plots back against them.”

The Riyadh airport attack prompted US President Donald Trump to say he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis, after having reportedly rebuffed previous Saudi requests.

The Houthis warned the US against intervention, with political bureau member Mohammed Al Bukhaiti telling AFP they would target American interests in the region.

Bukhaiti said the purpose of the campaign against Saudi targets was to send a message to the crown prince “that he can no longer wage aggression against Yemen from a safe position”.

World.title: Army conducts successful test launch of hypersonic Fatah-2 extended range missile: ISPR
World.content:
The Pakistan Army successfully test-launched the Fatah-2 extended range (ER) hypersonic ballistic missile, the military’s media wing said in a statement on Tuesday.

According to Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the Fatah-2 ER is equipped with advanced navigation and state-of-the-art avionics.

“It is capable of engaging targets with high precision and defeating [the] enemy’s missile defence systems due to its unique trajectory and manoeuvrability features,” it added.

“Fatah-2 ER, with its extended range, will further enhance [the] army’s reach and capability of engaging deep targets.”

The test launch was witnessed by Army Rocket Force Command (ARFC) chief Lt Gen Nauman Zakaria, senior army officers, scientists and engineers.

The ARFC commander “appreciated the dedication and technical prowess of scientists and engineers”, ISPR said.

It further said the president, prime minister, and the chief of defence forces congratulated the scientists and engineers on the successful test launch of the “extended range version of Fatah-2 weapon system”.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi congratulated the nation on the success of the test and termed it an important advancement in the defence sector.

Last week, the indigenously developed extended version of the Fatah-IV ground-launched cruise missile also underwent a successful test launch.

In a statement, ISPR said, “Equipped with advanced avionics and state-of-the-art navigational aids, the weapon system is capable of engaging targets at extended ranges with high precision and lethality.”

“The test also validated additional technical parameters of various sub-systems incorporated for improved accuracy and enhanced survivability,” it added.

World.title: Violence in response to a woman's refusal to marry 'profound shame' on society's conscience: Supreme Court
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Criticising patriarchal customs and gender-based violence, the Supreme Court (SC) on Tuesday said it was a profound shame on the conscience of any civilised society when a man, having failed to win a woman’s affection, answered her refusal with violence rather than acceptance.

“The sole reason he takes her life is to appease his wounded ego, as he was unable to secure her hand and marry her,” regretted Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar in a nine-page judgment he authored.

The observation was made by a three-member bench, which also included Justices Salahuddin Panhwar and Ishtiaq Ibrahim.

In its judgment, the bench rejected a criminal review petition by Muhammad Kamran, who sought the commutation of his death sentence to life imprisonment.

Kamran, who has already served around 15 years of his sentence in the death cell, was convicted for murdering a woman after she and her family rejected his marriage proposal.

Dismissing his review plea, the court ruled that a condemned prisoner could not claim, as a matter of right, that him having served 14 or 15 years of his sentence placed him in the same position as a person sentenced to life imprisonment.

“The latter entered prison under a sentence of life imprisonment; the former entered it under a sentence of death. The distinction does not lie in the number of years already spent in prison, but in the sentence which the court actually imposed,” the judgment emphasised.

Woman’s consent considered irrelevant, regrets SC

The court further observed: “Marriage is a mutual, voluntary covenant that necessitates free consent of both parties. But in a variety of patriarchal systems, it is accepted that men have the exclusive right to select, demand and enforce possession over a woman, irrespective of her wishes.”

The judgment stated that a woman “challenges the suitor’s perceived ownership when she exercises her fundamental right to say ‘no’”.

“Under a patriarchal mindset, this rejection is taken by that man as a blow to his ‘honour’ (ghairat), which results in stalking, home invasion, acid violence or femicide,” the judgment added.

The judgment also referred to several customs, such as that of ghag, to illustrate the manifestation of this mindset.

Ghag (proclamation in Pashto) is an archaic customary practice where a man unilaterally claims a woman as his bride without her or her guardians’ consent.

The court observed that historically, ghag was executed by firing gunshots outside the woman’s residence or making a public declaration.

“Ghag acts as an informal seal or taboo intimidating other perspective suitors away, holding a woman’s marital status hostage as if she is a territory, which is now marked by this man,” the judgment said, adding if the woman or her family resisted, the suitor would frequently employ violence to enforce his claim.

As a result, a woman may remain unmarried for years, or even decades, solely due to a declaration that was never followed by a legal or religious ceremony, engagement, or marriage, the court said.

It added that the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Elimination of Custom of Ghag Act, 2013, had already declared the custom a cognisable, non-bailable and non-compoundable criminal offence.

The judgment then referred to the customs of suara, also known as vani or badal-e-sulh, which it said operated differently from ghag, despite the fact that both portrayed situations where the decision to marry a woman was made by others for a purpose that was not in accordance with her own desires nor benefit.

Suara involves a girl or young woman from a family that has committed an offence, such as homicide, given in marriage to a man from the victim’s family as a form of compensation through decision made by a jirga, and serves as a substitute for a criminal proceeding or financial compensation, the court observed.

The practice was criminalised through Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2004 and further solidified by Prevention of Anti-Women Practices Act, 2011, it noted.

Similarly, there was the custom of watta-satta — another example where the setting of marriage was at the cost of the bride’s well being, the judgment said.

Watta-satta, which translates to “give-take”, is a “reciprocal marriage that is prevalent in our country involving a brother and sister from one family marrying a sister and brother from another family”, the judgment said.

“The common thread that unites all of these customs is that in this male-dominated society having patriarchal customs and traditions, a woman’s assent to her own marriage is considered irrelevant,” the court regretted.

It further stated that it is impossible to reconcile this mindset with Islam, which required woman’s free assent as a prerequisite for a valid nikah. Any adult person, either a man or a woman, was equally entitled to decide whether, when and with whom they would marry, the judgment said.

That entitlement, the judgment said, was not a concession that her family, tribe or society, as a whole, had granted to her, the judgment emphasised, adding that a woman possessed this privilege in her own right.

“There is no excuse for such behaviour, regardless of whether it is committed in the name of honour, custom, injured pride, or emotions.”

The judgment further highlighted that Pakistan was party to the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW). Its Article 16 obliged states to ensure that a woman had the same right to freely choose a spouse and to enter into a marriage only with her free and full consent, the court noted.

“A domestic custom or such prevalent mindset that nullifies this choice by force cannot be permitted to survive under the guise of local practice,” the judgment said.

In the case at hand, the petitioner, who murdered a woman in cold blood, seemed to have “suffered from the mindset which led to beliefs that a woman is a commodity and it was the right of the suitor to have her, with no possibility of refusal because commodities cannot express”, the court held.

The court further said that the attempt to present a woman’s lawful refusal as “provocation” or as a mitigating circumstance was a very “absurd ground” for the plea at hand because no individual had the right to deprive another of their life just because of refusing a marriage proposal.

Accepting such an argument would constitute judicial endorsement of the notion that a woman’s will was subordinate to a man’s preference, the court declared.

The court held that the petitioner had failed to point out any error to justify the SC’s review jurisdiction under Article 188 of the Constitution. “The submissions advanced are, in substance, a request to rearrange and reweigh matters, which this court, sitting in review, cannot undertake,” it said.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”
